title: Federal Register NOI/NOA Refresh
text:
Purpose: Refresh Phase 2 Federal Register data and link high-confidence notices to NEPA projects: - NOI (Notice of Intent): project initiation date → noi_publication_date - NOA (Notice of Availability): project end date (FEIS/FSEIS/FONSI/Final EA) → noa_availability_date
Default behavior: extract_data.py --mode analysis does not call the Federal Register API or scan NEPATEC pages. It merges data/analysis/federal_register/federal_register.parquet if that file already exists.


Matching is entirely document-number-driven in two steps:

NEPATEC page scan: DuckDB scans all EA/EIS/CE pages for FR Doc. references and federalregister.gov URLs. Doc numbers are proximity-filtered (500-char window) with priority:

fr_doc_noi — NOI-like phrase nearby (“notice of intent”, “notice of preparation”, etc.)
fr_doc_noa — NOA-like phrase nearby (“final environmental impact statement”, “fonsi”, “notice of availability”, “record of decision”, “final supplemental eis”, etc.)
fr_doc_non_noi — no recognized phrase (excluded from matching)

Direct fetch + title match: All unique valid doc numbers (fr_doc_noi, fr_url, fr_doc_noa) are fetched in a single combined pass (GET /api/v1/documents/{doc_num}.json). Fetched records are then split by title type:

NOI corpus: records with NOI-type titles (Notice of Intent / Notice of Preparation / Notice of Scoping)
NOA corpus: records with NOA-type titles (Final EIS, Final Supplemental EIS, FONSI, Final EA)

A match is auto-accepted only when direct doc number evidence + ≥N title tokens + correct title type + process alignment all agree.
A third step supplements NOA coverage for EIS projects with no direct fr_doc_noa evidence:
NOA title search (EIS fallback): For unmatched EIS projects with a known noi_publication_date, the FR API is searched by project title keywords with a date window anchored to noi_date + 365 days. This recovers FEIS notices that cannot self-cite their own FR doc number (the number is assigned at publication, after the FEIS body is written). Acceptance requires ≥ max(standard, min(n, 3)) title token overlap and a FEIS/FSEIS title type. EA projects are excluded — FONSI matching without direct doc evidence is too risky. Provenance: noa_date_evidence_type = "fr_title_search_noi_anchored".

Key rules: - noi_publication_date is only populated from fr_doc_noi/fr_url evidence with an NOI-type FR title. - noa_availability_date is populated from fr_doc_noa direct evidence (EIS→FEIS/FSEIS, EA→FONSI/Final EA) or from the NOA title search fallback for EIS projects (noa_date_evidence_type = "fr_title_search_noi_anchored"). - Agency/state/sponsor alone is not sufficient — title overlap is always required. - CE projects: all evidence goes to manual review, never auto-accepted. - EA projects: no NOA title search fallback — only direct fr_doc_noa evidence. - Projects with no NEPATEC doc number evidence and no noi_publication_date get no NOA coverage.



Re-scans NEPATEC pages and direct-fetches all FR records:
conda run -n nepa python phase2/code/extract/extract_data.py \
  --mode analysis \
  --refresh-federal-register
The NEPATEC page scan always runs when --refresh-federal-register is set (~30–60s). To skip the rescan and reuse a cached evidence file, use the standalone script directly without --rescan-nepatec-evidence (see below).



Run this directly for more control over paths and options:
conda run -n nepa python phase2/code/extract/federal_register.py \
  --projects-path phase2/data/analysis/projects_combined.parquet \
  --output phase2/data/analysis/federal_register/federal_register.parquet \
  --corpus-output phase2/data/analysis/federal_register/noi_corups.parquet \
  --candidates-output phase2/data/analysis/federal_register/noi_candidates.parquet \
  --evidence-output phase2/data/analysis/federal_register/nepatec_fr_evidence.parquet \
  --cache-path phase2/data/analysis/federal_register/fr_noi_cache.json \
  --all-projects
Add --rescan-nepatec-evidence to force a fresh NEPATEC page scan. Required after: adding new fr_doc_noa proximity phrases (e.g., “notice of availability”, “record of decision”, “final supplemental eis”), expanding _NOA_PROXIMITY_PHRASES, or rebuilding NEPATEC processed data.

[fr-evidence]: NEPATEC DuckDB scan progress per process type (EA, EIS, CE).
[FR direct]: Direct API fetch progress — shows fetched/not_found/network_calls counts.
[FR match]: Offline NOI matching progress.
[FR noa-match]: Offline NOA matching progress (direct fr_doc_noa evidence path).
[FR noa-title]: Phase 3 title search fallback — attempted/supplemented counts for unmatched EIS projects.







noi_corups.parquet: FR records for NOI doc numbers fetched from API.
noi_candidates.parquet: All scored NOI candidate links.





noa_corpus.parquet: FR records for NOA doc numbers fetched from API (FEIS/FSEIS/FONSI/Final EA).
noa_candidates.parquet: All scored NOA candidate links.





nepatec_fr_evidence.parquet: One row per FR Doc. number found per NEPATEC page; cached across refreshes. evidence_type values: fr_doc_noi, fr_doc_noa, fr_doc_non_noi, fr_url.
noi_manual_review_candidates.csv: Candidate rows for projects with multiple competing high-confidence NOI candidates.
noa_manual_review_candidates.csv: NOA candidate rows requiring manual review (CE evidence, process mismatch, insufficient title overlap).
federal_register.parquet: One row per NEPA project; noi_publication_date and noa_availability_date populated where auto-accepted.

fr_noi_fetch_report.csv was part of the legacy keyword/windowed fetch path and is removed during refresh.













Condition
Outcome




EA/EIS: fr_doc_noi evidence + ≥N title tokens + NOI-type FR title + no process conflict
Auto-accept (noi_publication_date populated)


EA/EIS: fr_url evidence + ≥N title tokens + NOI-type FR title + no process conflict
Auto-accept


EA/EIS: doc number joins but FR title is not NOI-type
Manual review


EA/EIS: doc number joins but title overlap < N
Manual review


EA/EIS: doc number joins but process conflict
Manual review


CE: any NEPATEC doc number evidence
Manual review (no auto-accept)


No NEPATEC doc number evidence
Unmatched













Condition
Outcome




EIS: fr_doc_noa evidence + ≥N title tokens + FEIS/FSEIS-type FR title + EIS project
Auto-accept (noa_availability_date populated)


EA: fr_doc_noa evidence + ≥N title tokens + FONSI/Final EA title + EA project
Auto-accept


Any: fr_doc_noa evidence + NOA title + title overlap < N
Manual review


Any: fr_doc_noa evidence + process mismatch (EA project + FEIS title)
Manual review


CE: any fr_doc_noa evidence
Manual review


EIS: no fr_doc_noa evidence + noi_publication_date known + ≥3 title tokens → title search → FEIS title + strong overlap
Auto-accept (noa_date_evidence_type = "fr_title_search_noi_anchored")


EA/CE: no fr_doc_noa evidence
Unmatched (no title search fallback)



N = required title token overlap, scaled by title length: 1→1, 2→2, 3→2, 4+→3.











Column
Description




project_id, process_type
Project identity


document_id, file_name, main_document
Source document


page_number
Page where evidence was found


evidence_type
fr_doc_noi (NOI phrase nearby), fr_doc_noa (NOA phrase nearby), fr_doc_non_noi (no recognized phrase), fr_url


fr_document_number
Normalized to ASCII hyphen — the join key


fr_document_number_raw
Original extracted string (may contain en-dash)


nearby_noi_phrase
Nearest recognized phrase within 500 chars (if any)


fr_date_text_parsed
ISO date from prose (“Published in the Federal Register on…”)















Field
Description

nepatec_fr_doc_number for auto-accepted direct-evidence matches


noi_nepatec_evidence_document_id
NEPATEC document where FR doc number was found


noi_nepatec_evidence_file_name
File name of that document


noi_nepatec_evidence_page_number
Page number of the FR doc bracket













Field
Description

FR publication date of FEIS/FONSI notice (end-of-process signal)


noa_document_number
FR document number of the NOA record


noa_match_status
accepted, review_required, or unmatched


noa_match_reason
Specific reason code


noa_date_evidence_type
nepatec_fr_doc_noa for auto-accepted matches


noa_nepatec_evidence_document_id
NEPATEC document where NOA doc number was found


noa_nepatec_evidence_file_name
File name of that document


noa_nepatec_evidence_page_number
Page number of the FR doc bracket

title: Timeline Extraction
text:
Purpose: Extract initiation and decision dates for NEPA reviews using a BERT classifier with optional LLM adjudication. Input: data/analysis/projects_combined.parquet + regex candidate cache. Output: data/analysis/timeline_{ce,ea,eis}.parquet, timeline_{ea,eis}_llm.parquet, timeline_targeted_llm.parquet Cost: LLM adjudication ~$0.60–$1.00 (Claude Haiku) for EA + EIS full runs. Targeted re-adjudication ~$0.44. Prerequisites: Base dataset built (runbook 01).

Note on prior organization: The targeted re-adjudication for programmatic/tiered projects was previously documented as a standalone “Deliverable 02” section in the README. It is step 7 in the full rebuild below because it operates on timeline outputs — it is a timeline operation, not a reviews operation. Reviews (runbook 03) must still run before step 7.













Stage
CE
EA
EIS




Regex cache
timeline_regex_ce.parquet
timeline_regex_ea.parquet
timeline_regex_eis.parquet


BERT training data
bert_traindata.parquet
← same file
← same file


Sample test (post-train)
timeline_ce_sample{N}.parquet
timeline_ea_sample{N}.parquet
timeline_eis_sample{N}.parquet


Full BERT run
timeline_ce.parquet
timeline_ea.parquet
timeline_eis.parquet


Post LLM adjudication
(none)
timeline_ea_llm.parquet
timeline_eis_llm.parquet



Append _v{N} to sample files when iterating through multiple training rounds (e.g. timeline_ce_sample20_v2.parquet). Full run files are overwritten each time.




Use when regex patterns or training logic have changed and classifiers need retraining from scratch.
# Step 1 — Rebuild regex candidate cache for all sources
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --regex-prep --source CE
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --regex-prep --source EA
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --regex-prep --source EIS
# Output: data/analysis/timeline_regex_{ce,ea,eis}.parquet

# Step 2 — Rebuild BERT training data
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-generate
# Output: data/analysis/bert_traindata.parquet

# Step 3 — Retrain classifiers
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-train --source CE
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-train --source EA
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-train --source EIS

# Step 4 — Smoke test on 20 projects before committing to full run
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-run --sample 20 --source CE \
    --output data/analysis/timeline_ce_sample20.parquet

# Step 5 — Full BERT inference
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-run --source CE \
    --output data/analysis/timeline_ce.parquet
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-run --source EA \
    --output data/analysis/timeline_ea.parquet
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-run --source EIS \
    --output data/analysis/timeline_eis.parquet

# Step 6 — LLM adjudication for EA and EIS (not needed for CE at scale)
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY='sk-ant-...'

python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --llm-adjudicate \
    --input data/analysis/timeline_ea.parquet \
    --provider claude \
    --output data/analysis/timeline_ea_llm.parquet

python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --llm-adjudicate \
    --input data/analysis/timeline_eis.parquet \
    --provider claude \
    --output data/analysis/timeline_eis_llm.parquet

# Step 7 — Targeted re-adjudication for programmatic/tiered projects
# Run after step 6 AND after reviews extraction (runbook 03) is complete.
# Auto-selects ~73 programmatic/tiered projects with missing initiation or decision dates.
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py \
    --llm-adjudicate \
    --input data/analysis/timeline_ea_llm.parquet,data/analysis/timeline_eis_llm.parquet \
    --nonstandard-incomplete \
    --max-candidates 125 \
    --context-chars 400 \
    --promote-rod-language \
    --year-window 15 \
    --provider claude \
    --output data/analysis/timeline_targeted_llm.parquet
Step 7 flag notes: - --nonstandard-incomplete — filters to programmatic/tiered projects with missing dates; no manual ID file needed. - --max-candidates 125 — raises cap from 30 (EIS default) to 125 for large programmatic EISs. - --promote-rod-language — promotes ROD/FONSI dates to Tier A even if BERT mislabeled them. - --year-window 15 — drops candidates >15 years before the latest found date, removing NEPA citation noise. - Targeted output is ~73 rows. Full timeline files are not modified. Patched automatically by 00_setup.R.




Use when models are current and only BERT inference + adjudication outputs need refreshing.
CE only:
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-run --source CE \
    --output data/analysis/timeline_ce.parquet
EA:
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-run --source EA \
    --output data/analysis/timeline_ea.parquet

python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --llm-adjudicate \
    --input data/analysis/timeline_ea.parquet \
    --provider claude \
    --output data/analysis/timeline_ea_llm.parquet
EIS:
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-run --source EIS \
    --output data/analysis/timeline_eis.parquet

python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --llm-adjudicate \
    --input data/analysis/timeline_eis.parquet \
    --provider claude \
    --output data/analysis/timeline_eis_llm.parquet




Restrict to clean energy projects only (add --clean-energy to any --bert-run command):
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-run --source EA --clean-energy \
    --output data/analysis/timeline_ea_clean.parquet
Debug a single project (searches CE, EA, and EIS sources automatically):
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --project-id <UUID> --hybrid --use-regex-cache




On the first pass, skip manual corrections entirely — run steps 1–5 above using weak supervision alone to get a working baseline. Then inspect the output, add corrections, and retrain. You do not need to get corrections right before starting.
After a full run, inspect the output for systematic errors (e.g. CE projects still missing initiation dates). Corrections are added to:
data/analysis/manual_training_corrections.csv
Required columns: project_id, date, correct_type (one of decision, initiation, review, other)
Once corrections are added, you only need to re-run steps 2–5 (not step 1 — the regex cache is unchanged):
# Regenerate training data with corrections applied
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-generate

# Retrain affected source(s)
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-train --source CE

# Smoke test
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-run --sample 20 --source CE \
    --output data/analysis/timeline_ce_sample20_v2.parquet

# Re-run full inference
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-run --source CE \
    --output data/analysis/timeline_ce.parquet
Matching note: Corrections are matched on (project_id, date). If the same date appears in multiple contexts for a project, the correction applies to all of them. You can make the match more precise by also checking context in the CSV (not currently implemented — avoid duplicate dates per project when possible).
Timing: Add corrections after inspecting --bert-run output and identifying a cohort of systematic misses (e.g. 20–50 CE initiation false negatives). Corrections before the first run are not useful — you need the model’s output to know what to fix. Plan on at least one correction cycle after the initial build.





--source accepts CE, EA, EIS, or comma-separated combinations. Defaults to CE if omitted.
spaCy enrichment runs by default during --regex-prep. Use --no-spacy to skip.
Initiation class imbalance is a known bottleneck; improve via pattern expansion + weighting + manual examples.
Timeline selection prioritizes strong signature cues over latest-date heuristics.
dep_verb, sig_flag, ner_decision_signal are the spaCy-enriched columns used by BERT.

title: Timeline Extraction
text:
Use when regex patterns or training logic have changed and classifiers need retraining from scratch.
# Step 1 — Rebuild regex candidate cache for all sources
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --regex-prep --source CE
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --regex-prep --source EA
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --regex-prep --source EIS
# Output: data/analysis/timeline_regex_{ce,ea,eis}.parquet

# Step 2 — Rebuild BERT training data
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-generate
# Output: data/analysis/bert_traindata.parquet

# Step 3 — Retrain classifiers
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-train --source CE
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-train --source EA
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-train --source EIS

# Step 4 — Smoke test on 20 projects before committing to full run
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-run --sample 20 --source CE \
    --output data/analysis/timeline_ce_sample20.parquet

# Step 5 — Full BERT inference
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-run --source CE \
    --output data/analysis/timeline_ce.parquet
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-run --source EA \
    --output data/analysis/timeline_ea.parquet
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-run --source EIS \
    --output data/analysis/timeline_eis.parquet

# Step 6 — LLM adjudication for EA and EIS (not needed for CE at scale)
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY='sk-ant-...'

python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --llm-adjudicate \
    --input data/analysis/timeline_ea.parquet \
    --provider claude \
    --output data/analysis/timeline_ea_llm.parquet

python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --llm-adjudicate \
    --input data/analysis/timeline_eis.parquet \
    --provider claude \
    --output data/analysis/timeline_eis_llm.parquet

# Step 7 — Targeted re-adjudication for programmatic/tiered projects
# Run after step 6 AND after reviews extraction (runbook 03) is complete.
# Auto-selects ~73 programmatic/tiered projects with missing initiation or decision dates.
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py \
    --llm-adjudicate \
    --input data/analysis/timeline_ea_llm.parquet,data/analysis/timeline_eis_llm.parquet \
    --nonstandard-incomplete \
    --max-candidates 125 \
    --context-chars 400 \
    --promote-rod-language \
    --year-window 15 \
    --provider claude \
    --output data/analysis/timeline_targeted_llm.parquet
Step 7 flag notes: - --nonstandard-incomplete — filters to programmatic/tiered projects with missing dates; no manual ID file needed. - --max-candidates 125 — raises cap from 30 (EIS default) to 125 for large programmatic EISs. - --promote-rod-language — promotes ROD/FONSI dates to Tier A even if BERT mislabeled them. - --year-window 15 — drops candidates >15 years before the latest found date, removing NEPA citation noise. - Targeted output is ~73 rows. Full timeline files are not modified. Patched automatically by 00_setup.R.

text:
On the first pass, skip manual corrections entirely — run steps 1–5 above using weak supervision alone to get a working baseline. Then inspect the output, add corrections, and retrain. You do not need to get corrections right before starting.
After a full run, inspect the output for systematic errors (e.g. CE projects still missing initiation dates). Corrections are added to:
data/analysis/manual_training_corrections.csv
Required columns: project_id, date, correct_type (one of decision, initiation, review, other)
Once corrections are added, you only need to re-run steps 2–5 (not step 1 — the regex cache is unchanged):
# Regenerate training data with corrections applied
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-generate

# Retrain affected source(s)
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-train --source CE

# Smoke test
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-run --sample 20 --source CE \
    --output data/analysis/timeline_ce_sample20_v2.parquet

# Re-run full inference
python phase2/code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-run --source CE \
    --output data/analysis/timeline_ce.parquet

title: Phase 2 RAG Build Plan
text:
Build a CAFT-facing RAG application that answers questions over NEPATEC2.0 source text, project metadata, and selected Phase 2 deliverable artifacts. The app should build on the existing Streamlit/DuckDB document explorer architecture, use Gemma 4 E2B as the fast local default during development, offer Gemma 4 E4B as a quality option, and keep the implementation under phase2/rag. Larger Gemma 4 models such as 26B or 31B can remain optional later benchmarks, but they are too large and slow for the default local path.
The product goal is answers with evidence, not a semantic-search tool. Retrieval is still required internally, but the user experience should be: ask a question, receive a grounded answer, see cited sources, and click through to the source page.




Audience: CAFT staff, likely 5 users.
Expected use: up to roughly 10,000 queries per month, unevenly distributed.
Data scope: NEPATEC source text first; final Phase 2 deliverables may be added if they improve answer quality.
Access pattern: browser-based app, eventually linked from the existing website or hosted similarly to the document explorer.
Logging: session-only chat history by default. Avoid persistent query logs unless CAFT explicitly wants them.
Failure mode: best guess is acceptable only with a strong, visible warning and source limitations.
Correctness requirement: answers must cite evidence where applicable and distinguish sourced claims from inference.




Do not build one monolithic DuckDB/FTS store over all page text. The Phase 2 page scale is too large for a single easy-to-host file:



Process
Pages




CE
73,544


EA
469,106


EIS
6,131,757


Total
6,674,407



A single FTS index over 6.7M pages would take hours to build, create a multi-GB DuckDB file, and risks exceeding Hugging Face’s 5 GB per-file limit or making app cold starts too slow.


Build the RAG store as shards:

CE shard: one CE chunk/page shard.
EA shard: one EA chunk/page shard.
EIS shards: many EIS chunk/page shards, split by stable document_id ordering or hash buckets.
Never split a single document_id across shards.
Write a shard manifest that records process type, shard id, file paths, row counts, document counts, and build timestamp.

This keeps each deployable artifact small enough for Hugging Face Dataset storage and lets the app route to the right shard. HF supports multi-file datasets, so deployment should upload the manifest plus all shard files. The simplest MVP can download all shards at startup. If that is too slow, the app should download the manifest first and then lazily download only the needed shards. DuckDB can read page shards directly with a glob such as read_parquet('.../pages_eis_*.parquet') for lazy EIS page lookup.
Because DuckDB FTS requires a materialized table, each searchable shard should also have its own DuckDB file with a rag_chunks table and FTS index:
phase2/rag/data/
├── manifest.json
├── rag_catalog.duckdb
├── pages_ce.parquet
├── pages_ea.parquet
├── pages_eis_000.parquet
├── pages_eis_001.parquet
├── chunks_ce.parquet
├── chunks_ea.parquet
├── chunks_eis_000.parquet
├── chunks_eis_001.parquet
├── rag_chunks_ce.duckdb
├── rag_chunks_ea.duckdb
├── rag_chunks_eis_000.duckdb
└── rag_chunks_eis_001.duckdb
The app should query only relevant shard indexes when a process type or selected project is known. For whole-corpus questions, it can fan out across shards with per-shard top-k retrieval, then merge and rerank the evidence.




The existing document explorer already solves several production problems:

Streamlit app shell and browser UI.
DuckDB-backed project/document/page lookup.
Hugging Face dataset download support through NEPA_DB_HF_REPO and hf_hub_download.
Full-text page search with DuckDB FTS and LIKE fallback.
Project filters, document browser, page reader, and source-page navigation.

The RAG app should reuse this architecture instead of replacing it. The main difference is that the Phase 2 RAG app should live under phase2/rag, use sharded artifacts, and expose an answer workflow in addition to the existing browse/read workflow.



phase2/rag/
├── README.md
├── Makefile
├── .env.example
├── app/
│   ├── app.py
│   └── requirements.txt
├── scripts/
│   ├── 01_build_text_store.py
│   ├── 02_build_chunks.py
│   ├── 03_build_indexes.py
│   └── 04_eval_rag.py
├── src/
│   └── nepa_rag/
│       ├── __init__.py
│       ├── config.py
│       ├── db.py
│       ├── query_router.py
│       ├── retrieval.py
│       ├── evidence.py
│       ├── text_formatting.py
│       ├── chunking.py
│       ├── prompts.py
│       ├── llm.py
│       ├── answer.py
│       └── session_history.py
├── eval/
│   ├── questions.yaml
│   └── expected_sources.csv
├── deploy/
│   ├── Dockerfile
│   └── hf_space.md
└── data/
    └── .gitignore
Generated databases, indexes, model caches, parquet shards, and logs should not be committed. Use phase2/rag/data/.gitignore rather than .gitkeep:
*
!.gitignore
At minimum, generated artifacts should exclude:
*.duckdb
*.duckdb.wal
*.parquet
*.json
models/
model_cache/
.cache/
logs/



Pin DuckDB to a modern version and load local configuration through .env.
phase2/rag/app/requirements.txt should include:
streamlit>=1.35
duckdb>=1.1
pandas>=2.0
huggingface_hub>=0.34
python-dotenv>=1.0
requests>=2.31
src/nepa_rag/config.py should:

call dotenv.load_dotenv();
define typed config values with defaults;
validate required values before app startup;
keep model configuration fully environment-driven;
avoid hard-coding Ollama tags.

.env.example should include:
# Local data
NEPA_RAG_DATA_DIR=phase2/rag/data
NEPA_RAG_CATALOG=phase2/rag/data/rag_catalog.duckdb
NEPA_RAG_MANIFEST=phase2/rag/data/manifest.json

# Hugging Face dataset repo for Phase 2 RAG artifacts
NEPA_RAG_DB_HF_REPO=YOUR_HF_USERNAME/nepa-phase2-rag-db
NEPA_RAG_DB_HF_REVISION=main

# LLM provider
LLM_PROVIDER=ollama
LLM_MODEL=gemma4:e2b
LLM_QUALITY_MODEL=gemma4:e4b
LLM_FALLBACK_MODEL=gemma4:e2b
OLLAMA_HOST=http://localhost:11434
LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=120
LLM_NUM_CTX=4096
LLM_NUM_PREDICT=350

# Retrieval
RAG_TOP_K_PER_SHARD=3
RAG_MAX_CONTEXT_PASSAGES=4
RAG_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS=2500
RAG_REQUIRE_SOURCE_LABELS=true

# App behavior
RAG_SESSION_HISTORY_ONLY=true
RAG_DEFAULT_SCOPE=selected_project
The actual Gemma 4 Ollama tag may differ by quantization and Ollama packaging. The app should not assume these exact tags exist. Local setup must require:
ollama pull <configured-fast-tag>
ollama pull <configured-quality-tag>
Use gemma4:e2b as the fast default and fallback for local CPU-bound testing. Use gemma4:e4b as a selectable quality model when latency is acceptable. Gemma 4 26B and 31B should be treated as optional benchmarks, not the default local models.
For local CPU-bound testing, keep prompts and generations small:
RAG_TOP_K_PER_SHARD=3
RAG_MAX_CONTEXT_PASSAGES=4
RAG_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS=2500
LLM_NUM_CTX=4096
LLM_NUM_PREDICT=350





Build a small catalog database containing metadata and shard information:

projects
documents
shards
optional deliverable/result metadata

The catalog should not include all page text. It should be small enough to download quickly at app startup.



Build process-specific page shards for lazy document viewing and per-project page lookup:
pages_ce.parquet
pages_ea.parquet
pages_eis_000.parquet
pages_eis_001.parquet
...
Each page shard must include:
shard_id
process_type
document_id
project_id
page_number
page_number_int
page_text
Pages parquets do not contain project_id. The build script must join through documents:
pages.document_id
  -> documents_combined.document_id
  -> documents_combined.project_id
  -> projects_combined.project_id
page_number is stored as text in source parquets. Build scripts must preserve the original page_number and derive page_number_int safely:
COALESCE(
    TRY_CAST(regexp_extract(CAST(page_number AS VARCHAR), '([0-9]+)', 1) AS INTEGER),
    0
) AS page_number_int
This handles non-numeric page labels such as i, A-1, and appendix-style pages without losing the original label.



Build matching chunk shards:
chunks_ce.parquet
chunks_ea.parquet
chunks_eis_000.parquet
chunks_eis_001.parquet
...
Proposed rag_chunks schema:
chunk_id
shard_id
process_type
project_id
project_title
lead_agency
lead_agency_harmonized
project_state
project_type
document_id
file_name
document_type
document_type_clean
document_type_category
main_document
page_number
page_number_int
chunk_index_on_page
char_start
char_end
chunk_text
token_estimate
source_label
Use this exact source_label format so prompts, citations, and validators can parse it consistently:
[Project: {project_title} ({project_id}); Document: {file_name} ({document_id}); Page: {page_number}]
The answer prompt should require citations by exact source_label, and answer.py should validate that every cited label exists in the retrieved evidence set.
Chunking rules:

Keep page boundaries intact for citations.
Prefer paragraph-bounded chunks when possible.
Target roughly 800-1,500 tokens per chunk.
Add 100-200 token overlap only when splitting long pages.
Preserve project_id, document_id, page_number, and source_label on every chunk.
Prioritize main_document == "YES" during retrieval.

CE page length warning: CE “pages” average roughly 12,765 characters (~3,200 tokens), compared to ~2,200 characters for EA and EIS. CE records are full documents concatenated into one row, not individual PDF pages. The chunking script must handle CE pages as long documents requiring 3–4 sub-page splits each, not as single-chunk inputs. EA and EIS pages typically fit in 1–2 chunks.
Reuse the paragraph and heading regex logic already in app/app.py, especially:

BULLET_RE
SECTION_HEADING_RE
NUMBERED_HEADING_RE
LETTERED_HEADING_RE
ALL_CAPS_HEADING_RE
TOC_HEADING_RE

Move shared text cleanup/chunking logic into src/nepa_rag/text_formatting.py and src/nepa_rag/chunking.py. Do not duplicate these regexes inside the build scripts or import the Streamlit app directly into build code.



Each chunk shard should have a matching DuckDB FTS shard:
rag_chunks_ce.duckdb
rag_chunks_ea.duckdb
rag_chunks_eis_000.duckdb
...
DuckDB FTS is static for this use case. Build it only after all rows have been inserted. If chunks are rebuilt, the FTS index must be rebuilt too.
Use this SQL in 03_build_indexes.py after materializing each shard’s rag_chunks table:
INSTALL fts;
LOAD fts;
PRAGMA create_fts_index(
    'rag_chunks',
    'chunk_id',
    'chunk_text',
    stemmer='porter',
    stopwords='english',
    overwrite=1
);
DuckDB FTS is TF-IDF based, not true BM25. Avoid calling it BM25 in code or documentation. Use names such as fts_score, tfidf_score, or search_score.



Add these later only if they improve deliverable production:

final report text from phase2/reports
output tables from phase2/output
Federal Register artifacts from phase2/data/analysis/federal_register
timeline outputs
architecture/runbook markdown for methodology questions

Deliverable artifacts should be labeled as analysis outputs, not source documents, so the model does not confuse computed results with NEPATEC evidence.






Responsibilities:

Read Phase 2 projects, documents, and page parquets.
Use projects_combined.project_id and projects_combined.lead_agency; do not join through processes_combined.
Join pages through documents to attach project_id and project metadata.
Create rag_catalog.duckdb.
Create sharded page parquets.
Create manifest.json.

Required joins:
pages.document_id
  -> documents_combined.document_id
  -> documents_combined.project_id
  -> projects_combined.project_id
Idempotency:

Re-running the script must replace the catalog and page shards for the requested build scope.
Use temporary output paths and atomic rename where practical.
Remove stale shard files listed in the old manifest before writing the new manifest.




Responsibilities:

Read page shards from manifest.json.
Generate chunk shards.
Preserve source metadata and source_label.
Reuse shared chunking helpers from src/nepa_rag/.

Idempotency:

Re-running the script must replace chunk shards, not append duplicates.
For any DuckDB staging table, use DROP TABLE IF EXISTS rag_chunks before recreation.
After this script runs, 03_build_indexes.py is required because FTS indexes are stale.




Responsibilities:

Build one DuckDB FTS file per chunk shard.
Materialize the shard’s rag_chunks table before creating the FTS index.
Record index file paths and row counts back into manifest.json.

Idempotency:

Re-running the script must replace each index DuckDB.
Use DROP TABLE IF EXISTS rag_chunks and overwrite=1 for FTS creation.
If any chunk shard changes, rebuild the corresponding FTS shard.




Post-MVP task. This should not block the first working local app.
Responsibilities:

Run representative questions through the router, retrieval, and answer pipeline.
Check retrieval hit rate, citation correctness, warning behavior, latency, and use of structured data.
Write a small report to phase2/rag/eval/.





Add a simple Makefile so the local rebuild path is one command:
.PHONY: rag-store rag-chunks rag-index rag-build rag-eval rag-app

rag-store:
    conda run -n nepa python phase2/rag/scripts/01_build_text_store.py

rag-chunks:
    conda run -n nepa python phase2/rag/scripts/02_build_chunks.py

rag-index:
    conda run -n nepa python phase2/rag/scripts/03_build_indexes.py

rag-build: rag-store rag-chunks rag-index

rag-eval:
    conda run -n nepa python phase2/rag/scripts/04_eval_rag.py

rag-app:
    conda run -n nepa streamlit run phase2/rag/app/app.py



Use a new Hugging Face Dataset repo for Phase 2 RAG artifacts rather than reusing the existing document explorer DB repo.
Recommended repo:
YOUR_HF_USERNAME/nepa-phase2-rag-db
Upload:

manifest.json
rag_catalog.duckdb
page parquet shards
chunk parquet shards
per-shard DuckDB FTS files

The app should use NEPA_RAG_DB_HF_REPO, not the old document explorer NEPA_DB_HF_REPO, so the two apps can evolve independently.



A full RAG system still needs retrieval, but retrieval should be hidden behind the answer workflow. Do not build a separate semantic-search UI unless later requested.


Route each question before retrieval:

Selected-project mode

Primary project scoping signal should come from the UI, not NLP.
If the user has selected a project in the explorer, treat that project as authoritative scope.
Restrict retrieval to that project unless the user explicitly asks for comparison or whole-corpus search.

Free-text project resolution

Use only when no project is selected.
Check exact project_id first.
Then run a DuckDB ILIKE title search over projects.
If there are multiple plausible matches, ask the user to choose rather than guessing.
Avoid fuzzy NLP project detection in the MVP.

Deliverable-specific question

Use deliverable outputs and architecture docs first.
Pull NEPATEC source examples only when needed for evidence.

Corpus-wide factual question

Use DuckDB for exact counts, filters, and tabular summaries.
Use RAG only to explain or cite examples.

Corpus-wide source-text question

Fan out retrieval across relevant shards.
Merge per-shard top-k results.
Return a warning if retrieved evidence is sparse or concentrated in only a few projects.

Unsupported or ambiguous question

Ask for clarification when needed, or answer with a strong limitation warning.





Start with deterministic retrieval, because the existing explorer already has the needed text store:

Structured lookup

Resolve selected project, documents, process type, agency, state, energy type, timeline fields, Federal Register artifacts, and shard ids.

DuckDB FTS / TF-IDF retrieval

Search rag_chunks.chunk_text in relevant shard indexes.
Apply metadata filters from the query router.
Boost main documents, title matches, Federal Register evidence pages, and timeline/date contexts.

Evidence assembly

Deduplicate adjacent chunks from the same page.
Keep no more than 10-20 source passages in the answer prompt.
Always preserve source metadata and source_label.

Optional vector fallback

Do not implement first unless FTS misses obvious evidence.
If needed, add an internal embedding index for retrieval only. This should not become a separate semantic-search feature.






Use the configured Gemma 4 fast model for local development and answer synthesis. Start with gemma4:e2b for smoke tests and CPU-bound work, and make gemma4:e4b available as a user-selectable quality mode when latency is acceptable.
The answer prompt should pass structured evidence, not a raw dump of pages:
QUESTION
USER_SCOPE
STRUCTURED_FACTS
SOURCE_PASSAGES
DELIVERABLE_CONTEXT
INSTRUCTIONS
Required answer behavior:

Answer from the supplied evidence.
If evidence is incomplete, give the best supported answer with a clear warning.
Cite each factual claim using exact source_label values.
Separate direct evidence from inference.
Never invent dates, counts, agencies, project titles, document numbers, or citations.
For exact counts and tables, use DuckDB results rather than model reasoning.
Include a short “Evidence used” section with clickable source-page links in the app.

Proposed response shape:
Answer
Confidence / warning
Evidence used
Notes and limitations
Suggested follow-up query
answer.py should validate model output before display:

every citation must match a retrieved source_label;
warnings must be present when retrieval confidence is low;
exact counts should be sourced from structured query output;
if validation fails, the app should show a warning and the source cards rather than silently trusting the answer.




Use a provider abstraction from the start:
LLM_PROVIDER=ollama
LLM_MODEL=gemma4:e2b
LLM_QUALITY_MODEL=gemma4:e4b
LLM_FALLBACK_MODEL=gemma4:e2b
OLLAMA_HOST=http://localhost:11434
The first implementation should call a local Ollama server from the Streamlit app. Keep the provider interface generic enough to swap in vLLM, Hugging Face Inference Endpoints, Vertex AI, or another remote endpoint later.
Implementation notes:

Use Gemma 4 E2B as the default fast synthesis model for local testing.
Offer Gemma 4 E4B as a quality model when local hardware supports it.
Keep the exact Ollama tag configurable because model tags and quantizations may differ.
Require ollama pull <configured-tag> during local setup.
Use gemma4:e2b as the documented local fallback if Gemma 4 E4B is too slow or too memory-heavy.
Benchmark local latency with realistic prompts before committing to a hosting path.
Use deterministic code for query routing. Do not spend large-model inference on simple routing decisions.
Do not expose model chain-of-thought. Store only the final answer, cited evidence, and UI state.
Keep prompts short enough for good latency even though Gemma 4 supports long context.






Run everything locally:
Streamlit app -> local sharded DuckDB/parquet artifacts -> local Ollama model
This validates correctness, prompts, retrieval, citations, and latency before deployment decisions.



Keep the document explorer pattern:
Website / Quarto navbar -> Hugging Face Space -> downloaded sharded RAG artifacts
For Gemma 4 E2B/E4B, the Space should initially be treated as the UI host, not necessarily the model host. A free CPU Space may still be too slow for acceptable inference. The app can call a separate model endpoint through environment variables.




Your machine as the model backend

Cost: near $0.
Path: expose a private HTTPS endpoint with Cloudflare Tunnel, Tailscale Funnel, or a similar tunnel.
Pros: cheapest way to keep using a local Gemma 4 model.
Cons: depends on your machine being awake, online, secure, and fast enough.

Paid GPU hosting

Cost: variable, likely nonzero if always-on.
Path: Hugging Face GPU Space, HF Inference Endpoint, RunPod, Modal, Baseten, Vertex AI, or Cloud Run/GKE with GPU.
Pros: better reliability for CAFT.
Cons: larger Gemma 4 models need serious memory, especially with long context; always-on GPU hosting will not be free.

Hosted API fallback

Cost: usually low at 10,000 queries/month if prompts are controlled.
Path: keep the same provider interface and swap from local Gemma to hosted API if self-hosting is not practical.
Pros: easiest reliability story.
Cons: may not satisfy the open-model preference; privacy/data-use rules must be checked.





A cold start is the delay when an app or model server has been idle and must restart before answering. For this RAG app, cold start could include starting Streamlit, downloading/opening the catalog, downloading needed shards, loading the model, and warming the first inference request.
Cold start affects wait time, not answer correctness. For Gemma 4 E2B/E4B, model cold starts should be much lighter than 26B/31B, but still depend on hardware and deployment.







Copy the existing Streamlit app structure into phase2/rag/app.
Keep project search, document browsing, full-text search, and page navigation.
Update the app title and environment variables for the RAG deployment.
Keep the current Hugging Face dataset download pattern, but use NEPA_RAG_DB_HF_REPO.





Add src/nepa_rag/config.py.
Add .env.example.
Add phase2/rag/data/.gitignore.
Add a Makefile with rag-build and rag-app targets.





Adapt the Phase 1 DuckDB builder to Phase 2 paths.
Join pages through documents to attach project_id.
Output rag_catalog.duckdb, page shards, and manifest.json.
Make the script idempotent.





Generate paragraph-aware chunk shards from page shards.
Reuse shared text formatting/chunking helpers from src/nepa_rag/.
Write consistent source_label values.
Make the script idempotent.





Materialize each chunk shard into its own DuckDB.
Create the DuckDB FTS index with stemmer='porter' and stopwords='english'.
Rebuild indexes after every chunk rebuild.





Use selected project context from the UI as the primary project-specific scope.
Use exact project_id or DuckDB ILIKE title search only as fallback.
Return a visible scope label to users, such as “Answering within selected project” or “Searching across corpus.”





Start with DuckDB structured lookup plus FTS over relevant shard indexes.
Rank and deduplicate evidence.
Return source cards with project_id, project title, file name, document type, page number, and snippet.
Add source-page links that jump into the existing document viewer.





Add llm.py with an Ollama provider first.
Add answer.py to combine router output, retrieved evidence, prompt template, model response, and citations.
Add strict output validation so the app can detect missing citations or unsupported claims.





Add an “Ask” tab above or beside the existing browser.
Show answer, warning/confidence, evidence cards, and source-page links.
Keep session-only chat history.
Add a “clear session” button.
Do not persist user queries by default.




Create phase2/rag/eval/questions.yaml with representative tests:

project-specific timeline question
Federal Register / NOI evidence question
broad corpus question
deliverable-production question
unsupported question that should trigger a warning
question with an ambiguous project title

Score each test for:

retrieval hit rate
citation correctness
answer faithfulness
warning behavior
latency
whether the answer uses structured data where required

This is important, but it should not block the first working local MVP.



After the local MVP works, benchmark:

average latency per query
p95 latency
prompt token size
model memory use
shard download behavior
failure cases
cold start time

Use those results to choose between:

website link to HF Space UI plus your local model endpoint;
paid GPU app/model hosting;
hosted API fallback.












Risk
Mitigation




EIS scale makes one DB too large
Use sharded page, chunk, and FTS artifacts; never build one FTS over all 6.7M pages.


Shard fan-out is slow for whole-corpus questions
Route by selected project/process first; use per-shard top-k and merge results; cache downloaded shards.


Pages lack project_id
Join pages through documents_combined before writing page/chunk shards.


Re-running build scripts creates duplicate chunks
Make scripts idempotent with replace semantics and stale-shard cleanup.


FTS index becomes stale after chunk rebuild
Require 03_build_indexes.py after every 02_build_chunks.py run.


DuckDB FTS semantics are misunderstood
Document it as TF-IDF based, not BM25.


Gemma 4 E4B is too slow locally
Use gemma4:e2b as the default fast model; use DuckDB/code for routing and retrieval; reduce retrieved context.


Free hosting cannot serve local models reliably
Treat free hosting as UI-only; host the model separately or use paid GPU/API.


Broad corpus questions retrieve weak evidence
Add clear warnings; require source diversity; route exact counts to DuckDB.


Model invents unsupported details
Require exact source_label citations, validate labels, and show source cards directly under answers.


Long context causes latency and noise
Pass only ranked evidence snippets, not full documents.


CAFT users over-trust generated answers
Use visible confidence/warning labels and “Evidence used” sections.


Session logs create privacy concern
Keep chat history in Streamlit session state only; no persistent logs by default.


Deliverable outputs conflict with source text
Label deliverables as analysis outputs and prefer source text for factual evidence.







What EIS shard size should be the default: fixed document count, fixed approximate bytes, or fixed row count?
Should CAFT access use a simple shared password, Hugging Face auth, or a private app?
Can your local machine act as the model backend during the pilot, or does CAFT need a cloud-hosted model from day one?
Should final Phase 2 deliverables be indexed as answer context, or only as methodology/results references?
Should the app allow corpus-wide answers by default, or require users to explicitly choose “whole corpus” to avoid accidental broad searches?
What answer latency is acceptable for CAFT: 10 seconds, 30 seconds, 2 minutes?
Should the app export answer packets as PDF/HTML for deliverable production?
Should unsupported answers say “best guess” or “likely answer” when evidence is thin?
Should every answer include a downloadable evidence CSV?





Google announced Gemma 4 on April 2, 2026, including E2B, E4B, 26B MoE, and 31B Dense variants, Apache 2.0 licensing, long-context support, and Hugging Face/Ollama support: https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/gemma-4/
Hugging Face Spaces remains a good fit for the Streamlit UI and dataset-download pattern, but model serving should be benchmarked separately from the UI host. HF documents the default free Space as CPU Basic and notes that free Spaces sleep after inactivity: https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/spaces-overview
Hugging Face GPU Spaces are available as paid upgrades with larger CPU/GPU memory, which is relevant if the model is hosted in the same app rather than called through a separate endpoint: https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/spaces-gpus

title: Phase 2 RAG Build Plan
text:
Build a CAFT-facing RAG application that answers questions over NEPATEC2.0 source text, project metadata, and selected Phase 2 deliverable artifacts. The app should build on the existing Streamlit/DuckDB document explorer architecture, use Gemma 4 E2B as the fast local default during development, offer Gemma 4 E4B as a quality option, and keep the implementation under phase2/rag. Larger Gemma 4 models such as 26B or 31B can remain optional later benchmarks, but they are too large and slow for the default local path.
The product goal is answers with evidence, not a semantic-search tool. Retrieval is still required internally, but the user experience should be: ask a question, receive a grounded answer, see cited sources, and click through to the source page.

title: Phase 2 RAG Build Plan
text:
Audience: CAFT staff, likely 5 users.
Expected use: up to roughly 10,000 queries per month, unevenly distributed.
Data scope: NEPATEC source text first; final Phase 2 deliverables may be added if they improve answer quality.
Access pattern: browser-based app, eventually linked from the existing website or hosted similarly to the document explorer.
Logging: session-only chat history by default. Avoid persistent query logs unless CAFT explicitly wants them.
Failure mode: best guess is acceptable only with a strong, visible warning and source limitations.
Correctness requirement: answers must cite evidence where applicable and distinguish sourced claims from inference.

title: Phase 2 RAG Build Plan
text:
Do not build one monolithic DuckDB/FTS store over all page text. The Phase 2 page scale is too large for a single easy-to-host file:



Process
Pages




CE
73,544


EA
469,106


EIS
6,131,757


Total
6,674,407



A single FTS index over 6.7M pages would take hours to build, create a multi-GB DuckDB file, and risks exceeding Hugging Face’s 5 GB per-file limit or making app cold starts too slow.


Build the RAG store as shards:

CE shard: one CE chunk/page shard.
EA shard: one EA chunk/page shard.
EIS shards: many EIS chunk/page shards, split by stable document_id ordering or hash buckets.
Never split a single document_id across shards.
Write a shard manifest that records process type, shard id, file paths, row counts, document counts, and build timestamp.

This keeps each deployable artifact small enough for Hugging Face Dataset storage and lets the app route to the right shard. HF supports multi-file datasets, so deployment should upload the manifest plus all shard files. The simplest MVP can download all shards at startup. If that is too slow, the app should download the manifest first and then lazily download only the needed shards. DuckDB can read page shards directly with a glob such as read_parquet('.../pages_eis_*.parquet') for lazy EIS page lookup.
Because DuckDB FTS requires a materialized table, each searchable shard should also have its own DuckDB file with a rag_chunks table and FTS index:
phase2/rag/data/
├── manifest.json
├── rag_catalog.duckdb
├── pages_ce.parquet
├── pages_ea.parquet
├── pages_eis_000.parquet
├── pages_eis_001.parquet
├── chunks_ce.parquet
├── chunks_ea.parquet
├── chunks_eis_000.parquet
├── chunks_eis_001.parquet
├── rag_chunks_ce.duckdb
├── rag_chunks_ea.duckdb
├── rag_chunks_eis_000.duckdb
└── rag_chunks_eis_001.duckdb
The app should query only relevant shard indexes when a process type or selected project is known. For whole-corpus questions, it can fan out across shards with per-shard top-k retrieval, then merge and rerank the evidence.

title: Phase 2 RAG Build Plan
text:
The existing document explorer already solves several production problems:

Streamlit app shell and browser UI.
DuckDB-backed project/document/page lookup.
Hugging Face dataset download support through NEPA_DB_HF_REPO and hf_hub_download.
Full-text page search with DuckDB FTS and LIKE fallback.
Project filters, document browser, page reader, and source-page navigation.

The RAG app should reuse this architecture instead of replacing it. The main difference is that the Phase 2 RAG app should live under phase2/rag, use sharded artifacts, and expose an answer workflow in addition to the existing browse/read workflow.

text:
Pin DuckDB to a modern version and load local configuration through .env.
phase2/rag/app/requirements.txt should include:

# Local data

RAG_TOP_K_PER_SHARD=3

title: Phase 2 RAG Build Plan
text:
Build a small catalog database containing metadata and shard information:

projects
documents
shards
optional deliverable/result metadata

The catalog should not include all page text. It should be small enough to download quickly at app startup.



Build process-specific page shards for lazy document viewing and per-project page lookup:
pages_ce.parquet
pages_ea.parquet
pages_eis_000.parquet
pages_eis_001.parquet
...
Each page shard must include:
shard_id
process_type
document_id
project_id
page_number
page_number_int
page_text
Pages parquets do not contain project_id. The build script must join through documents:
pages.document_id
  -> documents_combined.document_id
  -> documents_combined.project_id
  -> projects_combined.project_id
page_number is stored as text in source parquets. Build scripts must preserve the original page_number and derive page_number_int safely:
COALESCE(
    TRY_CAST(regexp_extract(CAST(page_number AS VARCHAR), '([0-9]+)', 1) AS INTEGER),
    0
) AS page_number_int
This handles non-numeric page labels such as i, A-1, and appendix-style pages without losing the original label.



Build matching chunk shards:
chunks_ce.parquet
chunks_ea.parquet
chunks_eis_000.parquet
chunks_eis_001.parquet
...
Proposed rag_chunks schema:
chunk_id
shard_id
process_type
project_id
project_title
lead_agency
lead_agency_harmonized
project_state
project_type
document_id
file_name
document_type
document_type_clean
document_type_category
main_document
page_number
page_number_int
chunk_index_on_page
char_start
char_end
chunk_text
token_estimate
source_label
Use this exact source_label format so prompts, citations, and validators can parse it consistently:
[Project: {project_title} ({project_id}); Document: {file_name} ({document_id}); Page: {page_number}]
The answer prompt should require citations by exact source_label, and answer.py should validate that every cited label exists in the retrieved evidence set.
Chunking rules:

Keep page boundaries intact for citations.
Prefer paragraph-bounded chunks when possible.
Target roughly 800-1,500 tokens per chunk.
Add 100-200 token overlap only when splitting long pages.
Preserve project_id, document_id, page_number, and source_label on every chunk.
Prioritize main_document == "YES" during retrieval.

CE page length warning: CE “pages” average roughly 12,765 characters (~3,200 tokens), compared to ~2,200 characters for EA and EIS. CE records are full documents concatenated into one row, not individual PDF pages. The chunking script must handle CE pages as long documents requiring 3–4 sub-page splits each, not as single-chunk inputs. EA and EIS pages typically fit in 1–2 chunks.
Reuse the paragraph and heading regex logic already in app/app.py, especially:

BULLET_RE
SECTION_HEADING_RE
NUMBERED_HEADING_RE
LETTERED_HEADING_RE
ALL_CAPS_HEADING_RE
TOC_HEADING_RE

Move shared text cleanup/chunking logic into src/nepa_rag/text_formatting.py and src/nepa_rag/chunking.py. Do not duplicate these regexes inside the build scripts or import the Streamlit app directly into build code.



Each chunk shard should have a matching DuckDB FTS shard:
rag_chunks_ce.duckdb
rag_chunks_ea.duckdb
rag_chunks_eis_000.duckdb
...
DuckDB FTS is static for this use case. Build it only after all rows have been inserted. If chunks are rebuilt, the FTS index must be rebuilt too.
Use this SQL in 03_build_indexes.py after materializing each shard’s rag_chunks table:
INSTALL fts;
LOAD fts;
PRAGMA create_fts_index(
    'rag_chunks',
    'chunk_id',
    'chunk_text',
    stemmer='porter',
    stopwords='english',
    overwrite=1
);
DuckDB FTS is TF-IDF based, not true BM25. Avoid calling it BM25 in code or documentation. Use names such as fts_score, tfidf_score, or search_score.



Add these later only if they improve deliverable production:

final report text from phase2/reports
output tables from phase2/output
Federal Register artifacts from phase2/data/analysis/federal_register
timeline outputs
architecture/runbook markdown for methodology questions

Deliverable artifacts should be labeled as analysis outputs, not source documents, so the model does not confuse computed results with NEPATEC evidence.

title: Phase 2 RAG Build Plan
text:
Responsibilities:

Read Phase 2 projects, documents, and page parquets.
Use projects_combined.project_id and projects_combined.lead_agency; do not join through processes_combined.
Join pages through documents to attach project_id and project metadata.
Create rag_catalog.duckdb.
Create sharded page parquets.
Create manifest.json.

Required joins:
pages.document_id
  -> documents_combined.document_id
  -> documents_combined.project_id
  -> projects_combined.project_id
Idempotency:

Re-running the script must replace the catalog and page shards for the requested build scope.
Use temporary output paths and atomic rename where practical.
Remove stale shard files listed in the old manifest before writing the new manifest.




Responsibilities:

Read page shards from manifest.json.
Generate chunk shards.
Preserve source metadata and source_label.
Reuse shared chunking helpers from src/nepa_rag/.

Idempotency:

Re-running the script must replace chunk shards, not append duplicates.
For any DuckDB staging table, use DROP TABLE IF EXISTS rag_chunks before recreation.
After this script runs, 03_build_indexes.py is required because FTS indexes are stale.




Responsibilities:

Build one DuckDB FTS file per chunk shard.
Materialize the shard’s rag_chunks table before creating the FTS index.
Record index file paths and row counts back into manifest.json.

Idempotency:

Re-running the script must replace each index DuckDB.
Use DROP TABLE IF EXISTS rag_chunks and overwrite=1 for FTS creation.
If any chunk shard changes, rebuild the corresponding FTS shard.




Post-MVP task. This should not block the first working local app.
Responsibilities:

Run representative questions through the router, retrieval, and answer pipeline.
Check retrieval hit rate, citation correctness, warning behavior, latency, and use of structured data.
Write a small report to phase2/rag/eval/.

text:
Add a simple Makefile so the local rebuild path is one command:
.PHONY: rag-store rag-chunks rag-index rag-build rag-eval rag-app

rag-chunks:

rag-build: rag-store rag-chunks rag-index

rag-app:
    conda run -n nepa streamlit run phase2/rag/app/app.py

title: Phase 2 RAG Build Plan
text:
Use a new Hugging Face Dataset repo for Phase 2 RAG artifacts rather than reusing the existing document explorer DB repo.
Recommended repo:
YOUR_HF_USERNAME/nepa-phase2-rag-db
Upload:

manifest.json
rag_catalog.duckdb
page parquet shards
chunk parquet shards
per-shard DuckDB FTS files

The app should use NEPA_RAG_DB_HF_REPO, not the old document explorer NEPA_DB_HF_REPO, so the two apps can evolve independently.

title: Phase 2 RAG Build Plan
text:
A full RAG system still needs retrieval, but retrieval should be hidden behind the answer workflow. Do not build a separate semantic-search UI unless later requested.


Route each question before retrieval:

Selected-project mode

Primary project scoping signal should come from the UI, not NLP.
If the user has selected a project in the explorer, treat that project as authoritative scope.
Restrict retrieval to that project unless the user explicitly asks for comparison or whole-corpus search.

Free-text project resolution

Use only when no project is selected.
Check exact project_id first.
Then run a DuckDB ILIKE title search over projects.
If there are multiple plausible matches, ask the user to choose rather than guessing.
Avoid fuzzy NLP project detection in the MVP.

Deliverable-specific question

Use deliverable outputs and architecture docs first.
Pull NEPATEC source examples only when needed for evidence.

Corpus-wide factual question

Use DuckDB for exact counts, filters, and tabular summaries.
Use RAG only to explain or cite examples.

Corpus-wide source-text question

Fan out retrieval across relevant shards.
Merge per-shard top-k results.
Return a warning if retrieved evidence is sparse or concentrated in only a few projects.

Unsupported or ambiguous question

Ask for clarification when needed, or answer with a strong limitation warning.





Start with deterministic retrieval, because the existing explorer already has the needed text store:

Structured lookup

Resolve selected project, documents, process type, agency, state, energy type, timeline fields, Federal Register artifacts, and shard ids.

DuckDB FTS / TF-IDF retrieval

Search rag_chunks.chunk_text in relevant shard indexes.
Apply metadata filters from the query router.
Boost main documents, title matches, Federal Register evidence pages, and timeline/date contexts.

Evidence assembly

Deduplicate adjacent chunks from the same page.
Keep no more than 10-20 source passages in the answer prompt.
Always preserve source metadata and source_label.

Optional vector fallback

Do not implement first unless FTS misses obvious evidence.
If needed, add an internal embedding index for retrieval only. This should not become a separate semantic-search feature.

title: Phase 2 RAG Build Plan
text:
Use the configured Gemma 4 fast model for local development and answer synthesis. Start with gemma4:e2b for smoke tests and CPU-bound work, and make gemma4:e4b available as a user-selectable quality mode when latency is acceptable.
The answer prompt should pass structured evidence, not a raw dump of pages:
QUESTION
USER_SCOPE
STRUCTURED_FACTS
SOURCE_PASSAGES
DELIVERABLE_CONTEXT
INSTRUCTIONS
Required answer behavior:

Answer from the supplied evidence.
If evidence is incomplete, give the best supported answer with a clear warning.
Cite each factual claim using exact source_label values.
Separate direct evidence from inference.
Never invent dates, counts, agencies, project titles, document numbers, or citations.
For exact counts and tables, use DuckDB results rather than model reasoning.
Include a short “Evidence used” section with clickable source-page links in the app.

Proposed response shape:
Answer
Confidence / warning
Evidence used
Notes and limitations
Suggested follow-up query
answer.py should validate model output before display:

every citation must match a retrieved source_label;
warnings must be present when retrieval confidence is low;
exact counts should be sourced from structured query output;
if validation fails, the app should show a warning and the source cards rather than silently trusting the answer.

title: Phase 2 RAG Build Plan
text:
Use a provider abstraction from the start:
LLM_PROVIDER=ollama
LLM_MODEL=gemma4:e2b
LLM_QUALITY_MODEL=gemma4:e4b
LLM_FALLBACK_MODEL=gemma4:e2b
OLLAMA_HOST=http://localhost:11434
The first implementation should call a local Ollama server from the Streamlit app. Keep the provider interface generic enough to swap in vLLM, Hugging Face Inference Endpoints, Vertex AI, or another remote endpoint later.
Implementation notes:

Use Gemma 4 E2B as the default fast synthesis model for local testing.
Offer Gemma 4 E4B as a quality model when local hardware supports it.
Keep the exact Ollama tag configurable because model tags and quantizations may differ.
Require ollama pull <configured-tag> during local setup.
Use gemma4:e2b as the documented local fallback if Gemma 4 E4B is too slow or too memory-heavy.
Benchmark local latency with realistic prompts before committing to a hosting path.
Use deterministic code for query routing. Do not spend large-model inference on simple routing decisions.
Do not expose model chain-of-thought. Store only the final answer, cited evidence, and UI state.
Keep prompts short enough for good latency even though Gemma 4 supports long context.

title: Phase 2 RAG Build Plan
text:
Run everything locally:
Streamlit app -> local sharded DuckDB/parquet artifacts -> local Ollama model
This validates correctness, prompts, retrieval, citations, and latency before deployment decisions.



Keep the document explorer pattern:
Website / Quarto navbar -> Hugging Face Space -> downloaded sharded RAG artifacts
For Gemma 4 E2B/E4B, the Space should initially be treated as the UI host, not necessarily the model host. A free CPU Space may still be too slow for acceptable inference. The app can call a separate model endpoint through environment variables.




Your machine as the model backend

Cost: near $0.
Path: expose a private HTTPS endpoint with Cloudflare Tunnel, Tailscale Funnel, or a similar tunnel.
Pros: cheapest way to keep using a local Gemma 4 model.
Cons: depends on your machine being awake, online, secure, and fast enough.

Paid GPU hosting

Cost: variable, likely nonzero if always-on.
Path: Hugging Face GPU Space, HF Inference Endpoint, RunPod, Modal, Baseten, Vertex AI, or Cloud Run/GKE with GPU.
Pros: better reliability for CAFT.
Cons: larger Gemma 4 models need serious memory, especially with long context; always-on GPU hosting will not be free.

Hosted API fallback

Cost: usually low at 10,000 queries/month if prompts are controlled.
Path: keep the same provider interface and swap from local Gemma to hosted API if self-hosting is not practical.
Pros: easiest reliability story.
Cons: may not satisfy the open-model preference; privacy/data-use rules must be checked.





A cold start is the delay when an app or model server has been idle and must restart before answering. For this RAG app, cold start could include starting Streamlit, downloading/opening the catalog, downloading needed shards, loading the model, and warming the first inference request.
Cold start affects wait time, not answer correctness. For Gemma 4 E2B/E4B, model cold starts should be much lighter than 26B/31B, but still depend on hardware and deployment.

title: Phase 2 RAG Build Plan
text:
Risk
Mitigation




EIS scale makes one DB too large
Use sharded page, chunk, and FTS artifacts; never build one FTS over all 6.7M pages.


Shard fan-out is slow for whole-corpus questions
Route by selected project/process first; use per-shard top-k and merge results; cache downloaded shards.


Pages lack project_id
Join pages through documents_combined before writing page/chunk shards.


Re-running build scripts creates duplicate chunks
Make scripts idempotent with replace semantics and stale-shard cleanup.


FTS index becomes stale after chunk rebuild
Require 03_build_indexes.py after every 02_build_chunks.py run.


DuckDB FTS semantics are misunderstood
Document it as TF-IDF based, not BM25.


Gemma 4 E4B is too slow locally
Use gemma4:e2b as the default fast model; use DuckDB/code for routing and retrieval; reduce retrieved context.


Free hosting cannot serve local models reliably
Treat free hosting as UI-only; host the model separately or use paid GPU/API.


Broad corpus questions retrieve weak evidence
Add clear warnings; require source diversity; route exact counts to DuckDB.


Model invents unsupported details
Require exact source_label citations, validate labels, and show source cards directly under answers.


Long context causes latency and noise
Pass only ranked evidence snippets, not full documents.


CAFT users over-trust generated answers
Use visible confidence/warning labels and “Evidence used” sections.


Session logs create privacy concern
Keep chat history in Streamlit session state only; no persistent logs by default.


Deliverable outputs conflict with source text
Label deliverables as analysis outputs and prefer source text for factual evidence.

import os
if os.environ.get("CONDA_DEFAULT_ENV") != "nepa":
    raise SystemExit("Please run in conda env 'nepa'.")

import sys
import re
import duckdb
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Optional
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer

# Reuse section label map from extract_timeline.py
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parents[2] / "extract"))
from extract_timeline import _build_section_label_map



DATA_DIR = Path("data")
EA_PAGES_PATH = DATA_DIR / "processed" / "ea" / "pages.parquet"
PROJECTS_PATH = DATA_DIR / "analysis" / "projects_combined.parquet"
REVIEWS_PATH = DATA_DIR / "analysis" / "projects_reviews.parquet"
OUTPUT_PATH = DATA_DIR / "analysis" / "fonsi" / "fonsi_embeddings.parquet"
OUTPUT_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# FONSI identification patterns (for title/filename matching)
FONSI_TITLE_PATTERNS = [
    r"\bFONSI\b",
    r"finding of no significant impact",
    r"mitigated.*finding",
    r"mitigated FONSI",
]

# Sections to skip (same as D2)
SKIP_SECTION_PATTERNS = [
    r"appendix", r"appendices", r"references", r"bibliography",
    r"cover sheet", r"table of contents", r"list of figures",
]

EMBEDDING_MODEL = "all-MiniLM-L6-v2"
BATCH_SIZE = 256
MAX_WORDS_PER_CHUNK = 200
MIN_WORDS_PER_CHUNK = 30



def identify_fonsi_projects(conn: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection) -> list:
    """
    Identify FONSI project IDs from two sources:
    1. projects_reviews.parquet where review_type == 'fonsi'
    2. EA document title/filename containing FONSI keywords
    """
    fonsi_ids = set()

    # Source 1: reviews table (preferred — more reliable)
    if Path(REVIEWS_PATH).exists():
        ids_from_reviews = conn.execute(f"""
            SELECT DISTINCT project_id
            FROM read_parquet('{REVIEWS_PATH}')
            WHERE lower(review_type) = 'fonsi'
               OR lower(review_type) LIKE '%finding of no significant%'
        """).fetchdf()["project_id"].tolist()
        fonsi_ids.update(ids_from_reviews)

    # Source 2: EA page titles (fallback; may over-include)
    # Look for FONSI language in first 5 pages
    if Path(EA_PAGES_PATH).exists():
        pattern_sql = " OR ".join([
            f"regexp_matches(lower(page_text), '{p.lower()}')"
            for p in FONSI_TITLE_PATTERNS
        ])
        ids_from_pages = conn.execute(f"""
            SELECT DISTINCT project_id
            FROM read_parquet('{EA_PAGES_PATH}')
            WHERE page_num <= 5
              AND ({pattern_sql})
        """).fetchdf()["project_id"].tolist()
        fonsi_ids.update(ids_from_pages)

    print(f"Identified {len(fonsi_ids)} FONSI projects")
    return list(fonsi_ids)



def chunk_page(page_text: str, max_words: int = MAX_WORDS_PER_CHUNK) -> list[str]:
    """Split page text into ~200-word chunks."""
    paragraphs = [p.strip() for p in page_text.split('\n\n') if p.strip()]
    chunks = []
    current = []
    current_words = 0

    for para in paragraphs:
        words = len(para.split())
        if words < MIN_WORDS_PER_CHUNK:
            current.append(para)
            current_words += words
            if current_words >= max_words:
                chunks.append(' '.join(current))
                current, current_words = [], 0
        else:
            if current:
                chunks.append(' '.join(current))
                current, current_words = [], 0
            chunks.append(para)

    if current:
        chunks.append(' '.join(current))

    return [c for c in chunks if len(c.split()) >= MIN_WORDS_PER_CHUNK]



def extract_fonsi_features(
    sample: Optional[int] = None,
    output_path: Path = OUTPUT_PATH,
) -> pd.DataFrame:

    run_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    conn = duckdb.connect()
    model = SentenceTransformer(EMBEDDING_MODEL)

    # Identify FONSI projects
    fonsi_ids = identify_fonsi_projects(conn)
    if sample:
        import random; random.seed(42)
        fonsi_ids = random.sample(fonsi_ids, min(sample, len(fonsi_ids)))

    all_results = []

    # Process in batches of 50 projects
    for i in range(0, len(fonsi_ids), 50):
        batch_ids = fonsi_ids[i:i+50]
        ids_str = ",".join(f"'{p}'" for p in batch_ids)

        pages = conn.execute(f"""
            SELECT project_id, page_num, page_text
            FROM read_parquet('{EA_PAGES_PATH}')
            WHERE project_id IN ({ids_str})
              AND length(page_text) > 100
            ORDER BY project_id, page_num
        """).fetchdf()

        for project_id, proj_pages in pages.groupby("project_id"):
            proj_pages = proj_pages.sort_values("page_num")
            full_pages = list(zip(proj_pages["page_num"], proj_pages["page_text"]))

            # Filter sections — reuse _build_section_label_map
            section_map = _build_section_label_map(full_pages)
            filtered_pages = []
            for page_num, page_text in full_pages:
                section = section_map.get(page_num, "")
                if any(re.search(p, section, re.IGNORECASE) for p in SKIP_SECTION_PATTERNS):
                    continue
                filtered_pages.append((page_num, page_text))

            # Chunk all filtered pages
            all_chunks = []
            all_positions = []
            all_page_nums = []
            pos = 0
            for page_num, page_text in filtered_pages:
                chunks = chunk_page(page_text)
                all_chunks.extend(chunks)
                all_positions.extend(range(pos, pos + len(chunks)))
                all_page_nums.extend([page_num] * len(chunks))
                pos += len(chunks)

            if not all_chunks:
                continue

            # Generate embeddings in batch
            embeddings = model.encode(
                all_chunks,
                batch_size=BATCH_SIZE,
                normalize_embeddings=True,
                show_progress_bar=False
            )

            for j, (chunk_text, chunk_pos, chunk_page, embedding) in enumerate(
                zip(all_chunks, all_positions, all_page_nums, embeddings)
            ):
                all_results.append({
                    "project_id": project_id,
                    "paragraph_text": chunk_text[:1000],  # cap at 1000 chars
                    "paragraph_position": chunk_pos,
                    "page_num": chunk_page,
                    "embedding": embedding.tolist(),
                    "fonsi_extraction_run_at": run_at,
                })

        print(f"Batch {i//50 + 1}: processed {len(batch_ids)} FONSI projects")

    df = pd.DataFrame(all_results)
    df.to_parquet(output_path, index=False)
    print(f"Wrote {len(df)} rows to {output_path}")
    return df


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import argparse
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--sample", type=int, default=None, help="Pilot: run on N projects")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    extract_fonsi_features(sample=args.sample)





Using Python for BERTopic (easier than R for this task). Can export results to CSV for R visualization.
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path
from bertopic import BERTopic
from umap import UMAP
from hdbscan import HDBSCAN

FONSI_PATH = Path("data/analysis/fonsi/fonsi_embeddings.parquet")
OUTPUT_DIR = Path("output/deliverable06")
OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

def analyze_fonsi_patterns(
    min_cluster_size: int = 10,
    n_topics: int = None,  # None = auto-detect
    random_state: int = 42,
) -> None:

    # Load embeddings
    df = pd.read_parquet(FONSI_PATH)
    embeddings = np.array(df["embedding"].tolist())
    paragraphs = df["paragraph_text"].tolist()

    print(f"Loaded {len(df)} paragraphs from {df['project_id'].nunique()} FONSI projects")

    # BERTopic setup — set random states for reproducibility
    umap_model = UMAP(
        n_components=5,
        n_neighbors=15,
        min_dist=0.0,
        metric='cosine',
        random_state=random_state,
    )
    hdbscan_model = HDBSCAN(
        min_cluster_size=min_cluster_size,
        metric='euclidean',
        cluster_selection_method='eom',
        prediction_data=True,
    )

    topic_model = BERTopic(
        umap_model=umap_model,
        hdbscan_model=hdbscan_model,
        language="english",
        calculate_probabilities=True,
        verbose=True,
        nr_topics=n_topics,  # None = automatic
    )

    topics, probs = topic_model.fit_transform(paragraphs, embeddings)

    # Topic info
    topic_info = topic_model.get_topic_info()
    print(f"\nFound {len(topic_info) - 1} topics (excluding outlier topic -1)")
    print(topic_info.head(20))

    # Save cluster assignments
    df["topic_id"] = topics
    df["topic_prob"] = probs.max(axis=1) if probs.ndim > 1 else probs
    df[["project_id", "paragraph_position", "paragraph_text", "topic_id", "topic_prob"]].to_csv(
        OUTPUT_DIR / "fonsi_cluster_assignments.csv", index=False
    )

    # Save topic definitions (top terms per topic)
    topic_rows = []
    for topic_id in topic_info["Topic"].tolist():
        if topic_id == -1:
            continue
        top_words = topic_model.get_topic(topic_id)
        topic_rows.append({
            "topic_id": topic_id,
            "count": topic_info.loc[topic_info["Topic"] == topic_id, "Count"].values[0],
            "top_terms": ", ".join([w for w, _ in top_words[:10]]),
            "label": "",  # manual label — fill in after reviewing
        })
    pd.DataFrame(topic_rows).to_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "fonsi_topics.csv", index=False)

    # Topic distribution by project (one row per project-topic)
    project_topics = df.groupby(["project_id", "topic_id"]).size().reset_index(name="n_paragraphs")
    project_topics.to_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "fonsi_topic_distribution.csv", index=False)

    print(f"\nOutputs written to {OUTPUT_DIR}/")
    print("Next step: review fonsi_topics.csv and manually fill in the 'label' column")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import argparse
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--min-cluster-size", type=int, default=10)
    parser.add_argument("--n-topics", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--random-state", type=int, default=42)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    analyze_fonsi_patterns(
        min_cluster_size=args.min_cluster_size,
        n_topics=args.n_topics,
        random_state=args.random_state,
    )
