import spacy

def extract_mitigation_conditions(df: pd.DataFrame, topic_ids_of_interest: list) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Extract mitigation conditions from paragraphs in specified topic clusters.
    Looks for sentences with obligation language + environmental action verb.
    """
    nlp = spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")

    OBLIGATION_PATTERNS = [r"\bshall\b", r"\bmust\b", r"\bwill be required\b", r"\bshall be\b"]
    ENV_VERBS = ["mitigate", "minimize", "avoid", "monitor", "implement",
                 "reduce", "revegetate", "restore", "protect", "install"]

    mitigation_rows = []
    target_paragraphs = df[df["topic_id"].isin(topic_ids_of_interest)]

    for _, row in target_paragraphs.iterrows():
        doc = nlp(row["paragraph_text"])
        for sent in doc.sents:
            sent_text = sent.text.strip()
            has_obligation = any(re.search(p, sent_text, re.IGNORECASE) for p in OBLIGATION_PATTERNS)
            has_env_verb = any(v in sent_text.lower() for v in ENV_VERBS)
            if has_obligation and has_env_verb:
                mitigation_rows.append({
                    "project_id": row["project_id"],
                    "condition_text": sent_text[:500],
                    "topic_id": row["topic_id"],
                })

    return pd.DataFrame(mitigation_rows)






Pilot first: Run --sample 100 on 100 FONSI projects. Inspect fonsi_topics.csv — are the topics interpretable? Can you assign human-readable labels?
Present pilot to CATF: Share top 5-10 topics with example paragraphs. Get confirmation that (a) the clustering is sensible and (b) mitigation extraction is desired.
Cluster stability: Run BERTopic twice with same random_state. If topics shift significantly, increase min_cluster_size or switch to k-means for reproducibility.
Coverage check: Print df['project_id'].nunique() before and after section filtering. If filtering removes >80% of paragraphs, reduce filter aggressiveness.





FONSI identification precision: Title/page-text matching may include non-FONSI EA documents. Manual review of 20 identified projects before full run is recommended.
BERTopic non-determinism: Even with random_state set, HDBSCAN can produce different results across runs due to numerical precision. Document the random_state and min_cluster_size used in all outputs. If instability is a problem, switch to k-means.
Scope: Open-ended deliverable. Without CATF input, results may not align with their needs. Pilot + CATF review is essential before full implementation.
_build_section_label_map import: Same risk as D2 — test the import before assuming it works cleanly from a different directory.

        for project_id, proj_pages in pages.groupby("project_id"):
            proj_pages = proj_pages.sort_values("page_num")
            full_pages = list(zip(proj_pages["page_num"], proj_pages["page_text"]))

            # Filter sections — reuse _build_section_label_map
            section_map = _build_section_label_map(full_pages)
            filtered_pages = []
            for page_num, page_text in full_pages:
                section = section_map.get(page_num, "")
                if any(re.search(p, section, re.IGNORECASE) for p in SKIP_SECTION_PATTERNS):
                    continue
                filtered_pages.append((page_num, page_text))

            # Chunk all filtered pages
            all_chunks = []
            all_positions = []
            all_page_nums = []
            pos = 0
            for page_num, page_text in filtered_pages:
                chunks = chunk_page(page_text)
                all_chunks.extend(chunks)
                all_positions.extend(range(pos, pos + len(chunks)))
                all_page_nums.extend([page_num] * len(chunks))
                pos += len(chunks)

            if not all_chunks:
                continue

            # Generate embeddings in batch
            embeddings = model.encode(
                all_chunks,
                batch_size=BATCH_SIZE,
                normalize_embeddings=True,
                show_progress_bar=False
            )

            for j, (chunk_text, chunk_pos, chunk_page, embedding) in enumerate(
                zip(all_chunks, all_positions, all_page_nums, embeddings)
            ):
                all_results.append({
                    "project_id": project_id,
                    "paragraph_text": chunk_text[:1000],  # cap at 1000 chars
                    "paragraph_position": chunk_pos,
                    "page_num": chunk_page,
                    "embedding": embedding.tolist(),
                    "fonsi_extraction_run_at": run_at,
                })

        print(f"Batch {i//50 + 1}: processed {len(batch_ids)} FONSI projects")

    df = pd.DataFrame(all_results)
    df.to_parquet(output_path, index=False)
    print(f"Wrote {len(df)} rows to {output_path}")
    return df


if __name__ == "__main__":

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--sample", type=int, default=None, help="Pilot: run on N projects")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    extract_fonsi_features(sample=args.sample)

Using Python for BERTopic (easier than R for this task). Can export results to CSV for R visualization.
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path
from bertopic import BERTopic
from umap import UMAP
from hdbscan import HDBSCAN

FONSI_PATH = Path("data/analysis/fonsi/fonsi_embeddings.parquet")
OUTPUT_DIR = Path("output/deliverable06")
OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

def analyze_fonsi_patterns(
    min_cluster_size: int = 10,
    n_topics: int = None,  # None = auto-detect
    random_state: int = 42,
) -> None:

    # Load embeddings
    df = pd.read_parquet(FONSI_PATH)
    embeddings = np.array(df["embedding"].tolist())
    paragraphs = df["paragraph_text"].tolist()

    print(f"Loaded {len(df)} paragraphs from {df['project_id'].nunique()} FONSI projects")

    # BERTopic setup — set random states for reproducibility
    umap_model = UMAP(
        n_components=5,
        n_neighbors=15,
        min_dist=0.0,
        metric='cosine',
        random_state=random_state,
    )
    hdbscan_model = HDBSCAN(
        min_cluster_size=min_cluster_size,
        metric='euclidean',
        cluster_selection_method='eom',
        prediction_data=True,
    )

    topic_model = BERTopic(
        umap_model=umap_model,
        hdbscan_model=hdbscan_model,
        language="english",
        calculate_probabilities=True,
        verbose=True,
        nr_topics=n_topics,  # None = automatic
    )

    topics, probs = topic_model.fit_transform(paragraphs, embeddings)

    # Topic info
    topic_info = topic_model.get_topic_info()
    print(f"\nFound {len(topic_info) - 1} topics (excluding outlier topic -1)")
    print(topic_info.head(20))

    # Save cluster assignments
    df["topic_id"] = topics
    df["topic_prob"] = probs.max(axis=1) if probs.ndim > 1 else probs
    df[["project_id", "paragraph_position", "paragraph_text", "topic_id", "topic_prob"]].to_csv(
        OUTPUT_DIR / "fonsi_cluster_assignments.csv", index=False
    )

    # Save topic definitions (top terms per topic)
    topic_rows = []
    for topic_id in topic_info["Topic"].tolist():
        if topic_id == -1:
            continue
        top_words = topic_model.get_topic(topic_id)
        topic_rows.append({
            "topic_id": topic_id,
            "count": topic_info.loc[topic_info["Topic"] == topic_id, "Count"].values[0],
            "top_terms": ", ".join([w for w, _ in top_words[:10]]),
            "label": "",  # manual label — fill in after reviewing
        })
    pd.DataFrame(topic_rows).to_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "fonsi_topics.csv", index=False)

    # Topic distribution by project (one row per project-topic)
    project_topics = df.groupby(["project_id", "topic_id"]).size().reset_index(name="n_paragraphs")
    project_topics.to_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "fonsi_topic_distribution.csv", index=False)

    print(f"\nOutputs written to {OUTPUT_DIR}/")
    print("Next step: review fonsi_topics.csv and manually fill in the 'label' column")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import argparse
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--min-cluster-size", type=int, default=10)
    parser.add_argument("--n-topics", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--random-state", type=int, default=42)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    analyze_fonsi_patterns(
        min_cluster_size=args.min_cluster_size,
        n_topics=args.n_topics,
        random_state=args.random_state,
    )

import spacy

def extract_mitigation_conditions(df: pd.DataFrame, topic_ids_of_interest: list) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Extract mitigation conditions from paragraphs in specified topic clusters.
    Looks for sentences with obligation language + environmental action verb.
    """
    nlp = spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")

    OBLIGATION_PATTERNS = [r"\bshall\b", r"\bmust\b", r"\bwill be required\b", r"\bshall be\b"]
    ENV_VERBS = ["mitigate", "minimize", "avoid", "monitor", "implement",
                 "reduce", "revegetate", "restore", "protect", "install"]

    mitigation_rows = []
    target_paragraphs = df[df["topic_id"].isin(topic_ids_of_interest)]

    for _, row in target_paragraphs.iterrows():
        doc = nlp(row["paragraph_text"])
        for sent in doc.sents:
            sent_text = sent.text.strip()
            has_obligation = any(re.search(p, sent_text, re.IGNORECASE) for p in OBLIGATION_PATTERNS)
            has_env_verb = any(v in sent_text.lower() for v in ENV_VERBS)
            if has_obligation and has_env_verb:
                mitigation_rows.append({
                    "project_id": row["project_id"],
                    "condition_text": sent_text[:500],
                    "topic_id": row["topic_id"],
                })

    return pd.DataFrame(mitigation_rows)

# --- Initiation date merge ---
# NOI dates are authoritative (not a fallback); override bert_initiation_date
merge_initiation <- function(tl) {
  tl |>
    left_join(
      fr |> select(project_id, noi_publication_date),
      by = "project_id"
    ) |>
    mutate(
      initiation_date = coalesce(
        as.Date(noi_publication_date),  # wins when present
        as.Date(bert_initiation_date)
      )
    )
}

# Decision date: bert_decision_date -> llm_decision_date
add_decision_date <- function(tl) {
  tl |> mutate(
    decision_date = coalesce(
      as.Date(bert_decision_date),
      as.Date(llm_decision_date)
    )
  )
}

ce  <- merge_initiation(ce)  |> add_decision_date()
ea  <- merge_initiation(ea)  |> add_decision_date()
eis <- merge_initiation(eis) |> add_decision_date()

# --- Duration calculation ---
calc_durations <- function(tl, source) {
  tl |>
    filter(!is.na(initiation_date), !is.na(decision_date)) |>
    mutate(
      duration_days = as.numeric(decision_date - initiation_date),
      process_type = source,
      # CEQ regulation periods
      period = case_when(
        decision_date >= as.Date("2023-08-16") ~ "post_FRA",
        decision_date >= as.Date("2022-08-16") ~ "post_IRA",
        decision_date >= as.Date("2020-09-14") ~ "post_2020_CEQ",
        TRUE ~ "pre_2020"
      )
    ) |>
    filter(duration_days > 0, duration_days < 365 * 25)
}

durations <- bind_rows(
  calc_durations(ce, "CE"),
  calc_durations(ea, "EA"),
  calc_durations(eis, "EIS")
) |>
  left_join(
    projects |> select(project_id, agency_name, project_energy_type, state),
    by = "project_id"
  )

# --- Analyses ---

# 1. Summary by process type × period
period_summary <- durations |>
  group_by(process_type, period) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    median_days = median(duration_days),
    p25 = quantile(duration_days, 0.25),
    p75 = quantile(duration_days, 0.75),
    mean_days = mean(duration_days),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 2. Pre/post-FRA statistical test (Wilcoxon rank-sum; durations are right-skewed)
for (pt in c("CE", "EA", "EIS")) {
  pre <- durations |> filter(process_type == pt, period == "pre_2020") |> pull(duration_days)
  post <- durations |> filter(process_type == pt, period == "post_FRA") |> pull(duration_days)
  if (length(pre) > 10 && length(post) > 10) {
    test <- wilcox.test(pre, post)
    cat(sprintf("%s pre vs post-FRA: W=%.1f, p=%.4f\n", pt, test$statistic, test$p.value))
  }
}

# 3. Agency-level comparison (top 10 agencies by project count)
top_agencies <- durations |>
  count(agency_name, sort=TRUE) |>
  head(10) |>
  pull(agency_name)

agency_summary <- durations |>
  filter(agency_name %in% top_agencies) |>
  group_by(agency_name, process_type) |>
  summarise(n = n(), median_days = median(duration_days), .groups = "drop")

# 4. Outliers (>2× IQR for case study packaging)
outliers <- durations |>
  group_by(process_type) |>
  mutate(iqr = IQR(duration_days), q75 = quantile(duration_days, 0.75)) |>
  filter(duration_days > q75 + 2 * iqr) |>
  select(project_id, process_type, duration_days, period, agency_name) |>
  arrange(desc(duration_days))

# --- Coverage caveat ---
coverage <- durations |>
  count(process_type, name = "n_with_duration") |>
  left_join(
    bind_rows(
      ce |> count() |> mutate(process_type = "CE"),
      ea |> count() |> mutate(process_type = "EA"),
      eis |> count() |> mutate(process_type = "EIS")
    ) |> rename(n_total = n),
    by = "process_type"
  ) |>
  mutate(coverage_pct = n_with_duration / n_total)

cat("Coverage rates:\n")
print(coverage)

# --- Outputs ---

write.csv(agency_summary, "output/deliverable04/timelines_by_agency.csv", row.names=FALSE)
write.csv(outliers, "output/deliverable04/timelines_outliers.csv", row.names=FALSE)
write.csv(coverage, "output/deliverable04/timelines_coverage.csv", row.names=FALSE)

import os

import sys

import duckdb

import spacy

from datetime import datetime, timezone

# Add extract/ to path for _build_section_label_map reuse

EA_PAGES_PATH = DATA_DIR / "processed" / "ea" / "pages.parquet"
EIS_PAGES_PATH = DATA_DIR / "processed" / "eis" / "pages.parquet"
PROJECTS_PATH = ANALYSIS_DIR / "projects_combined.parquet"

# Resource area classification (expand keyword sets as needed)
RESOURCE_AREAS = {
    "air_quality": [
        "air quality", "air pollution", "criteria pollutant", "naaqs",
        "particulate matter", "pm2.5", "pm10", "ozone", "nox", "voc",
        "greenhouse gas", "ghg",  # also in climate_ghg but often in air sections
    ],
    "water": [
        "water quality", "groundwater", "surface water", "wetland", "floodplain",
        "stormwater", "runoff", "aquifer", "stream", "creek", "river",
        "section 404", "section 401",
    ],
    "biological": [
        "biological", "wildlife", "species", "habitat", "vegetation",
        "threatened", "endangered", "esa", "migratory bird", "raptor",
        "bat", "fish", "amphibian",
    ],
    "cultural": [
        "cultural", "historic", "archaeological", "tribal", "section 106",
        "nhpa", "traditional cultural", "sacred", "paleontological",
    ],
    "visual": [
        "visual", "viewshed", "aesthetics", "scenic", "landscape character",
        "visual resources", "visual contrast",
    ],
    "noise": [
        "noise", "vibration", "decibel", "dba", "sound level",
        "construction noise", "operational noise",
    ],
    "soils_geology": [
        "soil", "geology", "geologic", "erosion", "compaction",
        "landslide", "seismic", "subsidence", "prime farmland",
    ],
    "socioeconomic": [
        "socioeconomic", "employment", "jobs", "economy", "income",
        "population", "community", "environmental justice", "ej",
    ],
    "transportation": [
        "transportation", "traffic", "road", "highway", "access",
        "haul route", "vehicle trip", "level of service",
    ],
    "land_use": [
        "land use", "zoning", "compatibility", "adjacent land",
        "general plan", "consistency", "right.of.way",
    ],
    "climate_ghg": [
        "climate change", "greenhouse gas", "ghg", "carbon", "co2",
        "methane", "emissions", "global warming",
    ],
    "public_health": [
        "public health", "human health", "hazardous material", "hazmat",
        "toxic", "contamination", "exposure", "risk assessment",
    ],
}

# Significance phrase patterns (from significance_sketch.py, expanded)
SIGNIFICANCE_PATTERNS = {
    "significant_and_unavoidable": [
        r"significant and unavoidable",
        r"unavoidable significant",
        r"significant unavoidable",
        r"cannot be mitigated to below",
        r"remain significant",
    ],
    "less_than_significant": [
        r"less than significant",
        r"less-than-significant",
        r"not significant",
        r"no significant impact",
        r"would not be significant",
        r"will not be significant",
    ],
    "less_than_significant_with_mitigation": [
        r"less than significant with mitigation",
        r"less-than-significant with",
        r"with mitigation.*less than significant",
        r"mitigated to less than significant",
        r"reduced to less than significant",
    ],
    "no_significant_impact": [
        r"finding of no significant impact",
        r"\bFONSI\b",
        r"no significant impact",
    ],
    "significant_impact": [
        r"significant impact",
        r"would be significant",
        r"will be significant",
        r"is significant",
    ],
}

MITIGATION_PATTERNS = [
    r"mitigated to", r"reduced to", r"with implementation of",
    r"with mitigation", r"mitigation measure", r"following mitigation",
    r"with the following", r"through implementation",
]

# Sections to skip
SKIP_SECTION_PATTERNS = [
    r"appendix", r"appendices", r"references", r"bibliography",
    r"alternatives", r"project description", r"purpose and need",
    r"table of contents",
]



def classify_resource_area(text: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Match text against RESOURCE_AREAS keyword sets.
    Returns area name or None if no match.
    Longest match wins if multiple areas match.
    """
    text_lower = text.lower()
    matches = {}
    for area, keywords in RESOURCE_AREAS.items():
        for kw in keywords:
            if re.search(r'\b' + re.escape(kw) + r'\b', text_lower):
                matches[area] = matches.get(area, 0) + 1
    if not matches:
        return None
    return max(matches, key=matches.get)


def detect_significance_type(text: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Detect significance determination type in a sentence.
    Returns determination key or None.
    Priority: less_than_significant_with_mitigation > significant_and_unavoidable > ...
    """
    # Check in priority order
    for det_type in [
        "less_than_significant_with_mitigation",
        "significant_and_unavoidable",
        "no_significant_impact",
        "less_than_significant",
        "significant_impact",
    ]:
        for pat in SIGNIFICANCE_PATTERNS[det_type]:
            if re.search(pat, text, re.IGNORECASE):
                # Guard: avoid false positives for bare "significant_impact"
                if det_type == "significant_impact":
                    # Skip if it's part of a less-than-significant phrase
                    if re.search(r"less.than.significant|not significant", text, re.IGNORECASE):
                        continue
                return det_type
    return None


def detect_mitigation(sentence: str, context_window: str) -> bool:
    """
    True if mitigation language appears in same sentence or context_window (preceding 2 sentences).
    """
    combined = sentence + " " + context_window
    return any(re.search(pat, combined, re.IGNORECASE) for pat in MITIGATION_PATTERNS)


def extract_grammatical_subject(sent, nlp_doc) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Use spaCy dep-parse to find grammatical subject (nsubj) of significance phrase token.
    Returns the full NP span as string, or None.
    """
    for token in sent:
        if token.dep_ == "nsubj":
            # Walk up to find root verb's subject
            subtree = list(token.subtree)
            span_text = sent.doc[subtree[0].i:subtree[-1].i + 1].text
            return span_text
    return None



def extract_significance(
    projects_path: Path = PROJECTS_PATH,
    output_path: Path = OUTPUT_DIR / "projects_significance.parquet",
    use_llm: bool = False,
    sample: Optional[int] = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:

    run_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    conn = duckdb.connect()
    nlp = spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")

    # Load project list
    projects = conn.execute(f"""
        SELECT project_id, process_type
        FROM read_parquet('{projects_path}')
        WHERE process_type IN ('EA', 'EIS')
    """).fetchdf()

    if sample:
        projects = projects.sample(n=min(sample, len(projects)), random_state=42)

    all_results = []

    for source, pages_path in [("EA", EA_PAGES_PATH), ("EIS", EIS_PAGES_PATH)]:
        if not pages_path.exists():
            continue

        source_projects = projects[projects["process_type"] == source]["project_id"].tolist()
        if not source_projects:
            continue

        # Load pages in batches of 100 projects
        batch_size = 100
        for i in range(0, len(source_projects), batch_size):
            batch_ids = source_projects[i:i+batch_size]
            ids_str = ",".join(f"'{p}'" for p in batch_ids)

            pages = conn.execute(f"""
                SELECT project_id, page_num, page_text
                FROM read_parquet('{pages_path}')
                WHERE project_id IN ({ids_str})
                ORDER BY project_id, page_num
            """).fetchdf()

            # Group pages by project
            for project_id, proj_pages in pages.groupby("project_id"):
                proj_pages = proj_pages.sort_values("page_num")
                full_text_pages = list(zip(proj_pages["page_num"], proj_pages["page_text"]))

                # Build section map; filter to resource analysis sections
                section_map = _build_section_label_map(full_text_pages)
                filtered_pages = filter_resource_analysis_pages(full_text_pages, section_map)

                # Segment sentences via spaCy on filtered pages only
                page_texts = [p[1] for p in filtered_pages]
                prev_resource_area = None

                for page_num, page_text in filtered_pages:
                    doc = nlp(page_text)
                    sentences = list(doc.sents)

                    for j, sent in enumerate(sentences):
                        sent_text = sent.text.strip()
                        if len(sent_text) < 20:
                            continue

                        # Detect significance phrase
                        det_type = detect_significance_type(sent_text)
                        if not det_type:
                            continue

                        # Try dep-parse subject first
                        subj_text = extract_grammatical_subject(sent, doc)
                        resource_area = classify_resource_area(subj_text) if subj_text else None

                        # Fallback: resource area in same sentence
                        if not resource_area:
                            resource_area = classify_resource_area(sent_text)

                        # Fallback: preceding sentence's resource area
                        if not resource_area and j > 0:
                            resource_area = classify_resource_area(sentences[j-1].text)

                        # Fallback: last known resource area in document
                        if not resource_area:
                            resource_area = prev_resource_area

                        if resource_area:
                            prev_resource_area = resource_area

                        # Context window for mitigation detection
                        prev_sents = " ".join(s.text for s in sentences[max(0,j-2):j])
                        mit_flag = detect_mitigation(sent_text, prev_sents)

                        # Confidence: high if dep-parse subject found, medium if sentence-level, low if fallback
                        if subj_text and classify_resource_area(subj_text):
                            confidence = "high"
                        elif resource_area and classify_resource_area(sent_text):
                            confidence = "medium"
                        else:
                            confidence = "low"

                        all_results.append({
                            "project_id": project_id,
                            "resource_area": resource_area or "unknown",
                            "determination": det_type,
                            "mitigation_flag": mit_flag,
                            "context_text": sent_text[:500],
                            "source": source,
                            "confidence": confidence,
                            "significance_extraction_run_at": run_at,
                        })

    df = pd.DataFrame(all_results)

    # Optional: LLM adjudication for low-confidence cases
    if use_llm and len(df) > 0:
        df = adjudicate_with_llm(df[df["confidence"] == "low"], df)

    df.to_parquet(output_path, index=False)
    print(f"Wrote {len(df)} rows to {output_path}")
    return df


def filter_resource_analysis_pages(pages, section_map):
    """
    Keep only pages in resource analysis chapters; skip appendices, references, etc.
    Uses section_map from _build_section_label_map.
    """
    resource_sections = {
        "affected_environment", "environmental_consequences",
        "environmental_effects", "chapter_3", "environmental_analysis"
    }
    result = []
    for page_num, page_text in pages:
        section = section_map.get(page_num, "")
        # Skip if in known skip sections
        if any(re.search(pat, section, re.IGNORECASE) for pat in SKIP_SECTION_PATTERNS):
            continue
        # Keep if in resource analysis section (or if section is unknown — be permissive)
        if not section or any(rs in section.lower() for rs in resource_sections):
            result.append((page_num, page_text))
    return result



def adjudicate_with_llm(low_conf_rows: pd.DataFrame, full_df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Claude Haiku adjudication for ~20% low-confidence rows.
    Expects structured JSON: {"resource_area": "...", "determination": "..."}
    """
    import anthropic
    client = anthropic.Anthropic()

    PROMPT = """Extract the resource area and significance determination from this NEPA sentence.

Sentence: {text}

Resource areas: air_quality, water, biological, cultural, visual, noise, soils_geology,
socioeconomic, transportation, land_use, climate_ghg, public_health

Determinations: significant_and_unavoidable, less_than_significant,
less_than_significant_with_mitigation, no_significant_impact, significant_impact

Respond with JSON only: {{"resource_area": "...", "determination": "...", "confidence": "high/medium/low"}}"""
    # ... implementation: iterate low_conf_rows, call API, update fields



if __name__ == "__main__":
    import argparse
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--use-llm", action="store_true", help="Enable LLM adjudication for low-confidence rows")
    parser.add_argument("--sample", type=int, default=None, help="Number of projects to sample")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    extract_significance(use_llm=args.use_llm, sample=args.sample)





library(arrow)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)

sig <- read_parquet("data/analysis/significance/projects_significance.parquet")
projects <- read_parquet("data/analysis/projects_combined.parquet")
df <- left_join(sig, projects, by = "project_id")

# 1. Determination rates by resource area
by_area <- df |>
  count(resource_area, determination) |>
  group_by(resource_area) |>
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n))

# 2. Mitigation flag rates (proportion of determinations with mitigation conditions)
mitigation_rates <- df |>
  filter(determination %in% c("less_than_significant_with_mitigation", "significant_and_unavoidable")) |>
  group_by(resource_area) |>
  summarise(mitigation_pct = mean(mitigation_flag))

# 3. Rates by agency and process type
by_agency <- df |>
  count(agency_name, determination) |>
  group_by(agency_name) |>
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n))

# 4. Mitigated FONSI patterns
fonsi_patterns <- df |>
  filter(determination == "no_significant_impact") |>
  group_by(resource_area, mitigation_flag) |>
  count()

# Outputs
write.csv(by_area, "output/deliverable02/significance_by_resource_area.csv", row.names=FALSE)
write.csv(mitigation_rates, "output/deliverable02/mitigation_rates.csv", row.names=FALSE)
write.csv(by_agency, "output/deliverable02/significance_by_agency.csv", row.names=FALSE)
write.csv(fonsi_patterns, "output/deliverable02/fonsi_patterns.csv", row.names=FALSE)





Pilot: Run --sample 20 on 5 BLM EA/EIS documents. Manually inspect 20 extracted rows — verify resource area and determination match the source text.
Precision check: If dep-parse subject extraction precision <70% on pilot, fall back to sentence-level keyword matching for resource area (use Alternative A — sentence-level keyword).
Agency pilot: Run on top 4 agencies (BLM, DOE, USFS, Corps of Engineers) before full run. If precision <70% on pilot, scope down to those agencies only.
Section filter validation: Print section distribution before filtering — verify that >50% of pages are being filtered out (i.e., filter is working).





_build_section_label_map import: May need to adjust sys.path or copy relevant functions if import structure is complex. Check extract_timeline.py for the function signature before assuming it imports cleanly.
spaCy model availability: Requires en_core_web_sm. Install: python -m spacy download en_core_web_sm.
Agency format variation: EIS format varies widely. Section heading patterns may not fire for some agencies. If <50% of pages are filtered on pilot, expand SECTION_PATTERNS or reduce filter aggressiveness.
Pronoun subjects: dep-parse often finds “it”, “they”, “these” as subject. Fallback chain handles this — verify fallback fires correctly on pilot output.

                    sentences = list(doc.sents)

                    for j, sent in enumerate(sentences):
                        sent_text = sent.text.strip()
                        if len(sent_text) < 20:
                            continue

                        # Detect significance phrase
                        det_type = detect_significance_type(sent_text)
                        if not det_type:
                            continue

                        # Try dep-parse subject first
                        subj_text = extract_grammatical_subject(sent, doc)
                        resource_area = classify_resource_area(subj_text) if subj_text else None

                        # Fallback: resource area in same sentence
                        if not resource_area:
                            resource_area = classify_resource_area(sent_text)

                        # Fallback: preceding sentence's resource area
                        if not resource_area and j > 0:
                            resource_area = classify_resource_area(sentences[j-1].text)

                        # Fallback: last known resource area in document
                        if not resource_area:
                            resource_area = prev_resource_area

                        if resource_area:
                            prev_resource_area = resource_area

                        # Context window for mitigation detection
                        prev_sents = " ".join(s.text for s in sentences[max(0,j-2):j])
                        mit_flag = detect_mitigation(sent_text, prev_sents)

                        # Confidence: high if dep-parse subject found, medium if sentence-level, low if fallback
                        if subj_text and classify_resource_area(subj_text):
                            confidence = "high"
                        elif resource_area and classify_resource_area(sent_text):
                            confidence = "medium"
                        else:
                            confidence = "low"

                        all_results.append({
                            "project_id": project_id,
                            "resource_area": resource_area or "unknown",
                            "determination": det_type,
                            "mitigation_flag": mit_flag,
                            "context_text": sent_text[:500],
                            "source": source,
                            "confidence": confidence,
                            "significance_extraction_run_at": run_at,
                        })

    df = pd.DataFrame(all_results)

    # Optional: LLM adjudication for low-confidence cases
    if use_llm and len(df) > 0:
        df = adjudicate_with_llm(df[df["confidence"] == "low"], df)

    df.to_parquet(output_path, index=False)
    print(f"Wrote {len(df)} rows to {output_path}")
    return df


def filter_resource_analysis_pages(pages, section_map):
    """
    Keep only pages in resource analysis chapters; skip appendices, references, etc.
    Uses section_map from _build_section_label_map.
    """
    resource_sections = {
        "affected_environment", "environmental_consequences",
        "environmental_effects", "chapter_3", "environmental_analysis"
    }
    result = []
    for page_num, page_text in pages:
        section = section_map.get(page_num, "")
        # Skip if in known skip sections
        if any(re.search(pat, section, re.IGNORECASE) for pat in SKIP_SECTION_PATTERNS):
            continue
        # Keep if in resource analysis section (or if section is unknown — be permissive)
        if not section or any(rs in section.lower() for rs in resource_sections):
            result.append((page_num, page_text))
    return result



def adjudicate_with_llm(low_conf_rows: pd.DataFrame, full_df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Claude Haiku adjudication for ~20% low-confidence rows.
    Expects structured JSON: {"resource_area": "...", "determination": "..."}
    """
    import anthropic
    client = anthropic.Anthropic()

    PROMPT = """Extract the resource area and significance determination from this NEPA sentence.

Sentence: {text}

Resource areas: air_quality, water, biological, cultural, visual, noise, soils_geology,
socioeconomic, transportation, land_use, climate_ghg, public_health

Determinations: significant_and_unavoidable, less_than_significant,
less_than_significant_with_mitigation, no_significant_impact, significant_impact

Respond with JSON only: {{"resource_area": "...", "determination": "...", "confidence": "high/medium/low"}}"""
    # ... implementation: iterate low_conf_rows, call API, update fields



if __name__ == "__main__":
    import argparse
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--use-llm", action="store_true", help="Enable LLM adjudication for low-confidence rows")
    parser.add_argument("--sample", type=int, default=None, help="Number of projects to sample")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    extract_significance(use_llm=args.use_llm, sample=args.sample)

title: extract_timeline.py — Changes from Improvement Plan
text:
Date: 2026-03-30 Branch: timeline-duckdb
All changes are in code/extract/extract_timeline.py.



Problem: CE documents use form-field layouts (DOE Initiator Signature ... Date: 01/15/2020) that the existing INITIATION_PATTERNS_STRONG/MED never matched, causing systematic misses in CE initiation weak-supervision labeling.
Changes: - Added INITIATION_PATTERNS_CE_ONLY list (9 patterns) after INITIATION_PATTERNS_WEAK - Added _source_initiation_patterns(source) helper — returns base patterns + CE-specific ones when source == 'CE' - Updated auto_label_context(context) → auto_label_context(context, source=None) to accept source and call _source_initiation_patterns(source) instead of the two flat lists - Updated generate_bert_training_data() to pass dataset_source to auto_label_context()
Retrain required: Yes — --bert-generate then --bert-train --source CE




Problem: min_context_chars parameter in extract_dates_with_context() was declared but never used — the function always called _min_context_chars_for_sentence() directly, ignoring the parameter entirely.
Changes: - Fixed extract_dates_with_context() to use min_context_chars as a floor: min_chars = max(min_context_chars, _min_context_chars_for_sentence(span_text)) - Updated run_regex_prep() → _flush() to pass min_context_chars=200 (was effectively 80), giving 2–4 sentences of context per candidate instead of 1–2
Effect: Wider context improves section heading detection (Phase 1b) and richer BERT input. Does not affect any other call site — the global DATE_CONTEXT_WINDOW = 80 is unchanged.




Problem: Every candidate in the regex cache was a flat context string with no structural signal. BERT had no way to know whether a date appeared in a signature block, an NOI section, or a references list.
Changes: - Added SECTION_PATTERNS dict: per-source (CE, EA, EIS) + all-source heading patterns mapped to canonical labels (ce_determination, signature_block, review_checklist, noi, fonsi, rod, draft_eis, final_eis, references, legal_citations, etc.) - Added _build_section_label_map(page_text, source) — scans full page text for headings, returns sorted (position, label) list - Added _lookup_section_label(char_pos, section_map, max_lookback=1000) — finds nearest preceding heading within 1,000 chars of a date - Updated _flush() in run_regex_prep() to build the section map per-document (while full page text is in memory) and annotate each candidate with section_label
Effect: section_label is now a column in all rebuilt regex cache files. Always runs — no extra flag required.




Problem: The regex cache had no verb or role-phrase features. These are strong signals (e.g., dep_verb == 'sign' + sig_flag == True) for distinguishing decision vs. review dates.
Changes: - Added _enrich_with_spacy(cache_df, source) — runs nlp.pipe(batch_size=512) on cached context strings; extracts dep_verb (ROOT verb lemma), sig_flag (bool, from existing _is_signature_block()), ner_decision_signal (bool, role phrase or PERSON+decision verb) - Added use_spacy=False parameter to run_regex_prep(); enrichment pass runs after the cache is built when use_spacy=True - Added --use-spacy CLI flag to --regex-prep - Graceful degradation: if spaCy or en_core_web_sm not installed, columns are set to ''/False with a warning
New dependency (opt-in): pip install spacy && python -m spacy download en_core_web_sm




Problem: After adding new columns, _make_prefix() and _add_inference_prefix() needed to handle both old caches (no enrichment columns) and new caches gracefully.
Changes: - Updated _make_prefix() in generate_bert_training_data(): - Reads section_label, dep_verb, sig_flag/ner_decision_signal via .get() with empty fallbacks - Appends [sec:X], [verb:X], [sig:Y/N] tokens only when enrichment columns are present - Falls back to current [SRC] [DOCTYPE] format automatically for old caches - Added stale-cache warnings in generate_bert_training_data() when section_label or dep_verb columns are absent




Problem: At inference time (--bert-run), every candidate went through BERT regardless of how obvious the context was. auto_label_context() only ran during training, not inference.
Key design rule: REVIEW_PATTERNS_STRONG contexts always go to BERT — reviewer sign-off dates and final decision dates look identical to a pattern matcher but BERT can distinguish them.
Changes: - Added _pre_bert_triage(context, source, section_label, dep_verb, sig_flag) with 11 priority rules returning (action, label, confidence): - hard_discard: boilerplate, OTHER_PATTERNS_STRONG, references/legal section labels, historical context without decision signal - auto_classify → decision: strong decision patterns (no review pattern), signature_block + decision verb, sig_flag + decision verb, ce_determination section label (CE only) - auto_classify → initiation: strong initiation patterns (no decision/review cue), noi section (EA/EIS only) - bert: any REVIEW_PATTERNS_STRONG match, all other candidates - Wired into extract_with_bert(): only sends bert-tagged candidates to the model; merges results back in original order - Added triage_classified bool and section_label string to classified_dates output - Logs triage counts per run (hard_discard / auto_classify / bert)




Problem: _add_inference_prefix() only accepted source and doc_type; inference prefixes could not include the new enrichment features.
Changes: - Updated _add_inference_prefix(context, source, doc_type, section_label='', dep_verb='',   sig_flag=False) to accept optional enrichment kwargs - Builds the same structured prefix as _make_prefix() at training time - Falls back to [SRC] [DOCTYPE] format when enrichment fields are absent (backwards compatible) - Updated extract_with_bert() to pass section_label, dep_verb, sig_flag from each candidate dict when building prefixed contexts




Problem: _parse_adjudication_response() accepted any LLM-returned dates without validating date ordering or plausible review duration. No QA flag was surfaced in output.
Changes: - Added _PLAUSIBLE_GAP_DAYS dict: CE (30–2000), EA (60–3000), EIS (180–7000) days - Added _validate_adjudication(initiation_date_str, decision_date_str, source) returning pipe-delimited flag string: date_order_error, gap_too_short_Nd, gap_too_long_Nd, or '' - Updated _parse_adjudication_response(response_text, source=None): - Accepts optional source parameter - Parses both new (reason_initiation/reason_decision) and legacy (initiation_reasoning/decision_reasoning) JSON keys - Calls _validate_adjudication() and returns validation_flag in result dict - Returns reason_initiation and reason_decision columns - Updated run_llm_adjudication() to pass task['dataset_source'] to _parse_adjudication_response()




Problem: The adjudication prompt sent flat candidate lines without structural features. The JSON response used initiation_reasoning/decision_reasoning keys that didn’t match the plan’s reason_* naming.
Changes: - Updated candidate line format in _build_adjudication_prompt() to include [sec:X] and [verb:X] tokens when section_label/dep_verb fields are present on the candidate - Updated the JSON response format in the prompt to request reason_initiation and reason_decision (shorter, more direct) - Added a rule hint explaining [sec:] labels to Claude




Problem: _INIT_DOC_TYPE_BOOST had an empty CE entry and there was no triage rule for CE determination sections.
Changes: - Updated _INIT_DOC_TYPE_BOOST['CE'] to include 'CE_DETERMINATION': -2 (penalise CE determination forms for initiation scoring — they are decision documents) - Added ce_determination → auto_classify decision, 0.85 rule in _pre_bert_triage() for CE: many CE determination dates previously fell through as other because the section heading was the only reliable signal in short form-field contexts

title: extract_timeline.py — Changes from Improvement Plan
text:
Problem: min_context_chars parameter in extract_dates_with_context() was declared but never used — the function always called _min_context_chars_for_sentence() directly, ignoring the parameter entirely.
Changes: - Fixed extract_dates_with_context() to use min_context_chars as a floor: min_chars = max(min_context_chars, _min_context_chars_for_sentence(span_text)) - Updated run_regex_prep() → _flush() to pass min_context_chars=200 (was effectively 80), giving 2–4 sentences of context per candidate instead of 1–2
Effect: Wider context improves section heading detection (Phase 1b) and richer BERT input. Does not affect any other call site — the global DATE_CONTEXT_WINDOW = 80 is unchanged.

title: extract_timeline.py — Changes from Improvement Plan
text:
Problem: Every candidate in the regex cache was a flat context string with no structural signal. BERT had no way to know whether a date appeared in a signature block, an NOI section, or a references list.
Changes: - Added SECTION_PATTERNS dict: per-source (CE, EA, EIS) + all-source heading patterns mapped to canonical labels (ce_determination, signature_block, review_checklist, noi, fonsi, rod, draft_eis, final_eis, references, legal_citations, etc.) - Added _build_section_label_map(page_text, source) — scans full page text for headings, returns sorted (position, label) list - Added _lookup_section_label(char_pos, section_map, max_lookback=1000) — finds nearest preceding heading within 1,000 chars of a date - Updated _flush() in run_regex_prep() to build the section map per-document (while full page text is in memory) and annotate each candidate with section_label
Effect: section_label is now a column in all rebuilt regex cache files. Always runs — no extra flag required.

title: extract_timeline.py — Changes from Improvement Plan
text:
Problem: The regex cache had no verb or role-phrase features. These are strong signals (e.g., dep_verb == 'sign' + sig_flag == True) for distinguishing decision vs. review dates.
Changes: - Added _enrich_with_spacy(cache_df, source) — runs nlp.pipe(batch_size=512) on cached context strings; extracts dep_verb (ROOT verb lemma), sig_flag (bool, from existing _is_signature_block()), ner_decision_signal (bool, role phrase or PERSON+decision verb) - Added use_spacy=False parameter to run_regex_prep(); enrichment pass runs after the cache is built when use_spacy=True - Added --use-spacy CLI flag to --regex-prep - Graceful degradation: if spaCy or en_core_web_sm not installed, columns are set to ''/False with a warning
New dependency (opt-in): pip install spacy && python -m spacy download en_core_web_sm

title: extract_timeline.py — Changes from Improvement Plan
text:
Problem: After adding new columns, _make_prefix() and _add_inference_prefix() needed to handle both old caches (no enrichment columns) and new caches gracefully.
Changes: - Updated _make_prefix() in generate_bert_training_data(): - Reads section_label, dep_verb, sig_flag/ner_decision_signal via .get() with empty fallbacks - Appends [sec:X], [verb:X], [sig:Y/N] tokens only when enrichment columns are present - Falls back to current [SRC] [DOCTYPE] format automatically for old caches - Added stale-cache warnings in generate_bert_training_data() when section_label or dep_verb columns are absent

title: extract_timeline.py — Changes from Improvement Plan
text:
Problem: At inference time (--bert-run), every candidate went through BERT regardless of how obvious the context was. auto_label_context() only ran during training, not inference.
Key design rule: REVIEW_PATTERNS_STRONG contexts always go to BERT — reviewer sign-off dates and final decision dates look identical to a pattern matcher but BERT can distinguish them.
Changes: - Added _pre_bert_triage(context, source, section_label, dep_verb, sig_flag) with 11 priority rules returning (action, label, confidence): - hard_discard: boilerplate, OTHER_PATTERNS_STRONG, references/legal section labels, historical context without decision signal - auto_classify → decision: strong decision patterns (no review pattern), signature_block + decision verb, sig_flag + decision verb, ce_determination section label (CE only) - auto_classify → initiation: strong initiation patterns (no decision/review cue), noi section (EA/EIS only) - bert: any REVIEW_PATTERNS_STRONG match, all other candidates - Wired into extract_with_bert(): only sends bert-tagged candidates to the model; merges results back in original order - Added triage_classified bool and section_label string to classified_dates output - Logs triage counts per run (hard_discard / auto_classify / bert)

title: D1: Examples
text: Use this file to collect a small set of representative text chunks for Tier 4 calibration.

title: D1: Examples
text:
How to use these examples
These examples are not training data — the NLI model is zero-shot and runs without them. They serve two specific purposes:

1. Validate NLI hypothesis templates
Before running at scale, score each positive example through the NLI model using the hypothesis templates defined in tier4_refactor_spec.md. The correct class hypothesis should score ≥ 0.75. If a positive example scores below this on its correct class, adjust the hypothesis wording before proceeding.
# Quick validation loop (run once before full corpus)
from sentence_transformers import CrossEncoder
model = CrossEncoder("cross-encoder/nli-MiniLM2-L6-H768")

chunk = "DOE is proposing to provide federal funding..."
hypothesis = "This text shows that a federal agency is funding this project."
score = model.predict([[chunk, hypothesis]])[0]  # entailment score
assert score >= 0.75, f"Positive example scored too low: {score:.3f}"


2. Calibrate auto-accept thresholds
Run hard negative examples (boilerplate chunks under “Hard negatives”) through the NLI model. All class hypotheses should score ≤ 0.50 for a well-calibrated negative. If a boilerplate chunk scores above 0.50 on any class, either tighten the hypothesis wording or raise the auto-accept threshold in the spec (default 0.90).
Do this calibration on the example bank before any full-corpus run. It takes minutes and prevents silent miscalibration at scale.

Seven mutually exclusive primary classes, with a strict priority ordering used when signals conflict:








Priority
Class
Core signal




1

2

Secondary triggers are stored in nepa_trigger_secondary (list) for multi-label combo analysis.






Hand-labeled gold-standard examples loaded from manual_training_corrections.csv. These are ingested first and cannot be overwritten by any subsequent tier. ~400 projects.



Maps lead_agency_harmonized to trigger class using known jurisdiction rules. A result from Tier 1a that is auto-accepted goes directly to finalized; others go to provisional and may be sent to Tier 4 for confirmation.
Key mappings: - FERC, FAA, FCC → federal_permit (auto-accept) - BPA, WAPA, CBP, PMA → federal_direct_action (auto-accept) - BLM, USFS as authorizing agency → federal_land (auto-accept via T1a_BLM_USFS_land_control) - DOE, USACE → routed to Tier 4 (ambiguous without verb evidence)
Adds ~1,500 projects. Highest-yield deterministic tier.



Applies TIER1B_PATTERNS (regex list) against the concatenated project title and description. Each pattern tuple is (regex, class, rule_slug, confidence). If the resulting rule_id (T1b_{slug}) is in AUTO_ACCEPT_RULE_IDS, the result is auto-accepted; otherwise it goes to provisional.
Currently auto-accepted rules: T1b_ferc_license, T1b_special_use, T1b_row_grant, T1b_land_exchange. All other high-confidence Tier 1b matches go to provisional.
Adds ~37 projects to finalized (many more to provisional).



Scans the document titles of the first retrieved documents for each project via DuckDB. Applies _is_programmatic_title, _is_programmatic_exclusion, and DOC_TITLE_PATTERNS.
Currently auto-accepted rules: T2_doc_title_peis, T2_doc_title_row, T2_doc_title_permit_app, T2_doc_title_license_amendment, T2_doc_title_loan_guarantee.
Adds ~282 projects.



Extracts the “Purpose and Need” section (and related candidate sections) from document pages via DuckDB, then applies the same TIER1B_PATTERNS + additional purpose-specific patterns.
Currently auto-accepted rules: T3_npdes, T3_agency_grant, T3_blm_land, T3_nfs_land.
Adds ~481 projects.



Runs only on projects where lead_agency_harmonized contains “Department of Energy” AND process_type == "CE". Uses a fine-tuned SetFit model at phase2/models/trigger_setfit (6-class logistic regression head over a sentence-transformer backbone).
How confidence works in SetFit: predict_proba returns a probability vector over all classes, e.g. [0.04, 0.71, 0.03, 0.14, 0.05, 0.03]. Two gates must both pass: - top_prob >= SETFIT_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD (currently 0.80) - margin = top_prob - second_prob >= SETFIT_MARGIN_THRESHOLD (currently 0.15)
If both gates pass, the result is auto-accepted as confidence="high". If either gate fails, the project falls through to Tier 4 unchanged. With a logistic regression head trained on a small example bank, probabilities rarely concentrate above 0.80. In the April 2026 run, 0 projects cleared the gate despite 436 inference batches.



Receives all projects not yet finalized where should_send_to_tier4 returns True. This includes: projects with no provisional result, projects from ambiguous agencies (DOE, USACE), and projects with medium/low confidence provisionals.
How confidence works in Tier 4 NLI: Uses cross-encoder/nli-deberta-v3-base (or cross-encoder/nli-MiniLM2-L6-H768 as configured). For each candidate class, the model receives the retrieved chunk text as the premise and a natural-language hypothesis as the hypothesis. The entailment score is the final_score per chunk. Scores are aggregated across chunks into a per-project doc_score per candidate class. Three gates must all pass:

doc_score >= threshold: TIER4_BASE_THRESHOLD (0.72) if agency metadata priors exist, TIER4_NO_PRIOR_THRESHOLD (0.78) otherwise
margin >= TIER4_MARGIN_THRESHOLD (0.08): top class must score at least 0.08 above second
affirmative_support: at least one chunk must have cue_score >= 0.25 or entailment_score >= 0.82

If all three pass, auto_resolve=True and the project is finalized as confidence="high" (if doc_score >= 0.95) or confidence="medium" (otherwise). If any gate fails, the project gets rule_id="T4_local_uncertain" with confidence="low" and is queued for Tier 5 (or finalized as unknown if --use-llm is not set).
Diagnostics written to: - phase2/data/analysis/nepa_trigger/tier4_chunk_scores.parquet - phase2/data/analysis/nepa_trigger/tier4_doc_scores.parquet



Claude Haiku receives the Tier 4 uncertain queue (target: <250 projects) with retrieved context chunks and returns structured JSON classification. Only runs with --use-llm flag.







Returns True only when: - rule_id is in AUTO_ACCEPT_RULE_IDS (explicit whitelist of trusted rules), OR - rule_id starts with T4_local_ or T4_embed_ and confidence is high/medium, OR - rule_id == "T5_llm" and confidence is high/medium



Returns True (send to Tier 4) when: - result is None — no provisional result exists for this project - rule_id is in SEND_TO_TIER4_RULE_IDS (T1a_DOE_direct_action, T1a_DOE_funding, T3_sec404) - evidence_source == "agency_metadata" — agency-level priors need document confirmation - confidence != "high" — low/medium confidence provisionals need adjudication
Returns False (do NOT send to Tier 4) when confidence is "high" and the rule is not in SEND_TO_TIER4_RULE_IDS. This creates a logic gap: projects with high-confidence provisional results from rules NOT in AUTO_ACCEPT_RULE_IDS are neither finalized nor sent to Tier 4. They fall through to _make_unknown at the end of the pipeline.



For each result: if should_auto_accept → add to finalized. Otherwise → add to provisional (keeping the higher-confidence result if one already exists).







Projects can have a high-confidence provisional result that is silently discarded: - Rule fires → confidence=“high” → should_auto_accept returns False (rule not in AUTO_ACCEPT_RULE_IDS) → goes to provisional - should_send_to_tier4 returns False (confidence==“high”) → never sent to Tier 4 - At end of pipeline: _make_unknown is called → appears as unknown in output
The original provisional rule_id and evidence text ARE preserved in the unknown record’s nepa_trigger_evidence_text and nepa_trigger_evidence_source fields. In the April 2026 run: 12,528 of the 13,324 had evidence_source="description", indicating a Tier 1b pattern match was silently dropped. Fix: either add those rule IDs to AUTO_ACCEPT_RULE_IDS or change should_send_to_tier4 to also forward high-confidence provisionals to Tier 4.



SETFIT_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD = 0.80 is too strict for a logistic regression head trained on a small example bank. In the April 2026 run, 0 DOE CE projects cleared the gate despite 436 inference batches. Lower to 0.60–0.65.



Of 17,943 unknowns: - 16,963 (94.5%) are CEs - 14,193 (79.1%) are DOE - 13,324 are unresolved_after_tier4 (provisional fallthrough, all had a rule fire) - 4,619 are T4_local_uncertain (Tier 4 processed but all three gates failed)

Why a tiered pipeline instead of just LLM? Agency metadata alone resolves ~60% of projects deterministically and cheaply. Running LLM on all 20K projects would cost ~$20–40 at Haiku pricing and introduce hallucination risk for cases trivially answered by agency type. The tiered approach reserves LLM for genuine ambiguity (target: <250 projects).
Why SetFit for DOE CE classification? DOE CEs are the largest ambiguous class (~14K projects). A fine-tuned SetFit model provides fast batched inference on MPS and requires only a modest labeled example bank. DeBERTa fine-tuning would overfit on the available training set. SetFit is appropriate for data scarcity (few labeled examples per class, not label quality issues).
Why NLI (cross-encoder) for Tier 4? The Tier 4 adjudication task is better framed as textual entailment than classification: given a retrieved passage, does it entail the hypothesis “this project is triggered by federal land use”? Cross-encoders compute a joint representation of (passage, hypothesis) and produce calibrated entailment scores. This is a data scarcity problem where expressing classes as natural language hypotheses avoids the need for labeled training data.
Multi-label consideration: Many projects are triggered by multiple nexus factors simultaneously (e.g., federal land AND DOE funding). Primary trigger is priority-resolved for all figures; secondary triggers are stored separately.
Funding detail layer: Funding mechanism and amount extraction is deliberately downstream of trigger classification. Grant/loan/amount parsing is restricted to federal_funding primary projects, suppresses land-authorization grant phrases such as right-of-way grants, and requires project-specific funding context before extracting dollar amounts. Amount coverage is expected to be partial; conflicting candidate amounts are preserved in JSON and flagged for manual review.

title: D1: NEPA Triggered — Architecture
text:
Why a tiered pipeline instead of just LLM? Agency metadata alone resolves ~60% of projects deterministically and cheaply. Running LLM on all 20K projects would cost ~$20–40 at Haiku pricing and introduce hallucination risk for cases trivially answered by agency type. The tiered approach reserves LLM for genuine ambiguity (target: <250 projects).
Why SetFit for DOE CE classification? DOE CEs are the largest ambiguous class (~14K projects). A fine-tuned SetFit model provides fast batched inference on MPS and requires only a modest labeled example bank. DeBERTa fine-tuning would overfit on the available training set. SetFit is appropriate for data scarcity (few labeled examples per class, not label quality issues).
Why NLI (cross-encoder) for Tier 4? The Tier 4 adjudication task is better framed as textual entailment than classification: given a retrieved passage, does it entail the hypothesis “this project is triggered by federal land use”? Cross-encoders compute a joint representation of (passage, hypothesis) and produce calibrated entailment scores. This is a data scarcity problem where expressing classes as natural language hypotheses avoids the need for labeled training data.
Multi-label consideration: Many projects are triggered by multiple nexus factors simultaneously (e.g., federal land AND DOE funding). Primary trigger is priority-resolved for all figures; secondary triggers are stored separately.
Funding detail layer: Funding mechanism and amount extraction is deliberately downstream of trigger classification. Grant/loan/amount parsing is restricted to federal_funding primary projects, suppresses land-authorization grant phrases such as right-of-way grants, and requires project-specific funding context before extracting dollar amounts. Amount coverage is expected to be partial; conflicting candidate amounts are preserved in JSON and flagged for manual review.

title: extract_data.py — Pipeline Architecture
text:
Script: phase2/code/extract/extract_data.py
Purpose: Main entry point for the Phase 2 data pipeline. Downloads raw NEPATEC data, builds analysis-ready parquet files, and merges enrichment artifacts (Federal Register NOI, timeline data). Every downstream deliverable script starts from projects_combined.parquet produced here.



flowchart TD
    A[NEPATEC HuggingFace dataset] -->|--mode extract| B[phase2/data/processed/\nea/ eis/ ce/ parquets]
    B -->|--mode analysis| C[run_raw_extraction\nenrich_project_descriptions]
    C --> D[create_combined_projects]

Manual filter flags







Clean energy projects are identified from NEPATEC metadata (project type, sponsor, title keywords). Two classification levels:

project_energy_type = "Clean" — broad filter, includes borderline cases flagged by project_energy_type_questions
project_energy_type_strict = "Clean" — tighter; used for conservative analysis cuts

Military/nuclear waste exclusions are applied via curated ID lists in data/analysis/exclusions/. Projects reclassified to "Other" retain the project_military_to_exclude or project_nuclear_waste_to_exclude flag for auditability.
Note: The current Phase 2 analysis uses n_clean = 20,725 projects where project_energy_type == "Clean".




The Federal Register enrichment is intentionally opt-in at refresh time:
Default (offline):
  → merges data/analysis/federal_register/federal_register.parquet if present
  → if does not exist, projects get null NOI/NOA fields (not an error)

With --refresh-federal-register:
  → calls federal_register.py refresh_federal_register_noi()
  → runs NEPATEC page scan (DuckDB) + targeted FR API fetches
  → rewrites federal_register.parquet, then merges
This keeps normal analysis runs fast and deterministic. See federal_register.md for NOI/NOA matching architecture and runbooks/federal_register.md for refresh commands.




# Default: build analysis parquets offline
conda run -n nepa python phase2/code/extract/extract_data.py --mode analysis

# Build + refresh Federal Register NOI (network required)
conda run -n nepa python phase2/code/extract/extract_data.py --mode analysis --refresh-federal-register

# Download raw data from HuggingFace (first-time setup)
conda run -n nepa python phase2/code/extract/extract_data.py --mode extract

# Full rebuild from scratch
conda run -n nepa python phase2/code/extract/extract_data.py --mode all











File
Description




data/analysis/processes_combined.parquet
One row per NEPA process (process_type, lead_agency, dates)


data/analysis/documents_combined.parquet
One row per NEPA document with classification flags







Why DuckDB for page scanning? The full NEPATEC corpus is ~6M+ pages across EA/EIS/CE parquets — too large to load into pandas. All page-level operations (FR doc number scan, regex extraction, section detection) use DuckDB read_parquet() with predicate pushdown.
Why is FR refresh opt-in? The NEPATEC page scan takes 30–60 seconds, and the FR API calls add network latency. Analysis runs that don’t need updated NOI dates should remain fast and reproducible without external dependencies.
Why no timeline merge here? Timeline data (timeline_*.parquet) is merged at the deliverable level rather than baked into projects_combined.parquet. This keeps the base dataset stable across different timeline pipeline iterations and lets deliverables choose which timeline artifact to use.

title: Regulatory Page Count Extraction
text:
Purpose: Estimate FRA-compliant page counts for clean energy EA and EIS final documents. Input: data/analysis/projects_combined.parquet + page-level text. Output: data/analysis/projects_page_counts.parquet Cost: Free (no LLM calls). Prerequisites: Base dataset built (runbook 01).



python code/extract/extract_pages.py --run
Re-run whenever projects_combined.parquet is updated with new projects.





The FRA defines a “page” as 500 words, excluding maps, figures, and appendices (40 C.F.R. § 1508.1(bb)).
Script computes regulatory_pages = CEIL(body_word_count / 500) by detecting embedded appendix sections and excluding low-content pages.
Output is joined into the Deliverable 5 R pipeline by code/deliverable05/00_setup.R.

title: NEPA
text:
Refactor Architecture
Add a ProcessConfig object and make pipeline behavior config-driven. Fields: process_type, doc_priority, doc_include, doc_exclude, cue_patterns, guardrails, final_date_rules, confidence_rules. Create three configs: CE_CONFIG, EA_CONFIG, EIS_CONFIG. Keep one shared execution flow; switch behavior by config only. Split extract_timeline.py into logical modules (can stay in one file initially, then move). timeline_config.py: process configs and cue libraries. timeline_documents.py: doc filtering and section-level inclusion/exclusion. timeline_candidates.py: regex date extraction + context windows. timeline_classifier.py: BERT inference wrapper + label mapping. timeline_rules.py: guardrails and post-classification normalization. timeline_finalize.py: exactly-two-date resolver. timeline_runner.py: orchestration and CLI entrypoints. Add a clear orchestrator API. run_timeline(process_types=[“CE”], energy_type=“Clean”, sample_size=None, output_file=None) Loop per process_type, load config, run same stages, append outputs. Persist one row per project with required outputs: initiation_date_final decision_date_final initiation_confidence decision_confidence initiation_provenance decision_provenance process_type timeline_status (complete, missing_initiation, missing_decision, ambiguous) Parameterization by Process Type
Document policy by process. CE: current approach remains. EA: prioritize FONSI, Decision Notice/Memo, final EA, then draft EA. EIS: prioritize ROD, final EIS, NOI/scoping notices, then draft EIS. Cue library by process. Shared labels stay: initiation, review, decision, other, plus optional expiration, historical. CE cues stay mostly unchanged. EA cues add stronger FONSI/EA-specific terms. EIS cues add stronger NOI/ROD/NOA/publication language. Final-date rules by process. CE: current signature-centric decision logic. EA: prefer FONSI/Decision Notice date over general signatures. EIS: prefer ROD date over FEIS publication date; initiation prefers NOI/scoping publication. Run Strategy Recommendation
Implement and validate EA first, then EIS (separate passes). Reason: easier debugging, clearer error attribution, smaller domain shift per pass. EA and EIS have different dominant decision artifacts (FONSI vs ROD). After both are stable, run EA+EIS together using per-process configs. Keep separate metrics by process in the same run. Do not mix CE in early stabilization runs. Bring CE back only after EA/EIS error rates converge. Final production mode: process_types=[“CE”,“EA”,“EIS”] with per-type configs and per-type evaluation report. EA/EIS Document Filtering
Prioritize these document types. EA decision: FONSI, Decision Notice, Decision Memo, signed approval pages. EIS decision: ROD. Initiation: NOI, scoping notices, early notice/publication docs. Secondary: final EA/FEIS if no explicit decision doc date exists. Exclude or de-prioritize. Appendices, technical appendices, references/bibliography-heavy sections, maps/figures tables of data. Generic cover pages unless they contain explicit decision/initiation cues. Boilerplate form metadata not tied to project action milestones. Section-level heuristics. Upweight pages containing headers like Record of Decision, Finding of No Significant Impact, Notice of Intent, Decision Notice. Downweight pages with citation-heavy patterns and form-template boilerplate. Cue Library Additions for EA/EIS
Initiation cues to add. notice of intent, noi, published in the federal register, scoping period, scoping meeting, notice of availability (for early stage context). Decision cues to add. EA: finding of no significant impact, fonsi, decision notice, decision memorandum. EIS: record of decision, rod signed, selected alternative, agency decision. Review/intermediate cues to keep distinct. draft eis, draft ea, public comment, comment period, final eis filed, response to comments. Keep these from being promoted to decision unless strong decision cues are present. Exactly-Two-Date Normalization Rules
Candidate ranking. Build scored candidate lists separately for initiation and decision. Score components: cue strength, doc-type priority, signer-title strength, context quality, temporal plausibility. Initiation resolution. Prefer earliest strong initiation from NOI/scoping/application cues. If missing, allow explicit fallback to earliest strong review with initiation_imputed=True. Decision resolution. Prefer strongest doc-specific decision cue (ROD/FONSI/Decision Notice) over generic signatures. Use latest only among high-strength decision candidates, not across all candidates. Confidence and provenance. Confidence tiers: high, medium, low from score thresholds. Provenance payload should include: doc_type, document_id, page_number, matched_text, cue_type, rule_path. Modeling Strategy (EA/EIS sample size constraints)
Risks. Overfitting due to small labeled EA/EIS sets. Class imbalance (initiation typically sparse). Domain shift from CE wording and structure. Recommended training approach. Phase 1: train a shared base classifier on CE+EA+EIS with strict balanced sampling across process and label. Phase 2: process-specific calibration layer via rules and thresholds per config. Optional Phase 3: light fine-tuning heads for EA and EIS only if shared model underperforms. Prevent CE domination. Per-batch stratified sampling by process_type and label. Class weights for initiation. Cap CE examples per epoch to near EA+EIS combined count. Validate by process-specific metrics, not only aggregate metrics. Evaluation Plan
Build a gold set. EA: 100-150 projects. EIS: 100-150 projects. Double-annotate a subset for agreement. Metrics. Date-level precision/recall for initiation and decision separately. Exact-match and tolerance-window match (±7 and ±30 days). Completion rate for exactly-two-date outputs. Temporal sanity checks: initiation <= decision, and duration distribution review. Error analysis loop. Slice errors by process, doc type, agency, cue path, and fallback mode. Track top failure patterns and map each to either cue updates or guardrail updates. Promotion gates. Do not merge EA/EIS into all-process run until each process clears target thresholds on gold set and sanity checks. No repository changes were made.

title: Timeline Extraction Status (Prompt-Ready)
text:
Last updated: 2026-02-18
Source of truth: code/extract/extract_timeline.py
Use this file as the canonical, up-to-date context for timeline extraction. If older notes conflict, trust the code and this document.



Sources supported in current run: CE, EA, EIS via --source.
Canonical workflow: --regex-prep -> --bert-run -> --llm-adjudicate.
--regex-prep writes per-source caches: regex_candidates_ce/ea/eis.parquet.
--bert-run is clean-energy only in CLI dispatch (clean_energy_only=True).
EIS gap rule is OFF; CE/EA gap rule is ON (730 days).
EA/EIS can use non-main-doc fallback when no main docs exist; flag is main_document_imputed.
LLM adjudication reads BERT candidates (bert_dates_json) only; no new date discovery.
Decision modes: priority_only, ea_eis_fallback, no_decision_candidates.
Guardrail strictness applies only to priority_only.
Adjudication caps: default 50/300; EIS 30/200 (max candidates/context chars).
Claude provider forces workers=1; currently retries 429 only (not 529/5xx).
Default adjudication output naming: <input_stem>_llm.parquet.




This pipeline extracts NEPA timeline dates from document text for clean-energy projects across: - CE - EA - EIS
Primary workflow is: 1. Regex candidate extraction (--regex-prep) 2. BERT date classification + timeline assembly (--bert-run) 3. Optional LLM post-adjudication (--llm-adjudicate)





Command entrypoint: --regex-prep
Function: run_regex_prep()
Key behavior: - Parses source(s) from --source (CE, EA, EIS, comma-separated). - Filters to clean energy in CLI dispatch (clean_energy_only=True). - Saves per-source cache by default: - data/analysis/regex_candidates_ce.parquet - data/analysis/regex_candidates_ea.parquet - data/analysis/regex_candidates_eis.parquet - Uses document_type_clean when available, else document_type. - Candidate rows include: - project_id, date, match, context, position, position_pct, doc_type, main_document_imputed, run_timestamp
Main-document logic: - CE: main-doc-only behavior enforced. - EA/EIS: main-doc-first; if a project has no main docs, falls back to non-main docs sorted by source-specific doc priority; those rows set main_document_imputed=True.



Command entrypoint: --bert-run
Function: run_bert_timeline_extraction()
Key behavior: - Filters project universe by dataset_source in --source. - Filters to clean energy in CLI dispatch (clean_energy_only=True). - Requires per-source regex caches (CE legacy fallback to regex_candidates.parquet is kept). - Applies per-source gap rule config: - CE: gap rule on (730 days) - EA: gap rule on (730 days) - EIS: gap rule off - Adds NOI fallback for initiation when no initiation date exists. - Carries filename-derived metadata bounds: - project_date_earliest_file_name - project_date_latest_file_name - project_file_name_dates - Carries main_document_imputed into project-level output.
Timeline status values: - complete - missing_initiation - missing_decision - no_dates
Default output: - data/analysis/projects_timeline_bert.parquet - or custom via --output.



Command entrypoint: --llm-adjudicate --input <bert_output.parquet>
Function: run_llm_adjudication()
What it does: - Reads BERT output parquet (bert_dates_json per project). - Filters candidate dates (_filter_candidates_for_llm). - Prompts LLM to pick one initiation and one decision date. - Writes LLM picks plus diagnostics back to parquet.
Providers: - --provider ollama - --provider claude (default model for Claude provider: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001)
Claude-specific behavior: - Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY env var. - Forces workers=1. - Retries 429 only (does not currently retry 529 overload or other 5xx).
Decision modes in adjudication: - priority_only (Tier A docs present: FONSI/ROD/DR/Decision Record) - ea_eis_fallback (Tier A absent, vetted fallback decision candidates) - no_decision_candidates
Guardrail: - Hard post-parse guardrail is only enforced for priority_only.
Cap/context limits: - Default (non-EIS): max_candidates=50, context_chars=300 - EIS: max_candidates=30, context_chars=200
Default output naming: - <input_stem>_llm.parquet in same folder unless --output is provided.






Command: --bert-generate
Function: generate_bert_training_data()
Behavior: - Auto-discovers available regex caches across CE/EA/EIS. - Falls back to legacy CE cache only if needed. - Auto-labels contexts via weak supervision. - Applies manual corrections if data/analysis/manual_training_corrections.csv exists. - Oversamples EA and EIS by 3x to reduce CE dominance. - Output: data/analysis/bert_training_data.parquet.



Command: --bert-train
Function: train_bert_classifier()
Behavior: - Trains classifier from bert_training_data.parquet. - Saves model to models/timeline_classifier/.






python code/extract/extract_timeline.py --regex-prep --source CE
python code/extract/extract_timeline.py --regex-prep --source EA
python code/extract/extract_timeline.py --regex-prep --source EIS

python code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-run --source CE,EA,EIS --output projects_timeline_bert_all.parquet

python code/extract/extract_timeline.py --llm-adjudicate --input projects_timeline_bert_all.parquet --provider claude --output projects_timeline_bert_all_llm.parquet



python code/extract/extract_timeline.py --regex-prep --source EA
python code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-run --source EA --output projects_timeline_bert_ea.parquet
python code/extract/extract_timeline.py --llm-adjudicate --input projects_timeline_bert_ea.parquet --provider claude



python code/extract/extract_timeline.py --regex-prep --source EIS
python code/extract/extract_timeline.py --bert-run --source EIS --output projects_timeline_bert_eis.parquet
python code/extract/extract_timeline.py --llm-adjudicate --input projects_timeline_bert_eis.parquet --provider claude





--llm-adjudicate can only choose among BERT-provided candidates (bert_dates_json). It cannot recover dates never extracted upstream.
EIS adjudication can still fail with claude_api_error (529): Overloaded; current code retries 429 only.
--llm-run path is legacy CE-oriented full-document/hybrid LLM flow; current EA/EIS production path should use --llm-adjudicate.
If you pass one shared --regex-cache filename while processing multiple sources in one --regex-prep call, later sources can overwrite earlier output. Prefer default per-source cache names.




When editing timeline tasks: 1. Assume this file and code/extract/extract_timeline.py are authoritative. 2. Use the regex -> BERT -> LLM-adjudicate mental model. 3. Preserve per-source behavior differences (especially EIS gap-rule off and EIS adjudication limits 30/200). 4. Do not infer behavior from older notes unless verified in code. 5. When proposing edits, state which stage is impacted: regex cache, BERT classification, or LLM adjudication.
