title: D1: NEPA Trigger Classification
text: This is an explanation of the trigger definitions we want to use for this deliverable.

title: D1: NEPA Trigger Classification
text:
Classification Schema
Each of these 6 classes triggers NEPA review. The main trigger classes are:

Federal Funding
Federal Land
Federal Permit
Federal Direct Action
Federal Program
Federal Property Transaction


1. Federal funding

Coding rule: Assign federal funding classification when the project receives direct or indirect federal financial support or when federal financial support is the reason the agency is involved in project approval or review.
Grants and direct funding:

“federal grant” / “DOE grant” / “DOT grant” / “HUD grant” / “USDA grant” / “grant funding”
“federal funding” / “federal financial assistance”
“DOE grant” / “DOE funding” / “DOT grant” / “DOT funding” / “HUD grant” / “HUD funding” / “USDA grant” / “USDA funding” (Tier 1b agency+type pattern)
“provide federal funding”
“DOE Funding” (standalone; Tier 4 context scan)
“DOE/Department of Energy” + “would provide” + “funds/funding/grant/awards/cost-share” (within same passage)
“total award value”
“Total Project Value”

Loans and loan guarantees:

“loan guarantee”
“Title XVII”

Cooperative agreements:

“through a cooperative agreement … partially fund” (within same passage)
“providing financial assistance to … under/through a cooperative agreement” (within same passage)
“awarding a grant … partially fund” (within same passage)

Cost sharing:

“cost share”
“DOE Funding = $[amount] … Cost Share = $[amount]” (Tier 1b; requires actual dollar figures)
“cost-shared arrangement”
“DOE’s (proposed) action is to provide … cost-shared arrangement” (within same passage; Tier 1b only)
“Federal Cost Share” + “Total Project Value” within same passage (Tier 1b)
“Federal Cost Share” standalone (Tier 4 context scan — lower specificity)

Legislative funding authorities:

“Inflation Reduction Act”
“Bipartisan Infrastructure Law” / “Bipartisan Infrastructure Act”
“Title XVII”

Formula-based programs:

“formula awards” / “formula-based awards” / “formula grants” / “formula-based grants”
“EECBG funding” / “DOE EECBG funding”
“State Energy Program” / “SEP” / “WAP” + “formula awards/grants” within same passage
“Administrative and Legal Requirements Document” / “ALRD” + “formula awards/grants” within same passage (medium confidence)

Document title (Tier 2 scan):

“loan guarantee” appearing in the document title

Agency metadata (Tier 1a — detected without text cues):

Agency is DOT / Department of Transportation → auto-assigned federal_funding
Agency is HUD / Department of Housing and Urban Development → auto-assigned federal_funding
Agency is FTA / Federal Transit Administration → auto-assigned federal_funding
Agency is FHWA / Federal Highway Administration → auto-assigned federal_funding
Note: DOE is ambiguous — it can indicate either federal_funding or federal_direct_action depending on verb context; DOE projects are routed to Tier 4 for adjudication



2. Federal land

Coding rule: Assign federal land classification when the project is located on, crosses, uses, or requires access to federally managed land or federally controlled property interests or when the project arises from federal land ownership, land management authority, easement authority, or right-of-way control.
ROW applications and grants on BLM / public land:

“application for a right-of-way grant”
“30-year right-of-way grant” + “BLM-administered lands” (within same passage)
“right-of-way (ROW)” + “public land administered by the Bureau of Land Management” (within same passage)
“request for a right-of-way” + “public land managed by BLM” (within same passage)
“public lands managed by the Bureau of Land Management”
“grant a perpetual ROW on BLM managed public land”
“perpetual right-of-way grant”
“rights-of-way over, upon, under, or through public lands”

ROW renewals and amendments:

“right-of-way renewal applications”
“right-of-way renewal and amendment”
“Request to Amend Existing Authorization”
“amend its ROW grant”

Special use permits:

“special use permit”
“current authorization with a defined ROW” + “Operation and Maintenance Plan” (either order, within same passage)

Easements:

“temporary and permanent easements”
“easement has expired”
“easement for the right-of-way” (Tier 1b; exact phrase)
“easement” + “right-of-way” within same passage (~120 chars) (Tier 4; broader proximity match)

Bureau of Indian Affairs:

“Bureau of Indian Affairs is requesting a new right-of-way (ROW)”

Bureau of Reclamation:

“lands administered by the Bureau of Reclamation” + “permissions must be sought” (within same passage)
“2920 Land Use Authorization”

FLPMA statutory authority:

“Title V of the Federal Land Policy and Management Act” + “respond to requests for rights-of-way across public lands” (within same passage)

Document title (Tier 2 scan):

“right-of-way” (any hyphen/spacing variant) appearing in the document title

Agency metadata (Tier 1a — detected without text cues):

Agency is BLM, Bureau of Land Management, USFS, Forest Service, NPS, National Park Service, FWS / USFWS, Fish and Wildlife Service, BOR / USBR, Bureau of Reclamation
Agency is BLM / Bureau of Land Management AND sponsor contains Forest Service / USFS AND title or description contains one of: “right-of-way” / “ROW” / “withdrawal” / “Public Land Order” / “FLPMA” → auto-assigned federal_land (T1a_BLM_USFS_land_control)



3. Federal permit

Coding rule: Assign federal permit classification when the  project needs a federal permit, license, certification, or approval--even if it is otherwise private or state-led--and the action is primarily a regulatory authorization, license, permit, or approval.
Army Corps / Section 404 permits:

“Department of the Army Environmental Assessment and Statement of Finding/Findings” + “(Standard) Individual Permit Application” within same passage (Tier 1b only)
“Standard Individual Permit Application” / “Individual Permit Application”
“Section 404 permit application”
“applied for an individual permit under Section 404”
“Department of Army permit” / “Department of the Army (DA) permit” + “Section 404” within same passage (180 chars)
“Clean Water Act” only when paired in the same passage with explicit permit language such as “Section 404” + “permit” / “permit application,” “permit application,” “issue a permit” / “issue a permit with conditions,” “deny a permit,” or “Section 10”
Do not use bare “Clean Water Act” by itself as a permit trigger
“Section 10” + “Rivers and Harbors” within same passage (80 chars)
“Nationwide Permit (NWP) Verification” (medium confidence)
“Nationwide, Regional General, or Standard Individual Permit may be required” (medium confidence)

NPDES:

“issuance of a National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System permit” (Tier 1b; without NPDES acronym)
“National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permit” (Tier 1b + Tier 4; with NPDES acronym)
“National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Construction Storm Water General Permit is required” (full phrase, Tier 1b)
“NPDES permit must be obtained”
“NPDES” + “permitting decision” within same passage (80 chars)
“Construction Storm Water General Permit is required”

Incidental take / ESA:

“incidental take permit application”
“Incidental Take Permit (ITP) under Section 10(a)(1)(B)”
“Renewed/Amended ITP is needed”
“Habitat Conservation Plan and Incidental Take Permit”

FERC:

“hydropower license”
“relicense” / “relicensing” (medium confidence)
“application for a certificate of public convenience and necessity”

Presidential permits:

“Amendment to Presidential Permit”
“(Amendment to) Presidential Permit” (Tier 4 broader form; covers both standalone and amendment)
“Issuance of Presidential Permit PP-[number]”
“Presidential Permit Application Review” (Tier 1b only)

NRC nuclear licenses:

“Early Site Permit”
“Combined License”
“License Renewal” / “Subsequent License Renewal”
“issuance of renewed facility operating licenses”
“NRC/FERC” + “license amendment” within same passage (80 chars) — OR — “license amendment” + “NRC/FERC/10 CFR 50.90/FERC order” within same passage (Tier 4 only)

Document title (Tier 2 scan):

“(Standard) Individual Permit Application”
“Hydropower License”
“Incidental Take Permit”
“Presidential Permit”
“Early Site Permit”
“Combined License”
“(Subsequent) License Renewal”
“certificate of public convenience and necessity”

Agency metadata (Tier 1a — detected without text cues):

Agency is FERC / Federal Energy Regulatory Commission → auto-assigned federal_permit
Agency is FAA / Federal Aviation Administration → auto-assigned federal_permit
Agency is FCC / Federal Communications Commission → auto-assigned federal_permit



4. Federal Direct Action

Coding rule: Assign federal direct action coding when the federal agency is not just approving someone else’s project but is the primary actor proposing, implementing, constructing, adopting, managing, or directly sponsoring the action.
Recognized federal actors — the following agency names are required to appear in any compound pattern below:

DOE / Department of Energy
NNSA / National Nuclear Security Administration
BPA / Bonneville / Bonneville Power Administration
WAPA / Western / Western Area Power Administration
Reclamation / Bureau of Reclamation / USBR
CBP / U.S. Customs and Border Protection
Forest Service / U.S. Forest Service / USFS
Bureau of Land Management / BLM
NPS / National Park Service
PNNL / Pacific Northwest National Laboratory

Compound patterns (actor + intent verb + action verb — all must appear in same passage):
Intent verbs recognized: “proposes to” / “propose to” / “is proposing to” / “will” / “would” / “would be to” / “is to”
Action verbs recognized: construct, install, build, operate, implement, manage, restore, undertake, develop, upgrade, expand, demolish, replace, retrofit, rebuild, reconductor, renovate, refurbish, relocate, repair, reconfigure, dismantle, modernize, improve
The compound patterns are:

[ACTOR] + (within 80 chars) + [INTENT VERB] + [ACTION VERB]
[ACTOR] + (within 80 chars) + [INTENT VERB] + “remove and replace”
[ACTOR] + (within 120 chars) + “construct, own, operate, and maintain”
[ACTOR] + (within 160 chars) + “constructed and operated” / “would be constructed and operated”
[ACTOR] + (within 160 chars) + “continue to occupy and maintain existing facilities” + (within 180 chars) + “refurbish existing facilities”
[ACTOR] + (within 160 chars) + “would functionally replace”
[ACTOR] + (within 520 chars) + “rebuild the existing”
[ACTOR] + (within 200 chars) + “upgrade/rebuild” + (within 160 chars) + “by removing” + (within 160 chars) + “and installing”

Specific literal pattern (no verb structure required):

“now that DOE has acquired ownership of the parcel, DOE proposes to operate and maintain the site”

Specific literal pattern (no verb structure required):

“now that DOE has acquired ownership of the parcel, DOE proposes to operate and maintain the site”

Standalone patterns (no actor name required):

“federal construction” / “federal facility” / “federal installation”
“military installation” / “military base” / “military facility” / “military construction”
“federal facility upgrade” / “federal facility expansion” / “federal facility construction” (Tier 1b; more specific form)
“vegetation management” + “National Forest” within same passage (~50 chars) (Tier 1b only)

Agency metadata (Tier 1a — detected without text cues):

AGENCY_DIRECT_ACTION_MAP — auto-assigned federal_direct_action without further review:

Power Marketing Administration
Bonneville Power Administration / BPA
Western Area Power Administration / WAPA
CBP / U.S. Customs and Border Protection

Note: DOE and USACE appear in FEDERAL_ACTION_ACTOR_PATTERN (used in compound text patterns above) but are classified as AGENCY_AMBIGUOUS in Tier 1a — they are NOT auto-assigned to federal_direct_action from metadata alone; verb context from document text is required to distinguish federal_direct_action from federal_funding (DOE) or federal_permit (USACE)



5. Federal programs

Coding rule: Assign the federal program classification when the NEPA action is not primarily a site-specific project, but a broader plan, rule, policy, or program rather than a single facility or construction project.
Programmatic document identifiers (full phrases):

“programmatic environmental impact statement”
“programmatic environmental assessment”
“Draft Programmatic Environmental Impact Statement” / “Final Programmatic Environmental Impact Statement” / “Supplemental Programmatic Environmental Impact Statement”
“this programmatic EIS” / “this programmatic EA” / “this programmatic Environmental…”

Programmatic acronyms and abbreviations:

“PEIS” / “DPEIS” / “FPEIS” / “SPEIS”
“PEA” (programmatic environmental assessment)
“SWEIS” (site-wide environmental impact statement)
“SWEA” (site-wide environmental assessment)
“program-wide” / “programwide”

Generic and tiered review types:

“generic environmental impact statement” / “generic environmental assessment” / “generic EIS” / “generic EA”
“Tier 1 review” / “Tier 1 NEPA review” / “Tier 1 environmental impact statement” / “Tier 1 EIS” / “Tier 1 EA” / “Tier i review” / “Tier one review”
“Environmental Impact Statement Tier 1” / “EIS Tier 1” / “EA Tier 1” (reversed order)
“site-wide environmental impact statement” / “site-wide environmental assessment” / “sitewide environmental assessment”

Resource and land management plans:

“resource management plan amendment” / “resource management plan revision”
“resource management plan” (standalone, in title or description)
“revision of the … land and resource management plan” (within same passage)
“final … land and resource management plan” / “proposed … land and resource management plan” (medium confidence)

Other program types:

“leasing program” / “leasing framework”
“corridor designation”
“rulemaking”
“policy framework”

Named federal energy programs (compound patterns — both terms must appear in same passage):

“integrated resource plan” + “programmatic environmental impact statement” / “supplemental environmental impact statement” / “draft EIS”
“integrated vegetation management program” + “programmatic environmental assessment”
“system-wide operations and maintenance” + “programmatic environmental assessment”
“uranium leasing program” + “programmatic environmental assessment”
“outer continental shelf oil and gas leasing program” + “programmatic environmental impact statement”
“solar energy development in six southwestern states” + “programmatic environmental impact statement”
“wind energy development on Bureau of Land Management-administered lands” + “programmatic environmental impact statement”
“updates to the western solar plan” + “solar PEIS” / “programmatic environmental impact statement” — OR — “2023 draft solar PEIS”
“designation of energy corridors on federal land” + “programmatic environmental impact statement”
“section 368 energy corridor revisions” + “resource management plan amendment” / “environmental impact statement”
“long-term experimental and management plan” + “environmental impact statement”

Document title (Tier 2 scan):

“programmatic” / “program-wide” / “PEIS” / “PEA” appearing in the document title (with exclusion check applied)

Excluded patterns:

“programmatic agreement” → refers to a Section 106 consultation agreement, not a NEPA program review
“programmatic biological opinion” → a Fish and Wildlife consultation document, not a NEPA program review
“programmatic consultation” → inter-agency coordination, not NEPA
“programmatic collaboration” → not NEPA



6. Federal property transaction

Coding rule: Assign federal property transaction coding when the federal action involves transfer or disposition of federally controlled land or property interests.
Land exchange:

“land exchange”
“fee-for-fee land exchange”
“exchange property with”
“asset exchange” + “rights-of-way/easements/line easements” within same passage (medium confidence)
“easement exchange” (document title only)

Disposal:

“dispose of land rights” / “dispose of the underlying land rights”
“land disposal”
“disposal of federal land” / “disposal of federal property” (Tier 1b: requires “of federal” qualifier)
“disposal” standalone (Tier 4 context scan — lower specificity)

Sale:

“sale of land rights”
“sell in fee”

Conveyance:

“conveyance of federal land” / “conveyance of federal property” (Tier 1b: requires “of federal” qualifier)
“conveyance” standalone (Tier 4 context scan — lower specificity)

Acquisition of land or easements:

“acquire land rights”
“acquire several road easements”
“acquire access road rights”
“acquire and release access road rights”
“purchase lots and easements” / “purchase two lots and easements” / “purchase lots and line easements”
“land purchase and easement acquisition” (document title only)
“land rights acquisition” (document title only)

Transfer of ownership or title:

“transfer ownership” + “easements/rights-of-way/associated easements/land rights” within same passage
“title transfer” + “easements/rights-of-way/land rights” within same passage
“title transfer” (document title — standalone)
“parcel transfer” (medium confidence)
“property transfer” near “transmission line” or “substation” in document title (contextual; document title only)

Document title (Tier 2 scan):

“land exchange”
“land disposal”
“sale of land rights”
“land purchase and easement acquisition”
“land rights acquisition”
“easement exchange”
“title transfer”
“transmission line … property transfer” / “substation … property transfer” (within ~40 characters in title)

Excluded patterns:

“acquired the property as part of … land exchange” — past acquisition context, not the current action
“completed a NEPA review of the land exchange” — historical reference to a prior review
“no transfer of land ownership” — explicitly negates a transfer
“only change would be in ownership of assets” — asset change without land conveyance
“land exchanges, withdrawals, and the implementation of RMP” — background policy mention in an RMP review
“disposal of land parcels” / “disposals of land parcels” — generic land management language, not a discrete transaction
“land exchange could lower/allow/play a role/be considered” — conditional future reference, not a proposed action
“land exchanges are considered on a case-by-case basis” — policy description, not a specific proposed action



7. Unknown or unclear

Coding rule: Assign the unknown classification only after attempting structured extraction from title, description, process metadata, agencies, and document text and the available materials do not allow reliable identification of the triggering nexus.

title: D1: NEPA Trigger Classification
text:
Class Hypotheses
These are the class-specific hypothesis statements used in Tier 4 to determine whether a document belongs to a class.

federal_funding

This text shows that a federal agency is funding, financing, or providing financial assistance for this project, including through a grant, loan, loan guarantee, cost-sharing arrangement, cooperative agreement, or formula-based award.

federal_direct_action

This text shows that a federal agency is the primary actor directly proposing, constructing, installing, operating, managing, upgrading, rebuilding, restoring, or otherwise implementing this project, rather than merely approving or permitting someone else’s project.

federal_land

This text shows that this project is located on, crosses, or requires access to federally managed land, or that the project requires a right-of-way grant, easement, special use permit, land use authorization, or similar approval tied to use of federal land.

federal_permit

This text shows that a federal permit, license, certification, or regulatory approval is required for this project, even if the project is otherwise privately or state-led.

federal_program

This text shows that this is a programmatic, generic, site-wide, or Tier 1 environmental review covering a class of actions or a geographic area, or a broader federal planning document such as a resource management plan revision, leasing program, corridor designation, or rulemaking.

federal_property_transaction

This text shows that this involves a federal land exchange, sale, disposal, conveyance, acquisition, or transfer of land, land rights, easements, or other real-property interests.

title: D1: NEPA Triggered — Implementation Plan
text:
Delete this file after deliverable01/ scripts are implemented.
Architecture reference: phase2/architecture/deliverable01.md Classification scheme reference: phase2/code/deliverable01/nepa_trigger_classification_scheme.md



Hard filter: 20,725 clean energy projects only. All DuckDB queries and dataframe loads must apply WHERE project_energy_type = 'Clean' from the first step. Do not process or output results for non-clean projects. Document this as a constant at the top of the extraction script.




Seven classes per nepa_trigger_classification_scheme.md. The old 3-class scheme (federal_land, federal_funding, federal_permit) is replaced entirely.







Code
Description




federal_action
Federal agency is the primary actor/proposer (not just authorizing a private applicant)


federal_program
Programmatic EIS, land-use plan revision, rulemaking, leasing framework


federal_property_transaction
Land exchange, disposal, conveyance, acquisition


federal_land
Project on/crossing federal land; ROW grant or special use permit to a private developer


federal_permit
Federal permit, license, or authorization is the primary nexus (e.g., FERC, USACE Section 404)


federal_funding
Federal grant, loan guarantee, cost-share, or financial assistance


unknown
NEPA review confirmed but trigger cannot be reliably identified



Priority order for primary trigger assignment (use when signals conflict): 1. federal_action 2. federal_program 3. federal_property_transaction 4. federal_land 5. federal_permit 6. federal_funding 7. unknown
Primary vs. secondary trigger: The primary trigger is the main focus of all analysis and figures. Secondary triggers are stored in nepa_trigger_secondary (list) and surface only in multi-label combo analysis and on explicit request. Do not display secondary labels in primary figures.


The critical boundary: BLM/USFS/NPS as the proposing/implementing agency vs. as the authorizing agency for a private developer.
Rule: If the lead agency is the grammatical subject of action verbs (construct, install, operate, implement, manage, maintain, restore) in the title or description, assign federal_action. If the lead agency is the authorizing body for a private applicant (grant, authorize, approve, evaluate an application from, consider a ROW request by), assign federal_land.
Verb signals for federal_action (agency as actor):
FEDERAL_ACTION_VERB_PATTERNS = [
    r'\b(?:proposes?\s+to|will|would)\s+(?:construct|install|build|operate|implement|manage|restore|undertake|develop|upgrade|expand)\b',
    r'\bagency.{0,20}(?:proposes|proposes to|will construct|will install|will implement)\b',
    r'\b(?:Forest Service|Bureau of Land Management|BLM|USFS|NPS|Bureau of Reclamation)\s+(?:proposes|will|plans to)\b',
    r'\bfederal\s+(?:construction|facility|installation|project|operation)\b',
    r'\bmilitary\s+(?:installation|base|facility|construction)\b',
]
Verb signals for federal_land (agency as authorizer):
FEDERAL_LAND_AUTHORIZER_PATTERNS = [
    r'\b(?:right.of.way|ROW)\s+(?:grant|application|request)\b',
    r'\b(?:applicant|proponent|developer|company)\b',
    r'\bspecial\s+use\s+(?:permit|authorization)\b',
    r'\bwould\s+(?:authorize|approve|grant|allow)\s+(?:a|the)\b',
    r'\b(?:application|request)\s+(?:by|from)\b',
    r'\bhas\s+(?:applied|submitted)\s+(?:an application|a request)\b',
]
When both sets match, prefer federal_action (higher priority). When only authorizer verbs are present alongside federal land agencies, assign federal_land. When neither set matches, fall through to standard agency-code heuristic.



All patterns are defined inline in 01_extract_nepa_trigger.py. Do not import from extract_reviews.py.
# Scan project/document title
PROGRAMMATIC_TITLE_PATTERNS = [
    r'\bprogrammatic\b',
    r'\bprogram[\-\s]?wide\b',
    r'\bpeis\b',
    r'\bpea\b',
]

# Strong indicators in description or first 5 pages
PROGRAMMATIC_STRONG_PATTERNS = [
    r'(?:draft|final|supplemental)\s+programmatic\s+environmental\s+(?:impact\s+statement|assessment)',
    r'programmatic\s+environmental\s+(?:impact\s+statement|assessment)',
    r'\b(?:dpeis|fpeis|speis|peis|pea)\b',
    r'this\s+programmatic\s+(?:eis|ea|environmental)',
    r'resource\s+management\s+plan\s+(?:amendment|revision)',
    r'\bleasing\s+(?:program|framework)\b',
    r'\bcorridor\s+designation\b',
]

# Exclusions — these contain "programmatic" but are NOT federal_program triggers
PROGRAMMATIC_EXCLUSION_PATTERNS = [
    r'programmatic\s+agreement',
    r'programmatic\s+biological\s+opinion',
    r'programmatic\s+consultation',
    r'programmatic\s+collaboration',
]
Apply: if title matches PROGRAMMATIC_TITLE_PATTERNS AND text does NOT match PROGRAMMATIC_EXCLUSION_PATTERNS, check for PROGRAMMATIC_STRONG_PATTERNS in description or first 5 pages to confirm.
Expected frequency: <3% of clean energy projects. Handle as a distinct category but do not invest heavily in validation. Projects classified as federal_program should be noted as potentially being umbrella reviews rather than individual site projects, and may warrant separate treatment in the analysis.



After primary/secondary assignment, add a computed binary flag:
df["is_dual_nexus"] = (
    (df["nepa_trigger_primary"] == "federal_land") &
    (df["nepa_trigger_secondary"].apply(lambda x: "federal_permit" in x if isinstance(x, list) else False))
)
This captures the canonical transmission-line case (crosses federal land + requires USACE Section 404) without collapsing it into either trigger type. Use in timeline comparisons to test whether dual-nexus projects have longer review durations.













Field
Type
Notes




project_id
string
Join key


nepa_trigger_primary
string
One of the 7 classes


nepa_trigger_secondary
list[string]
Additional detected classes; empty list if none


nepa_trigger_multi
list[string]
All detected classes (union)


nepa_trigger_evidence_text
string
Full sentence containing trigger signal (not character window)


nepa_trigger_evidence_source
string
agency_metadata, title, description, doc_title, purpose_and_need, embedding, llm


nepa_trigger_confidence
string
high, medium, low


nepa_trigger_rule_id
string
Which rule or tier fired (e.g., T1a_BLM_land, T1b_row_grant, T3_section_header)


nepa_trigger_manual_review
bool
Flag for human review


is_dual_nexus
bool
federal_land + federal_permit combination


nepa_trigger_extraction_run_at
string
ISO-8601 UTC timestamp set on all rows at runtime


nepa_trigger_llm_run_at
string
ISO-8601 UTC per-row timestamp; "" if no LLM call made



Evidence text: Extract the full sentence containing the match (sentence-boundary detection on the ±500 char window around the match), not a fixed character slice. This produces quotable text for the report.

Before the extraction pipeline, run a one-time EDA query to understand description coverage:
def run_eda(conn: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection) -> None:
    """
    Print description coverage and length stats for clean energy projects.
    Informs whether Tier 1b (description keyword match) will have useful coverage.
    Run once before implementing the full pipeline; outputs to stdout.
    """
    result = conn.execute(f"""
        SELECT
            process_type,
            COUNT(*) AS n,
            SUM(CASE WHEN project_description IS NOT NULL
                      AND LENGTH(project_description) > 50 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_with_desc,
            AVG(LENGTH(project_description)) AS avg_desc_len
        FROM read_parquet('{PROJECTS_PATH}')
        WHERE {CLEAN_ENERGY_FILTER}
        GROUP BY process_type
        ORDER BY process_type
    """).fetchdf()
    print(result.to_string())






Map lead agency codes to unambiguous trigger types. Apply verb disambiguation rule to separate federal_action from federal_land for land-managing agencies.
# Pure-signal agency → trigger type mappings (no ambiguity)
AGENCY_PERMIT_MAP = {
    "FERC", "Federal Energy Regulatory Commission",
    "FAA", "Federal Aviation Administration",
    "FCC", "Federal Communications Commission",
}
AGENCY_FUNDING_MAP = {
    "DOT", "Department of Transportation",
    "HUD", "Department of Housing and Urban Development",
    "FTA", "Federal Transit Administration",
    "FHWA", "Federal Highway Administration",
}
AGENCY_LAND_MAP = {
    "BLM", "Bureau of Land Management",
    "USFS", "FS", "US Forest Service", "Forest Service",
    "NPS", "National Park Service",
    "FWS", "USFWS", "Fish and Wildlife Service",
    "BOR", "USBR", "Bureau of Reclamation",
}
# DOE and USACE require verb disambiguation — do NOT assign in Tier 1a without verb check
AGENCY_AMBIGUOUS = {"DOE", "Department of Energy", "USACE", "Army Corps of Engineers"}
For land agencies, apply verb disambiguation from the patterns above. If action verbs found → federal_action; if authorizer verbs found or no verb match → federal_land.
Rule ID format: T1a_{AGENCY_CODE}_{trigger} (e.g., T1a_BLM_land, T1a_BLM_action).




Apply to all projects not resolved at confidence = high in Tier 1a, plus ambiguous agencies. Search project title and project description fields (no document access).
Pattern categories cover all 7 classes with specificity-ranked patterns (more specific patterns rank higher; match first specific pattern, record rule_id).
Key additions beyond the old plan: - federal_property_transaction: “land exchange”, “conveyance”, “disposal of federal land”, “parcel transfer” - federal_action: agency-name + action verb phrases (see disambiguation section above) - federal_program: inline patterns below (do not import from extract_reviews.py)
Rule ID format: T1b_{pattern_slug} (e.g., T1b_row_grant, T1b_sec404, T1b_loan_guarantee).




Scan NEPA document titles for unambiguous trigger phrases before touching page text. All patterns are defined inline in 01_extract_nepa_trigger.py — no import from extract_reviews.py or any other phase script.
Additional patterns: - “Land Exchange” → federal_property_transaction - “Right-of-Way” in title → federal_land - “Permit Application” / “License Amendment” → federal_permit - “Programmatic” + exclusion filter → federal_program
Rule ID format: T2_doc_title_{slug}.




For projects unresolved at Tier 2, extract the “Purpose and Need” section from pages.parquet. Do NOT scan full 30 pages — target the specific section.
PURPOSE_AND_NEED_HEADERS = [
    r'\bpurpose\s+and\s+need\b',
    r'\bneed\s+for\s+(?:federal\s+)?action\b',
    r'\bproposed\s+(?:federal\s+)?action\b',
    r'\bproject\s+purpose\b',
    r'\bstatement\s+of\s+need\b',
]

def extract_purpose_and_need(text: str, window: int = 600) -> str:
    """
    Detect Purpose and Need section header; return up to `window` chars following it.
    Returns empty string if no header found.
    """
    for pattern in PURPOSE_AND_NEED_HEADERS:
        m = re.search(pattern, text, re.IGNORECASE)
        if m:
            snippet = text[m.start():m.start() + window]
            return snippet
    return ""
Apply keyword matching to the extracted window. Capture the full sentence containing the match as nepa_trigger_evidence_text.
Scan only pages 1–10 per document (covers all Purpose and Need sections in practice).
Rule ID format: T3_pan_{slug} (e.g., T3_pan_row_grant).




For projects with no confident match after Tier 3, score candidate evidence text (Purpose and Need snippet or Tier 1b description) against class prototype sentences using all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (already in the pipeline).
CLASS_PROTOTYPES = {

Embed all prototypes at startup. For each unresolved project, embed the candidate text, compute cosine similarity to each class centroid, assign to highest class if similarity ≥ 0.45 threshold, else unknown. Set confidence = medium for assignments above threshold, low below.
Rule ID format: T4_embed_{class}.




For projects with confidence = low after all tiers (target ≤5% of 20,725 ≈ 1,000 projects). Only runs when --use-llm flag is set.
PROMPT = """You are classifying what triggered a NEPA environmental review for an energy project.
Given the text below, identify the primary federal nexus.

Classes:
- federal_action: federal agency is the primary actor constructing or implementing the project
- federal_program: programmatic EIS, land-use plan, rulemaking, or leasing framework
- federal_property_transaction: land exchange, disposal, or conveyance
- federal_land: project on or crossing federal land; ROW grant to a private developer
- federal_permit: federal permit, license, or authorization is the primary nexus
- federal_funding: federal grant, loan guarantee, or financial assistance
- unknown: cannot determine from the text provided

Text: {text}

Respond with JSON only:
{{"primary": "federal_land", "secondary": ["federal_permit"], "confidence": "high", "reasoning": "..."}}"""
Set nepa_trigger_llm_run_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat() per row on success.
Rule ID format: T5_llm.





CEs are 1–3 page forms, not narrative NEPA documents. Do not apply the full Tier 3 Purpose and Need extraction to CEs — the entire document may be 2 pages.
For CE records: 1. Apply Tiers 1a, 1b, 2 as normal. 2. If unresolved: scan the entire CE document text (no page limit, since documents are short). 3. If CE category code is available in metadata: build a lookup table mapping CE category codes to trigger types (e.g., BLM Instruction Memo 2012-044 categories map to federal_land). This may resolve more CE cases than text scanning.
Flag CE records with process_type = 'CE' in all diagnostic outputs for separate review.




Target: ≤5% of 20,725 projects flagged for manual review (~1,000 max). If the pipeline flags more than this, tighten confidence thresholds before finalizing.
Validation by rule batch rather than individual case review:
def build_validation_batches(df: pd.DataFrame, sample_per_batch: int = 20) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Group flagged cases by nepa_trigger_rule_id. For each unique rule that
    produced low-confidence results, sample up to `sample_per_batch` cases.
    Review the sample; if precision >= 0.85, accept the full batch without
    further review. If precision < 0.85, either fix the rule or flag all
    cases from that rule for individual review.
    """
    flagged = df[df["nepa_trigger_manual_review"] == True]
    batches = []
    for rule_id, group in flagged.groupby("nepa_trigger_rule_id"):
        sample = group.sample(min(sample_per_batch, len(group)), random_state=42)
        sample["validation_batch"] = rule_id
        sample["batch_size"] = len(group)
        batches.append(sample)
    return pd.concat(batches, ignore_index=True) if batches else pd.DataFrame()
Output validation_batches.csv alongside the main parquet. Reviewer works through batches in descending order of batch_size — fixing the largest broken rule has the most impact. Once a batch is reviewed and the rule confirmed, set nepa_trigger_manual_review = False for all rows from that rule.
Pre-validation step: Before the full run, spot-check 30 random BLM projects and 30 random FERC projects from Tier 1a results. If ≥28/30 are correctly classified, Tier 1a is trustworthy and those cases do not need manual_review = True even at medium confidence.




Each tier receives only the projects not yet resolved by all prior tiers. A project is “resolved” when nepa_trigger_confidence is high or medium. Low-confidence results from an earlier tier are kept but the project is still passed to the next tier to attempt a better classification.
def extract_nepa_triggers(use_llm=False, sample=None):
    conn = duckdb.connect()

    # Load clean energy project IDs and key metadata only.
    # dataset_source ('CE', 'EA', 'EIS') routes each project to the correct
    # docs/pages parquet in Tiers 2 and 3.
    projects = conn.execute(f"""
        SELECT project_id, lead_agency_harmonized, project_title,
               project_description, process_type, dataset_source
        FROM read_parquet('{PROJECTS_PATH}')
        WHERE {CLEAN_ENERGY_FILTER}
    """).fetchdf()
    if sample:
        projects = projects.sample(sample, random_state=42)

    all_project_ids = set(projects["project_id"])
    resolved = {}  # project_id -> result dict; grows as tiers run

    # Tier 1a
    r1a = tier1a_metadata(projects)
    resolved.update({r["project_id"]: r for r in r1a if r["nepa_trigger_confidence"] in ("high", "medium")})

    # Tier 1b — only unresolved
    unresolved = projects[~projects["project_id"].isin(resolved)]
    r1b = tier1b_title_description(unresolved)
    resolved.update({r["project_id"]: r for r in r1b if r["nepa_trigger_confidence"] in ("high", "medium")})

    # Tier 2 — only unresolved
    unresolved_ids = list(all_project_ids - set(resolved))
    r2 = tier2_doc_title(unresolved_ids, conn)
    resolved.update({r["project_id"]: r for r in r2 if r["nepa_trigger_confidence"] in ("high", "medium")})

    # Tier 3 — only unresolved; CE records handled separately (full doc scan, no page limit)
    unresolved_ids = list(all_project_ids - set(resolved))
    r3 = tier3_purpose_and_need(unresolved_ids, projects, conn)
    resolved.update({r["project_id"]: r for r in r3 if r["nepa_trigger_confidence"] in ("high", "medium")})

    # Tier 4 — embedding similarity on all still-unresolved
    unresolved_ids = list(all_project_ids - set(resolved))
    r4 = tier4_embedding(unresolved_ids, projects, conn)
    resolved.update({r["project_id"]: r for r in r4})

    # Tier 5 — LLM on confidence=low residuals (if --use-llm)
    if use_llm:
        low_conf = [pid for pid, r in resolved.items() if r["nepa_trigger_confidence"] == "low"]
        r5 = tier5_llm(low_conf, projects, conn)
        resolved.update({r["project_id"]: r for r in r5})

    # Any project with no assignment at all → unknown
    for pid in all_project_ids:
        if pid not in resolved:
            resolved[pid] = {
                "project_id": pid,
                "nepa_trigger_primary": "unknown",
                "nepa_trigger_secondary": [],
                "nepa_trigger_multi": [],
                "nepa_trigger_evidence_text": "",
                "nepa_trigger_evidence_source": "",
                "nepa_trigger_confidence": "low",
                "nepa_trigger_rule_id": "no_match",
                "nepa_trigger_manual_review": True,
                "nepa_trigger_llm_run_at": "",
            }

    return pd.DataFrame(list(resolved.values()))



run_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
final = extract_nepa_triggers(use_llm=args.use_llm, sample=args.sample)

# Compute is_dual_nexus (post-assignment)
final["is_dual_nexus"] = (
    (final["nepa_trigger_primary"] == "federal_land") &
    (final["nepa_trigger_secondary"].apply(
        lambda x: "federal_permit" in x if isinstance(x, list) else False
    ))
)

final["nepa_trigger_extraction_run_at"] = run_at
# nepa_trigger_llm_run_at is set per-row in Tier 5; fill "" elsewhere
if "nepa_trigger_llm_run_at" not in final.columns:
    final["nepa_trigger_llm_run_at"] = ""
else:
    final["nepa_trigger_llm_run_at"] = final["nepa_trigger_llm_run_at"].fillna("")

# One row per project_id — must hold before writing.
assert final["project_id"].is_unique, "Duplicate project_ids in output — check tier logic"

# Scope check: verify only clean energy project IDs are present.
clean_ids = set(projects["project_id"])
assert final["project_id"].isin(clean_ids).all(), "Non-clean project IDs in output"

# nepa_trigger_secondary must be a Python list (Arrow list<string> in parquet).
# Do NOT convert to JSON string — R's arrow::read_parquet() handles list columns natively.
assert final["nepa_trigger_secondary"].apply(isinstance, args=(list,)).all(), \
    "nepa_trigger_secondary must be list type"

# Enforce final column order before writing.
OUTPUT_COLS = [
    "project_id",
    "nepa_trigger_primary", "nepa_trigger_secondary", "nepa_trigger_multi",
    "nepa_trigger_evidence_text", "nepa_trigger_evidence_source",
    "nepa_trigger_confidence", "nepa_trigger_rule_id",
    "nepa_trigger_manual_review", "is_dual_nexus",
    "nepa_trigger_extraction_run_at", "nepa_trigger_llm_run_at",
]
final = final[OUTPUT_COLS]

final.to_parquet(OUTPUT_DIR / "projects_nepa_trigger.parquet", index=False)

# Write validation batches for manual review workflow
batches = build_validation_batches(final)
if not batches.empty:
    batches.to_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "validation_batches.csv", index=False)
    print(f"Validation batches written: {len(batches)} flagged cases across "
          f"{batches['validation_batch'].nunique()} rules")



if __name__ == "__main__":
    import argparse
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--eda", action="store_true", help="Run EDA check only; do not extract")
    parser.add_argument("--use-llm", action="store_true", help="Enable Tier 5 Haiku fallback")
    parser.add_argument("--sample", type=int, default=None)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.eda:
        run_eda(duckdb.connect())
    else:
        extract_nepa_triggers(use_llm=args.use_llm, sample=args.sample)

title: D1: NEPA Triggered — Implementation Plan
text: Hard filter: 20,725 clean energy projects only. All DuckDB queries and dataframe loads must apply WHERE project_energy_type = 'Clean' from the first step. Do not process or output results for non-clean projects. Document this as a constant at the top of the extraction script.

title: D1: NEPA Triggered — Implementation Plan
text:
Seven classes per nepa_trigger_classification_scheme.md. The old 3-class scheme (federal_land, federal_funding, federal_permit) is replaced entirely.







Code
Description




federal_action
Federal agency is the primary actor/proposer (not just authorizing a private applicant)


federal_program
Programmatic EIS, land-use plan revision, rulemaking, leasing framework


federal_property_transaction
Land exchange, disposal, conveyance, acquisition


federal_land
Project on/crossing federal land; ROW grant or special use permit to a private developer


federal_permit
Federal permit, license, or authorization is the primary nexus (e.g., FERC, USACE Section 404)


federal_funding
Federal grant, loan guarantee, cost-share, or financial assistance


unknown
NEPA review confirmed but trigger cannot be reliably identified



Priority order for primary trigger assignment (use when signals conflict): 1. federal_action 2. federal_program 3. federal_property_transaction 4. federal_land 5. federal_permit 6. federal_funding 7. unknown
Primary vs. secondary trigger: The primary trigger is the main focus of all analysis and figures. Secondary triggers are stored in nepa_trigger_secondary (list) and surface only in multi-label combo analysis and on explicit request. Do not display secondary labels in primary figures.


The critical boundary: BLM/USFS/NPS as the proposing/implementing agency vs. as the authorizing agency for a private developer.
Rule: If the lead agency is the grammatical subject of action verbs (construct, install, operate, implement, manage, maintain, restore) in the title or description, assign federal_action. If the lead agency is the authorizing body for a private applicant (grant, authorize, approve, evaluate an application from, consider a ROW request by), assign federal_land.
Verb signals for federal_action (agency as actor):
FEDERAL_ACTION_VERB_PATTERNS = [
    r'\b(?:proposes?\s+to|will|would)\s+(?:construct|install|build|operate|implement|manage|restore|undertake|develop|upgrade|expand)\b',
    r'\bagency.{0,20}(?:proposes|proposes to|will construct|will install|will implement)\b',
    r'\b(?:Forest Service|Bureau of Land Management|BLM|USFS|NPS|Bureau of Reclamation)\s+(?:proposes|will|plans to)\b',
    r'\bfederal\s+(?:construction|facility|installation|project|operation)\b',
    r'\bmilitary\s+(?:installation|base|facility|construction)\b',
]
Verb signals for federal_land (agency as authorizer):
FEDERAL_LAND_AUTHORIZER_PATTERNS = [
    r'\b(?:right.of.way|ROW)\s+(?:grant|application|request)\b',
    r'\b(?:applicant|proponent|developer|company)\b',
    r'\bspecial\s+use\s+(?:permit|authorization)\b',
    r'\bwould\s+(?:authorize|approve|grant|allow)\s+(?:a|the)\b',
    r'\b(?:application|request)\s+(?:by|from)\b',
    r'\bhas\s+(?:applied|submitted)\s+(?:an application|a request)\b',
]
When both sets match, prefer federal_action (higher priority). When only authorizer verbs are present alongside federal land agencies, assign federal_land. When neither set matches, fall through to standard agency-code heuristic.



All patterns are defined inline in 01_extract_nepa_trigger.py. Do not import from extract_reviews.py.
# Scan project/document title
PROGRAMMATIC_TITLE_PATTERNS = [
    r'\bprogrammatic\b',
    r'\bprogram[\-\s]?wide\b',
    r'\bpeis\b',
    r'\bpea\b',
]

# Strong indicators in description or first 5 pages
PROGRAMMATIC_STRONG_PATTERNS = [
    r'(?:draft|final|supplemental)\s+programmatic\s+environmental\s+(?:impact\s+statement|assessment)',
    r'programmatic\s+environmental\s+(?:impact\s+statement|assessment)',
    r'\b(?:dpeis|fpeis|speis|peis|pea)\b',
    r'this\s+programmatic\s+(?:eis|ea|environmental)',
    r'resource\s+management\s+plan\s+(?:amendment|revision)',
    r'\bleasing\s+(?:program|framework)\b',
    r'\bcorridor\s+designation\b',
]

# Exclusions — these contain "programmatic" but are NOT federal_program triggers
PROGRAMMATIC_EXCLUSION_PATTERNS = [
    r'programmatic\s+agreement',
    r'programmatic\s+biological\s+opinion',
    r'programmatic\s+consultation',
    r'programmatic\s+collaboration',
]
Apply: if title matches PROGRAMMATIC_TITLE_PATTERNS AND text does NOT match PROGRAMMATIC_EXCLUSION_PATTERNS, check for PROGRAMMATIC_STRONG_PATTERNS in description or first 5 pages to confirm.
Expected frequency: <3% of clean energy projects. Handle as a distinct category but do not invest heavily in validation. Projects classified as federal_program should be noted as potentially being umbrella reviews rather than individual site projects, and may warrant separate treatment in the analysis.



After primary/secondary assignment, add a computed binary flag:
df["is_dual_nexus"] = (
    (df["nepa_trigger_primary"] == "federal_land") &
    (df["nepa_trigger_secondary"].apply(lambda x: "federal_permit" in x if isinstance(x, list) else False))
)
This captures the canonical transmission-line case (crosses federal land + requires USACE Section 404) without collapsing it into either trigger type. Use in timeline comparisons to test whether dual-nexus projects have longer review durations.

import os
if os.environ.get("CONDA_DEFAULT_ENV") != "nepa":
    raise SystemExit("Please run in conda env 'nepa' (e.g., `conda run -n nepa python ...`).")

import duckdb
import pandas as pd
import re
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Optional

BASE_DIR   = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent  # repo root
DATA_DIR   = BASE_DIR / "data"
ANALYSIS_DIR = DATA_DIR / "analysis"
OUTPUT_DIR = ANALYSIS_DIR / "nepa_trigger"
OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

PROJECTS_PATH  = ANALYSIS_DIR / "projects_combined.parquet"
CE_PAGES_PATH  = DATA_DIR / "processed" / "ce"  / "pages.parquet"
EA_PAGES_PATH  = DATA_DIR / "processed" / "ea"  / "pages.parquet"
EIS_PAGES_PATH = DATA_DIR / "processed" / "eis" / "pages.parquet"
CE_DOCS_PATH   = DATA_DIR / "processed" / "ce"  / "documents.parquet"
EA_DOCS_PATH   = DATA_DIR / "processed" / "ea"  / "documents.parquet"
EIS_DOCS_PATH  = DATA_DIR / "processed" / "eis" / "documents.parquet"

# Columns needed from documents.parquet for Tier 2
DOC_COLUMNS = ["project_id", "document_id", "document_title", "file_name", "main_document"]

CLEAN_ENERGY_FILTER = "project_energy_type = 'Clean'"  # n = 20,725; hard constraint



Before the extraction pipeline, run a one-time EDA query to understand description coverage:
def run_eda(conn: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection) -> None:
    """
    Print description coverage and length stats for clean energy projects.
    Informs whether Tier 1b (description keyword match) will have useful coverage.
    Run once before implementing the full pipeline; outputs to stdout.
    """
    result = conn.execute(f"""
        SELECT
            process_type,
            COUNT(*) AS n,
            SUM(CASE WHEN project_description IS NOT NULL
                      AND LENGTH(project_description) > 50 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_with_desc,
            AVG(LENGTH(project_description)) AS avg_desc_len
        FROM read_parquet('{PROJECTS_PATH}')
        WHERE {CLEAN_ENERGY_FILTER}
        GROUP BY process_type
        ORDER BY process_type
    """).fetchdf()
    print(result.to_string())






Map lead agency codes to unambiguous trigger types. Apply verb disambiguation rule to separate federal_action from federal_land for land-managing agencies.
# Pure-signal agency → trigger type mappings (no ambiguity)
AGENCY_PERMIT_MAP = {
    "FERC", "Federal Energy Regulatory Commission",
    "FAA", "Federal Aviation Administration",
    "FCC", "Federal Communications Commission",
}
AGENCY_FUNDING_MAP = {
    "DOT", "Department of Transportation",
    "HUD", "Department of Housing and Urban Development",
    "FTA", "Federal Transit Administration",
    "FHWA", "Federal Highway Administration",
}
AGENCY_LAND_MAP = {
    "BLM", "Bureau of Land Management",
    "USFS", "FS", "US Forest Service", "Forest Service",
    "NPS", "National Park Service",
    "FWS", "USFWS", "Fish and Wildlife Service",
    "BOR", "USBR", "Bureau of Reclamation",
}
# DOE and USACE require verb disambiguation — do NOT assign in Tier 1a without verb check
AGENCY_AMBIGUOUS = {"DOE", "Department of Energy", "USACE", "Army Corps of Engineers"}
For land agencies, apply verb disambiguation from the patterns above. If action verbs found → federal_action; if authorizer verbs found or no verb match → federal_land.
Rule ID format: T1a_{AGENCY_CODE}_{trigger} (e.g., T1a_BLM_land, T1a_BLM_action).




Apply to all projects not resolved at confidence = high in Tier 1a, plus ambiguous agencies. Search project title and project description fields (no document access).
Pattern categories cover all 7 classes with specificity-ranked patterns (more specific patterns rank higher; match first specific pattern, record rule_id).
Key additions beyond the old plan: - federal_property_transaction: “land exchange”, “conveyance”, “disposal of federal land”, “parcel transfer” - federal_action: agency-name + action verb phrases (see disambiguation section above) - federal_program: inline patterns below (do not import from extract_reviews.py)
Rule ID format: T1b_{pattern_slug} (e.g., T1b_row_grant, T1b_sec404, T1b_loan_guarantee).




Scan NEPA document titles for unambiguous trigger phrases before touching page text. All patterns are defined inline in 01_extract_nepa_trigger.py — no import from extract_reviews.py or any other phase script.
Additional patterns: - “Land Exchange” → federal_property_transaction - “Right-of-Way” in title → federal_land - “Permit Application” / “License Amendment” → federal_permit - “Programmatic” + exclusion filter → federal_program
Rule ID format: T2_doc_title_{slug}.




For projects unresolved at Tier 2, extract the “Purpose and Need” section from pages.parquet. Do NOT scan full 30 pages — target the specific section.
PURPOSE_AND_NEED_HEADERS = [
    r'\bpurpose\s+and\s+need\b',
    r'\bneed\s+for\s+(?:federal\s+)?action\b',
    r'\bproposed\s+(?:federal\s+)?action\b',
    r'\bproject\s+purpose\b',
    r'\bstatement\s+of\s+need\b',
]

def extract_purpose_and_need(text: str, window: int = 600) -> str:
    """
    Detect Purpose and Need section header; return up to `window` chars following it.
    Returns empty string if no header found.
    """
    for pattern in PURPOSE_AND_NEED_HEADERS:
        m = re.search(pattern, text, re.IGNORECASE)
        if m:
            snippet = text[m.start():m.start() + window]
            return snippet
    return ""
Apply keyword matching to the extracted window. Capture the full sentence containing the match as nepa_trigger_evidence_text.
Scan only pages 1–10 per document (covers all Purpose and Need sections in practice).
Rule ID format: T3_pan_{slug} (e.g., T3_pan_row_grant).




For projects with no confident match after Tier 3, score candidate evidence text (Purpose and Need snippet or Tier 1b description) against class prototype sentences using all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (already in the pipeline).
CLASS_PROTOTYPES = {
    "federal_action": [
        "The Forest Service proposes to implement vegetation management on National Forest land.",
        "The Bureau of Land Management will construct a new facility at the site.",
        "This federal action consists of upgrading an existing federal facility.",
    ],
    "federal_program": [
        "This programmatic environmental impact statement evaluates a regional leasing framework.",
        "The Bureau of Land Management is revising its resource management plan.",
    ],
    "federal_land": [
        "The project requires a right-of-way grant across Bureau of Land Management land.",
        "The proposed transmission line would cross National Forest System lands.",
        "The applicant has applied for a special use permit on federal land.",
    ],
    "federal_permit": [
        "The project requires an individual permit from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers under Section 404.",
        "FERC approval is required before the project can proceed.",
        "The project requires authorization under Section 10 of the Rivers and Harbors Act.",
    ],
    "federal_funding": [
        "The project is funded through a Department of Energy loan guarantee.",
        "Federal financial assistance is provided through a DOE grant under Title XVII.",
        "The project is a recipient of federal funding through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law.",
    ],
    "federal_property_transaction": [
        "The proposed action consists of a land exchange between the federal government and a private party.",
        "The Bureau of Land Management proposes to convey this federal parcel to the state.",
    ],
}
Embed all prototypes at startup. For each unresolved project, embed the candidate text, compute cosine similarity to each class centroid, assign to highest class if similarity ≥ 0.45 threshold, else unknown. Set confidence = medium for assignments above threshold, low below.
Rule ID format: T4_embed_{class}.




For projects with confidence = low after all tiers (target ≤5% of 20,725 ≈ 1,000 projects). Only runs when --use-llm flag is set.
PROMPT = """You are classifying what triggered a NEPA environmental review for an energy project.
Given the text below, identify the primary federal nexus.

Classes:
- federal_action: federal agency is the primary actor constructing or implementing the project
- federal_program: programmatic EIS, land-use plan, rulemaking, or leasing framework
- federal_property_transaction: land exchange, disposal, or conveyance
- federal_land: project on or crossing federal land; ROW grant to a private developer
- federal_permit: federal permit, license, or authorization is the primary nexus
- federal_funding: federal grant, loan guarantee, or financial assistance
- unknown: cannot determine from the text provided

Text: {text}

Respond with JSON only:
{{"primary": "federal_land", "secondary": ["federal_permit"], "confidence": "high", "reasoning": "..."}}"""
Set nepa_trigger_llm_run_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat() per row on success.
Rule ID format: T5_llm.





CEs are 1–3 page forms, not narrative NEPA documents. Do not apply the full Tier 3 Purpose and Need extraction to CEs — the entire document may be 2 pages.
For CE records: 1. Apply Tiers 1a, 1b, 2 as normal. 2. If unresolved: scan the entire CE document text (no page limit, since documents are short). 3. If CE category code is available in metadata: build a lookup table mapping CE category codes to trigger types (e.g., BLM Instruction Memo 2012-044 categories map to federal_land). This may resolve more CE cases than text scanning.
Flag CE records with process_type = 'CE' in all diagnostic outputs for separate review.




Target: ≤5% of 20,725 projects flagged for manual review (~1,000 max). If the pipeline flags more than this, tighten confidence thresholds before finalizing.
Validation by rule batch rather than individual case review:
def build_validation_batches(df: pd.DataFrame, sample_per_batch: int = 20) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Group flagged cases by nepa_trigger_rule_id. For each unique rule that
    produced low-confidence results, sample up to `sample_per_batch` cases.
    Review the sample; if precision >= 0.85, accept the full batch without
    further review. If precision < 0.85, either fix the rule or flag all
    cases from that rule for individual review.
    """
    flagged = df[df["nepa_trigger_manual_review"] == True]
    batches = []
    for rule_id, group in flagged.groupby("nepa_trigger_rule_id"):
        sample = group.sample(min(sample_per_batch, len(group)), random_state=42)
        sample["validation_batch"] = rule_id
        sample["batch_size"] = len(group)
        batches.append(sample)
    return pd.concat(batches, ignore_index=True) if batches else pd.DataFrame()
Output validation_batches.csv alongside the main parquet. Reviewer works through batches in descending order of batch_size — fixing the largest broken rule has the most impact. Once a batch is reviewed and the rule confirmed, set nepa_trigger_manual_review = False for all rows from that rule.
Pre-validation step: Before the full run, spot-check 30 random BLM projects and 30 random FERC projects from Tier 1a results. If ≥28/30 are correctly classified, Tier 1a is trustworthy and those cases do not need manual_review = True even at medium confidence.




Each tier receives only the projects not yet resolved by all prior tiers. A project is “resolved” when nepa_trigger_confidence is high or medium. Low-confidence results from an earlier tier are kept but the project is still passed to the next tier to attempt a better classification.
def extract_nepa_triggers(use_llm=False, sample=None):
    conn = duckdb.connect()

    # Load clean energy project IDs and key metadata only.
    # dataset_source ('CE', 'EA', 'EIS') routes each project to the correct
    # docs/pages parquet in Tiers 2 and 3.
    projects = conn.execute(f"""
        SELECT project_id, lead_agency_harmonized, project_title,
               project_description, process_type, dataset_source
        FROM read_parquet('{PROJECTS_PATH}')
        WHERE {CLEAN_ENERGY_FILTER}
    """).fetchdf()
    if sample:
        projects = projects.sample(sample, random_state=42)

    all_project_ids = set(projects["project_id"])
    resolved = {}  # project_id -> result dict; grows as tiers run

    # Tier 1a
    r1a = tier1a_metadata(projects)
    resolved.update({r["project_id"]: r for r in r1a if r["nepa_trigger_confidence"] in ("high", "medium")})

    # Tier 1b — only unresolved
    unresolved = projects[~projects["project_id"].isin(resolved)]
    r1b = tier1b_title_description(unresolved)
    resolved.update({r["project_id"]: r for r in r1b if r["nepa_trigger_confidence"] in ("high", "medium")})

    # Tier 2 — only unresolved
    unresolved_ids = list(all_project_ids - set(resolved))
    r2 = tier2_doc_title(unresolved_ids, conn)
    resolved.update({r["project_id"]: r for r in r2 if r["nepa_trigger_confidence"] in ("high", "medium")})

    # Tier 3 — only unresolved; CE records handled separately (full doc scan, no page limit)
    unresolved_ids = list(all_project_ids - set(resolved))
    r3 = tier3_purpose_and_need(unresolved_ids, projects, conn)
    resolved.update({r["project_id"]: r for r in r3 if r["nepa_trigger_confidence"] in ("high", "medium")})

    # Tier 4 — embedding similarity on all still-unresolved
    unresolved_ids = list(all_project_ids - set(resolved))
    r4 = tier4_embedding(unresolved_ids, projects, conn)
    resolved.update({r["project_id"]: r for r in r4})

    # Tier 5 — LLM on confidence=low residuals (if --use-llm)
    if use_llm:
        low_conf = [pid for pid, r in resolved.items() if r["nepa_trigger_confidence"] == "low"]
        r5 = tier5_llm(low_conf, projects, conn)
        resolved.update({r["project_id"]: r for r in r5})

    # Any project with no assignment at all → unknown
    for pid in all_project_ids:
        if pid not in resolved:
            resolved[pid] = {
                "project_id": pid,
                "nepa_trigger_primary": "unknown",
                "nepa_trigger_secondary": [],
                "nepa_trigger_multi": [],
                "nepa_trigger_evidence_text": "",
                "nepa_trigger_evidence_source": "",
                "nepa_trigger_confidence": "low",
                "nepa_trigger_rule_id": "no_match",
                "nepa_trigger_manual_review": True,
                "nepa_trigger_llm_run_at": "",
            }

    return pd.DataFrame(list(resolved.values()))



run_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
final = extract_nepa_triggers(use_llm=args.use_llm, sample=args.sample)

# Compute is_dual_nexus (post-assignment)
final["is_dual_nexus"] = (
    (final["nepa_trigger_primary"] == "federal_land") &
    (final["nepa_trigger_secondary"].apply(
        lambda x: "federal_permit" in x if isinstance(x, list) else False
    ))
)

final["nepa_trigger_extraction_run_at"] = run_at
# nepa_trigger_llm_run_at is set per-row in Tier 5; fill "" elsewhere
if "nepa_trigger_llm_run_at" not in final.columns:
    final["nepa_trigger_llm_run_at"] = ""
else:
    final["nepa_trigger_llm_run_at"] = final["nepa_trigger_llm_run_at"].fillna("")

# One row per project_id — must hold before writing.
assert final["project_id"].is_unique, "Duplicate project_ids in output — check tier logic"

# Scope check: verify only clean energy project IDs are present.
clean_ids = set(projects["project_id"])
assert final["project_id"].isin(clean_ids).all(), "Non-clean project IDs in output"

# nepa_trigger_secondary must be a Python list (Arrow list<string> in parquet).
# Do NOT convert to JSON string — R's arrow::read_parquet() handles list columns natively.
assert final["nepa_trigger_secondary"].apply(isinstance, args=(list,)).all(), \
    "nepa_trigger_secondary must be list type"

# Enforce final column order before writing.
OUTPUT_COLS = [
    "project_id",
    "nepa_trigger_primary", "nepa_trigger_secondary", "nepa_trigger_multi",
    "nepa_trigger_evidence_text", "nepa_trigger_evidence_source",
    "nepa_trigger_confidence", "nepa_trigger_rule_id",
    "nepa_trigger_manual_review", "is_dual_nexus",
    "nepa_trigger_extraction_run_at", "nepa_trigger_llm_run_at",
]
final = final[OUTPUT_COLS]

final.to_parquet(OUTPUT_DIR / "projects_nepa_trigger.parquet", index=False)

# Write validation batches for manual review workflow
batches = build_validation_batches(final)
if not batches.empty:
    batches.to_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "validation_batches.csv", index=False)
    print(f"Validation batches written: {len(batches)} flagged cases across "
          f"{batches['validation_batch'].nunique()} rules")



if __name__ == "__main__":
    import argparse
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--eda", action="store_true", help="Run EDA check only; do not extract")
    parser.add_argument("--use-llm", action="store_true", help="Enable Tier 5 Haiku fallback")
    parser.add_argument("--sample", type=int, default=None)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.eda:
        run_eda(duckdb.connect())
    else:
        extract_nepa_triggers(use_llm=args.use_llm, sample=args.sample)

import os
if os.environ.get("CONDA_DEFAULT_ENV") != "nepa":
    raise SystemExit("Please run in conda env 'nepa'.")

import duckdb
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Optional
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer



DATA_DIR = Path("data")
EA_PAGES_PATH = DATA_DIR / "processed" / "ea" / "pages.parquet"
EIS_PAGES_PATH = DATA_DIR / "processed" / "eis" / "pages.parquet"
OUTPUT_PATH = DATA_DIR / "analysis" / "visual_impacts" / "projects_visual_impacts.parquet"
OUTPUT_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

QUERY_TEXT = "visual impacts of the project on viewsheds, aesthetics, visual resources, landscape character"
TOP_N = 5
MAX_WORDS_PER_CHUNK = 200
MIN_WORDS_PER_CHUNK = 30
BATCH_SIZE = 256



def chunk_page(page_text: str, max_words: int = MAX_WORDS_PER_CHUNK) -> list[str]:
    """Split page text into ~200-word paragraph chunks."""
    paragraphs = [p.strip() for p in page_text.split('\n\n') if p.strip()]
    chunks = []
    current = []
    current_words = 0
    for para in paragraphs:
        words = len(para.split())
        if words < MIN_WORDS_PER_CHUNK:
            current.append(para)
            current_words += words
            if current_words >= max_words:
                chunks.append(' '.join(current))
                current, current_words = [], 0
        else:
            if current:
                chunks.append(' '.join(current))
                current, current_words = [], 0
            if words <= max_words:
                chunks.append(para)
            else:
                # Split long paragraph by sentences
                sentences = para.split('. ')
                buf, buf_words = [], 0
                for sent in sentences:
                    sw = len(sent.split())
                    if buf_words + sw > max_words and buf:
                        chunks.append('. '.join(buf))
                        buf, buf_words = [sent], sw
                    else:
                        buf.append(sent)
                        buf_words += sw
                if buf:
                    chunks.append('. '.join(buf))
    if current:
        chunks.append(' '.join(current))
    return [c for c in chunks if len(c.split()) >= MIN_WORDS_PER_CHUNK]



def extract_visual_impacts(
    sample: Optional[int] = None,
    output_path: Path = OUTPUT_PATH,
) -> pd.DataFrame:

    run_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    model = SentenceTransformer('all-MiniLM-L6-v2')
    query_embedding = model.encode(QUERY_TEXT, normalize_embeddings=True)
    conn = duckdb.connect()

    all_results = []

    for source, pages_path in [("EA", EA_PAGES_PATH), ("EIS", EIS_PAGES_PATH)]:
        if not pages_path.exists():
            print(f"Skipping {source}: {pages_path} not found")
            continue

        project_ids = conn.execute(f"""
            SELECT DISTINCT project_id
            FROM read_parquet('{pages_path}')
        """).fetchdf()["project_id"].tolist()

        if sample:
            import random; random.seed(42)
            project_ids = random.sample(project_ids, min(sample, len(project_ids)))

        # Process in batches of 50 projects to manage memory
        for i in range(0, len(project_ids), 50):
            batch_ids = project_ids[i:i+50]
            ids_str = ",".join(f"'{p}'" for p in batch_ids)

            pages = conn.execute(f"""
                SELECT project_id, page_num, page_text
                FROM read_parquet('{pages_path}')
                WHERE project_id IN ({ids_str})
                  AND length(page_text) > 100
                ORDER BY project_id, page_num
            """).fetchdf()

            for project_id, proj_pages in pages.groupby("project_id"):
                all_chunks = []
                all_page_nums = []
                for _, row in proj_pages.iterrows():
                    chunks = chunk_page(row["page_text"])
                    all_chunks.extend(chunks)
                    all_page_nums.extend([row["page_num"]] * len(chunks))

                if not all_chunks:
                    continue

                # Encode all chunks
                chunk_embeddings = model.encode(
                    all_chunks, batch_size=BATCH_SIZE, normalize_embeddings=True
                )

                # Cosine similarity (embeddings are normalized, so dot product = cosine)
                similarities = np.dot(chunk_embeddings, query_embedding)

                # Top-N chunks
                top_idx = np.argsort(similarities)[-TOP_N:][::-1]
                top_texts = [all_chunks[j] for j in top_idx]
                top_pages = [all_page_nums[j] for j in top_idx]
                max_sim = float(similarities[top_idx[0]])

                page_range = f"{min(top_pages)}-{max(top_pages)}" if len(set(top_pages)) > 1 else str(top_pages[0])

                all_results.append({
                    "project_id": project_id,
                    "source": source,
                    "visual_impacts_text": top_texts,
                    "visual_impacts_max_similarity": max_sim,
                    "visual_impacts_page_range": page_range,
                    "visual_impacts_extraction_run_at": run_at,
                })

            print(f"[{source}] Batch {i//50 + 1}: processed {len(batch_ids)} projects")

    df = pd.DataFrame(all_results)
    df.to_parquet(output_path, index=False)
    print(f"Wrote {len(df)} rows to {output_path}")
    return df


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import argparse
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--sample", type=int, default=None)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    extract_visual_impacts(sample=args.sample)

ea <- read_parquet("data/analysis/_timeline/timeline_ea.parquet")
eis <- read_parquet("data/analysis/_timeline/timeline_eis.parquet")

projects <- read_parquet("data/analysis/projects_combined.parquet")

# Merge NOI dates — noi_publication_date wins over bert_initiation_date
merge_initiation <- function(tl, fr_df) {
  tl |>
    left_join(fr_df |> select(project_id, noi_publication_date), by = "project_id") |>
    mutate(
      initiation_date = coalesce(noi_publication_date, bert_initiation_date)
    )
}

ce  <- merge_initiation(ce, fr)
ea  <- merge_initiation(ea, fr)
eis <- merge_initiation(eis, fr)

# Calculate durations
calc_durations <- function(tl, source) {
  tl |>
    filter(!is.na(initiation_date), !is.na(bert_decision_date)) |>
    mutate(
      duration_days = as.numeric(bert_decision_date - initiation_date),
      process_type = source,
      period = case_when(
        bert_decision_date >= as.Date("2023-08-16") ~ "post_FRA",
        bert_decision_date >= as.Date("2020-09-14") ~ "post_2020_CEQ",
        TRUE ~ "pre_2020"
      )
    ) |>
    filter(duration_days > 0, duration_days < 365 * 20)  # sanity bounds
}

durations <- bind_rows(
  calc_durations(ce, "CE"),
  calc_durations(ea, "EA"),
  calc_durations(eis, "EIS")
) |>
  left_join(projects |> select(project_id, agency_name, project_energy_type, is_linear), by = "project_id")

# Analyses: median by period × process type; by energy type; outliers
summary_table <- durations |>
  group_by(process_type, period) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    median_days = median(duration_days),
    p25 = quantile(duration_days, 0.25),
    p75 = quantile(duration_days, 0.75),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

outliers <- durations |>
  group_by(process_type) |>
  mutate(iqr = IQR(duration_days), q75 = quantile(duration_days, 0.75)) |>
  filter(duration_days > q75 + 2 * iqr) |>
  select(project_id, process_type, duration_days, agency_name)

write.csv(summary_table, "output/deliverable03/durations_summary.csv", row.names=FALSE)

import os
if os.environ.get("CONDA_DEFAULT_ENV") != "nepa":
    raise SystemExit("Please run in conda env 'nepa'.")

import re
import duckdb
import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Optional



DATA_DIR = Path("data")
CE_PAGES_PATH = DATA_DIR / "processed" / "ce" / "pages.parquet"
PROJECTS_PATH = DATA_DIR / "analysis" / "projects_combined.parquet"
OUTPUT_PATH = DATA_DIR / "analysis" / "law_citations" / "ce_law_citations.parquet"
OUTPUT_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# Regex patterns by law — use word boundaries; case-insensitive
CITATION_PATTERNS = {
    "ARRA": [
        (r"\bAmerican Recovery and Reinvestment Act\b", "full_name"),
        (r"\bRecovery Act\b", "short_name"),
        (r"\bARRA\b", "acronym"),
        (r"\bSection 1603\b", "program"),       # ARRA energy grant
        (r"\bSection 1705\b", "program"),       # DOE loan guarantee (ARRA-era)
    ],
    "BIL": [
        (r"\bBipartisan Infrastructure Law\b", "full_name"),
        (r"\bInfrastructure Investment and Jobs Act\b", "full_name_alt"),
        (r"\bIIJA\b", "acronym"),
        (r"\bBIL\b", "acronym"),
    ],
    "IRA": [
        (r"\bInflation Reduction Act\b", "full_name"),
        # IRA acronym needs disambiguation — require co-occurrence with energy terms
        # Handled in disambiguation logic below
        (r"\bSection 60101\b", "program"),      # IRA clean energy provision
        (r"\bSection 50265\b", "program"),      # IRA direct pay
    ],
    "DOE_funding": [
        (r"\bDOE Loan Guarantee\b", "program"),
        (r"\bLoan Programs Office\b", "program"),
        (r"\bTitle XVII\b", "program"),
        (r"\bSection 1703\b", "program"),
        (r"\bDepartment of Energy.*grant\b", "funding"),
    ],
}

# Context words required near "IRA" to avoid false positives (Individual Retirement Account)
IRA_CONTEXT_REQUIRED = [
    r"clean energy", r"renewable", r"solar", r"wind", r"climate",
    r"greenhouse gas", r"battery", r"transmission", r"electric vehicle",
    r"inflation reduction"
]



def detect_citations(text: str) -> dict:
    """
    Detect law citations in text. Returns dict of {law_name: [(pattern, match_text, context)]}.
    IRA acronym requires co-occurrence with energy-related terms.
    """
    results = {}

    for law, patterns in CITATION_PATTERNS.items():
        matches = []
        for pat, pat_type in patterns:
            for m in re.finditer(pat, text, re.IGNORECASE):
                # Special disambiguation for IRA acronym
                if law == "IRA" and pat_type == "acronym":
                    # Check window ±200 chars for energy context
                    window = text[max(0, m.start()-200):m.end()+200]
                    has_context = any(
                        re.search(ctx, window, re.IGNORECASE)
                        for ctx in IRA_CONTEXT_REQUIRED
                    )
                    if not has_context:
                        continue  # skip — likely financial IRA

                # Extract context snippet
                context = text[max(0, m.start()-100):m.end()+100].strip()
                matches.append({
                    "pattern": pat,
                    "pattern_type": pat_type,
                    "match_text": m.group(),
                    "context": context,
                })
        if matches:
            results[law] = matches

    return results



def extract_law_citations(
    sample: Optional[int] = None,
    output_path: Path = OUTPUT_PATH,
) -> pd.DataFrame:

    run_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    conn = duckdb.connect()

    # Get CE project list
    projects = conn.execute(f"""
        SELECT project_id
        FROM read_parquet('{PROJECTS_PATH}')
        WHERE process_type = 'CE'
    """).fetchdf()

    if sample:
        projects = projects.sample(n=min(sample, len(projects)), random_state=42)

    project_ids = projects["project_id"].tolist()

    all_results = []

    # Process in batches of 200 projects
    batch_size = 200
    for i in range(0, len(project_ids), batch_size):
        batch_ids = project_ids[i:i+batch_size]
        ids_str = ",".join(f"'{p}'" for p in batch_ids)

        # Load first 20 pages per project
        pages = conn.execute(f"""
            SELECT project_id, page_num, string_agg(page_text, ' ') AS combined_text
            FROM read_parquet('{CE_PAGES_PATH}')
            WHERE project_id IN ({ids_str})
              AND page_num <= 20
              AND length(page_text) > 50
            GROUP BY project_id, page_num
            ORDER BY project_id, page_num
        """).fetchdf()

        # Combine all pages per project, then detect
        for project_id, proj_pages in pages.groupby("project_id"):
            full_text = " ".join(proj_pages["combined_text"].tolist())
            citations = detect_citations(full_text)

            for law_name, matches in citations.items():
                # One row per project-law pair
                first_match = matches[0]
                all_results.append({
                    "project_id": project_id,
                    "law_name": law_name,
                    "citation_count": len(matches),
                    "first_page": proj_pages.iloc[0]["page_num"],  # approx
                    "context_text": first_match["context"][:500],
                    "match_type": first_match["pattern_type"],
                    "law_citations_extraction_run_at": run_at,
                })

        if (i // batch_size) % 10 == 0:
            print(f"Processed batch {i//batch_size + 1} / {len(project_ids)//batch_size + 1}")

    df = pd.DataFrame(all_results)
    df.to_parquet(output_path, index=False)
    print(f"Wrote {len(df)} rows to {output_path}")
    return df


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import argparse
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--sample", type=int, default=None)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    extract_law_citations(sample=args.sample)





library(arrow); library(dplyr); library(lubridate); library(ggplot2); library(zoo)

projects  <- read_parquet("data/analysis/projects_combined.parquet")

# Merge on CE projects with dates
ce <- projects |>
  filter(process_type == "CE", !is.na(start_date)) |>
  mutate(start_date = as.Date(start_date))

# --- 1. Temporal trend analysis ---

# Monthly CE counts
monthly <- ce |>
  mutate(month = floor_date(start_date, "month")) |>
  count(month, name = "n_projects") |>
  filter(month >= as.Date("2007-01-01"), month <= as.Date("2025-01-01")) |>
  arrange(month) |>
  mutate(
    n_smoothed = rollmean(n_projects, k=3, fill=NA, align="right"),
    # Spike window flags
    arra_window = month >= as.Date("2009-03-01") & month <= as.Date("2010-02-28"),
    bil_window  = month >= as.Date("2021-12-01") & month <= as.Date("2022-11-30"),
    ira_window  = month >= as.Date("2022-09-01") & month <= as.Date("2023-08-31")
  )

# Spike summary: mean monthly CEs in window vs. 24-month pre-law baseline
spike_summary <- bind_rows(
  tibble(law="ARRA",
    window_mean = monthly |> filter(arra_window) |> pull(n_projects) |> mean(),

) |> mutate(spike_ratio = window_mean / baseline_mean)

# Law passage dates
law_dates <- tibble(
  law = c("ARRA", "BIL", "IRA"),
  passage_date = as.Date(c("2009-02-17", "2021-11-15", "2022-08-16")),

characterize_spike <- function(ce_df, window_start, window_end, baseline_start, baseline_end) {
  spike <- ce_df |> filter(start_date >= window_start, start_date <= window_end) |> mutate(period = "spike")
  baseline <- ce_df |> filter(start_date >= baseline_start, start_date <= baseline_end) |> mutate(period = "baseline")
  bind_rows(spike, baseline) |>
    count(period, project_energy_type) |>
    group_by(period) |>
    mutate(pct = n / sum(n))
}

arra_char <- characterize_spike(ce,
  as.Date("2009-03-01"), as.Date("2010-02-28"),

  as.Date("2020-09-01"), as.Date("2022-08-31")
