# --- 3. Citation rates ---
# What % of spike-window CEs have explicit law citation?
citation_rates <- ce |>
  mutate(
    arra_window = start_date >= as.Date("2009-03-01") & start_date <= as.Date("2010-02-28"),
    bil_window  = start_date >= as.Date("2021-12-01") & start_date <= as.Date("2022-11-30"),
    ira_window  = start_date >= as.Date("2022-09-01") & start_date <= as.Date("2023-08-31")
  ) |>
  left_join(citations, by = "project_id") |>

    n = n(),
    n_cited = sum(!is.na(law_name) & law_name == "ARRA"),

  )
# Repeat for BIL, IRA

# --- Outputs ---
dir.create("output/deliverable05", recursive=TRUE, showWarnings=FALSE)
write.csv(monthly, "output/deliverable05/spike_counts_monthly.csv", row.names=FALSE)
write.csv(spike_summary, "output/deliverable05/spike_summary.csv", row.names=FALSE)

title: Federal Register Evidence Matching Plan
text:
Add a NEPATEC-derived Federal Register evidence layer so the NOI matcher can use direct evidence from the project’s own documents — specifically FR Doc. numbers and Federal Register URLs — to join to the API corpus. A secondary goal is to use this evidence to improve project initiation date coverage, including for EA, EIS, and CE projects.
The final date used for timeline analysis should remain the Federal Register API publication_date, saved as noi_publication_date.



The current Phase 2 Federal Register workflow matches projects to Federal Register records using corpus-level title and context matching. This is a strong improvement over Phase 1, but it has two compounding problems:

Title-only matches are unreliable. A title match has no temporal anchor. If a project went through multiple review iterations, title matching can silently return an NOI date from a prior iteration rather than the current one.
Direct NEPATEC evidence is unused. Many NEPATEC documents already contain the FR Doc. number for their own NOI. This is a much stronger signal than title similarity.

Example:

Project: Jackalope Wind Energy Project
Project ID: bef66b39ae62bd8e8520e7d633a72604
NEPATEC document: Jackalope Federal Register Notice.pdf
NEPATEC page text includes: [FR Doc. 2024–05618 Filed 3–15–24; 8:45 am]
Federal Register API document_number: 2024-05618
Federal Register API publication_date: 2024-03-18

Note on en-dashes: Real NEPATEC page text uses en-dashes (–) in FR Doc. brackets, not ASCII hyphens (-). The API corpus uses ASCII hyphens. Normalization is required before joining.




Build the usual Phase 2 project, document, and page data from NEPATEC.
Scan EA/EIS/CE page text for Federal Register evidence using DuckDB.
Save the extracted evidence to a cacheable artifact.
Pull or load the Federal Register API NOI corpus.
Match NEPATEC projects to Federal Register documents using direct FR doc number evidence.
Title-only matches go to manual review only — they do not populate noi_publication_date.
Save the final project-level noi_publication_date into federal_register.parquet.
Merge federal_register.parquet into projects_combined.parquet.

Key principle: noi_publication_date is only ever populated from a direct FR doc number join. Title matching is a review signal, not a date source. This protects against prior-iteration contamination.



Add a new function in phase2/code/extract/federal_register.py:
def extract_nepatec_federal_register_evidence(
    projects: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    analysis_dir: Path,
    process_types: tuple[str, ...] = ("EA", "EIS", "CE"),
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    ...


This scan must use DuckDB, not pandas. The EIS page file has 6,131,757 rows and the EA page file has 469,106 rows. Loading either into pandas memory would be impractical. A DuckDB scan with a LIKE filter on page_text runs in approximately 30 seconds.
Pattern:
import duckdb

con = duckdb.connect()
result = con.execute("""
    SELECT p.document_id, p.page_number, p.page_text,
           d.project_id, d.file_name, d.document_title,

       OR p.page_text LIKE '%federalregister.gov%'

""", [pages_path, documents_path]).df()

The FR Doc. number is the primary join key to the API corpus. Extract it using a regex that handles both ASCII hyphens and Unicode dashes:
_FR_DOC_RE = re.compile(
    r'\[FR Doc\.?\s+(\d{4}[\-\u2013\u2014]\d+)',
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
Before joining to the API corpus, normalize extracted numbers to ASCII hyphen:
def _normalize_fr_doc_number(raw: str) -> str:
    """Normalize FR Doc number: replace en-dash/em-dash with ASCII hyphen."""
    return re.sub(r'[\u2013\u2014]', '-', raw).strip()
Example: 2024–05618 → 2024-05618 (joins to API document_number: 2024-05618).



Federal Register URLs embed the document number and can be used as an alternative extraction path:
federalregister.gov/documents/2024/03/18/2024-05618/...
Extract the document number from the URL path segment. Normalize using the same _normalize_fr_doc_number helper.



Volume/page citations of the form 89 FR 19348 appear in NEPATEC text but cannot be used as join keys. The Federal Register API corpus has no citation field. Record the raw citation text in fr_citation as context, but do not attempt to join on it.



NEPATEC documents frequently cite their own publication date in prose. Extract these as initiation date signals even when no FR Doc. bracket is present:
"Published in the Federal Register on March 18, 2024"
"Federal Register, Vol. 89, No. 55, March 19, 2024"
"as published at 89 FR 19348 (March 19, 2024)"
"published ... on [date]"
Store the extracted date text in fr_date_text and the parsed date in fr_date_text_parsed. These can validate a doc-number join (filed date in bracket should be ~1–5 days before publication) or provide a fallback initiation date signal for review when no doc number join succeeds.



Many Federal Register references in NEPATEC pages are not NOI records. A page may cite an FR Doc. number for a resource advisory council meeting, a rule, or an adjacent notice from a different project.
Require that each FR Doc. number on a page be within a reasonable proximity to at least one NOI-like phrase before treating it as evidence for this project. Accepted phrases:
Notice of Intent
Intent To Prepare
Notice of Preparation
Notice To Prepare
Notice of Scoping
Notice of Public Scoping
If no such phrase appears near the FR Doc. number (within ~500 characters), record the FR Doc. number with evidence_type = fr_doc_non_noi and exclude it from the primary join path. These rows are retained in the evidence table for diagnostics.
For CE pages, also accept:
Notice of Application
Notice of Proposed Action
Categorical Exclusion
These phrases are CE-specific initiation signals not typically present in EIS/EA documents.

file_name contains "Federal Register"
file_name contains "FR Notice"
file_name contains "NOI"
document_title contains "Notice of Intent"
document_title contains "Intent To Prepare"

The Federal Register evidence layer is also an opportunity to improve noi_publication_date coverage beyond what the existing title-match workflow achieves, and to support initiation dates for CE projects that have no current FR coverage. Three strategies are in scope for this plan:


Some projects publish a scoping notice in the Federal Register before or instead of a formal NOI. In some agency workflows these are the same document; in others the scoping notice is a separate FR record published at the start of the scoping period — earlier than the NOI.
Add these queries to NOI_CORPUS_QUERIES:
"Notice of Scoping"
"Notice of Public Scoping"
"Scoping for Environmental Impact"
Because a scoping notice and a formal NOI for the same project will have different document numbers, both can appear in the evidence table. When multiple FR records join for one project, apply the tie-break rule: prefer the earlier publication date as the initiation date. Send the multi-record case to manual review so a human can confirm.
Note: scoping meeting dates (mentioned in NEPATEC prose) are later than the scoping notice publication date and are extracted from unverified text with no external anchor. They do not provide earlier or more reliable initiation signals than the scoping notice itself, and ad-hoc extraction from prose duplicates what the BERT initiation model already attempts. Scoping meeting date extraction is out of scope here; improvements to that signal belong in the BERT timeline pipeline.



NEPATEC documents often state their own publication date in prose. Extracting these provides a validation signal for doc-number joins and a soft initiation date for projects where the FR Doc. bracket is absent or OCR-corrupted.
Example patterns:
"Published in the Federal Register on March 18, 2024"
"Federal Register, Vol. 89, No. 55, March 19, 2024"
"as published at 89 FR 19348 (March 19, 2024)"
Use for join validation only. Where both a doc number join and an explicit prose date are present, check that the parsed date matches the API publication_date within ~10 days. A large discrepancy is a flag for review and can downgrade a high-confidence accept to review.
Prose-date-only evidence (no doc number join) should never auto-populate noi_publication_date. The date has no external anchor — it could refer to any Federal Register record on the page.



For projects that have both a bert_initiation_date and an noi_publication_date from the FR pipeline, compare the two in the validation report:

Agreement within ~60 days: high audit confidence.
BERT date significantly earlier than FR date: BERT may have captured a pre-NOI scoping or pre-application signal (useful diagnostic, not necessarily wrong).
BERT date significantly later than FR date: likely BERT misclassification of a decision or comment period date; flag for review.

This is a validation report output only — it does not change any automated decisions in the pipeline. It provides a low-cost quality lens on BERT extraction accuracy for the projects where external ground truth exists.



CE projects do not publish NOIs, and the current corpus queries (targeting NOI language) will not return CE-specific records. Expanding corpus queries to catch CE-relevant Federal Register records (Notice of Application, Notice of Proposed Action) would require a separate set of CE-targeted queries with different acceptance logic.
This is deferred. For FERC-regulated CE projects in particular, FERC eLibrary is a more reliable source of application filing dates than the Federal Register API, and a FERC eLibrary integration is a better future investment than CE-specific FR corpus queries. CE pages will still be scanned for any FR Doc. evidence that happens to be present, but all CE results go to manual review and no CE coverage improvement is expected from this plan.

4. Score direct-evidence candidates.
5. Run title matching for projects with no direct evidence — output to review only.
6. Select accepted, review-required, and unmatched project-level outputs.


The FR document number is the join key:
nepatec_fr_evidence.fr_document_number  →  noi_corups.fr_document_number
Title and agency overlap are the acceptance gate, not alternative join keys. They determine whether a successful document-number join should be auto-accepted or sent to review. Title matching alone — without a document-number join — never populates noi_publication_date.

API document_number: 2024-05618                          ← join succeeds
API title: "Jackalope Wind Energy Project"               ← corroboration: accept
API publication_date: 2024-03-18                         ← becomes noi_publication_date



Title matching has no temporal anchor. If a project was re-noticed after a prior iteration, title matching can return the old NOI date. The only guard against prior-iteration contamination is requiring a direct document-number join from the project’s own NEPATEC documents — which will reference the NOI for the iteration being reviewed, not an older one.
Title matches are kept as a review signal only: a strong title hit with no doc number evidence means “there may be an NOI for this project but we cannot verify it automatically.”

Only FR doc references failed the NOI proximity filter and no URL evidence exists.
Evidence is metadata-only (file_name or document_title) with no page-level FR doc number.
Title match score is below threshold and no direct evidence exists.

Do not auto-accept a document number just because it appears somewhere in the project files. EIS pages commonly contain adjacent Federal Register notices or references to related proceedings.

title: Federal Register Evidence Matching Plan
text:
Add a NEPATEC-derived Federal Register evidence layer so the NOI matcher can use direct evidence from the project’s own documents — specifically FR Doc. numbers and Federal Register URLs — to join to the API corpus. A secondary goal is to use this evidence to improve project initiation date coverage, including for EA, EIS, and CE projects.
The final date used for timeline analysis should remain the Federal Register API publication_date, saved as noi_publication_date.

title: Federal Register Evidence Matching Plan
text:
The current Phase 2 Federal Register workflow matches projects to Federal Register records using corpus-level title and context matching. This is a strong improvement over Phase 1, but it has two compounding problems:

Title-only matches are unreliable. A title match has no temporal anchor. If a project went through multiple review iterations, title matching can silently return an NOI date from a prior iteration rather than the current one.
Direct NEPATEC evidence is unused. Many NEPATEC documents already contain the FR Doc. number for their own NOI. This is a much stronger signal than title similarity.

Example:

Project: Jackalope Wind Energy Project
Project ID: bef66b39ae62bd8e8520e7d633a72604
NEPATEC document: Jackalope Federal Register Notice.pdf
NEPATEC page text includes: [FR Doc. 2024–05618 Filed 3–15–24; 8:45 am]
Federal Register API document_number: 2024-05618
Federal Register API publication_date: 2024-03-18

Note on en-dashes: Real NEPATEC page text uses en-dashes (–) in FR Doc. brackets, not ASCII hyphens (-). The API corpus uses ASCII hyphens. Normalization is required before joining.

title: Federal Register Evidence Matching Plan
text:
Build the usual Phase 2 project, document, and page data from NEPATEC.
Scan EA/EIS/CE page text for Federal Register evidence using DuckDB.
Save the extracted evidence to a cacheable artifact.
Pull or load the Federal Register API NOI corpus.
Match NEPATEC projects to Federal Register documents using direct FR doc number evidence.
Title-only matches go to manual review only — they do not populate noi_publication_date.
Save the final project-level noi_publication_date into federal_register.parquet.
Merge federal_register.parquet into projects_combined.parquet.

Key principle: noi_publication_date is only ever populated from a direct FR doc number join. Title matching is a review signal, not a date source. This protects against prior-iteration contamination.

    WHERE p.page_text LIKE '%FR Doc%'
       OR p.page_text LIKE '%federalregister.gov%'
       OR p.page_text LIKE '%Federal Register%'
""", [pages_path, documents_path]).df()

They do not provide earlier or more reliable initiation signals than the scoping notice itself, and ad-hoc extraction from prose duplicates what the BERT initiation model already attempts. Scoping meeting date extraction is out of scope here; improvements to that signal belong in the BERT timeline pipeline.



NEPATEC documents often state their own publication date in prose. Extracting these provides a validation signal for doc-number joins and a soft initiation date for projects where the FR Doc. bracket is absent or OCR-corrupted.
Example patterns:
"Published in the Federal Register on March 18, 2024"
"Federal Register, Vol. 89, No. 55, March 19, 2024"
"as published at 89 FR 19348 (March 19, 2024)"
Use for join validation only. Where both a doc number join and an explicit prose date are present, check that the parsed date matches the API publication_date within ~10 days. A large discrepancy is a flag for review and can downgrade a high-confidence accept to review.
Prose-date-only evidence (no doc number join) should never auto-populate noi_publication_date. The date has no external anchor — it could refer to any Federal Register record on the page.



For projects that have both a bert_initiation_date and an noi_publication_date from the FR pipeline, compare the two in the validation report:

Agreement within ~60 days: high audit confidence.
BERT date significantly earlier than FR date: BERT may have captured a pre-NOI scoping or pre-application signal (useful diagnostic, not necessarily wrong).
BERT date significantly later than FR date: likely BERT misclassification of a decision or comment period date; flag for review.

This is a validation report output only — it does not change any automated decisions in the pipeline. It provides a low-cost quality lens on BERT extraction accuracy for the projects where external ground truth exists.



CE projects do not publish NOIs, and the current corpus queries (targeting NOI language) will not return CE-specific records. Expanding corpus queries to catch CE-relevant Federal Register records (Notice of Application, Notice of Proposed Action) would require a separate set of CE-targeted queries with different acceptance logic.
This is deferred. For FERC-regulated CE projects in particular, FERC eLibrary is a more reliable source of application filing dates than the Federal Register API, and a FERC eLibrary integration is a better future investment than CE-specific FR corpus queries. CE pages will still be scanned for any FR Doc. evidence that happens to be present, but all CE results go to manual review and no CE coverage improvement is expected from this plan.

title: Federal Register Evidence Matching Plan
text:
Update refresh_federal_register_noi(...) in phase2/code/extract/federal_register.py so the order becomes:
1. Fetch or load the Federal Register API corpus (expanded queries including scoping notices).
2. Extract or load NEPATEC Federal Register evidence (cached if available).
3. Join NEPATEC normalized fr_document_number to API document_number.
4. Score direct-evidence candidates.
5. Run title matching for projects with no direct evidence — output to review only.
6. Select accepted, review-required, and unmatched project-level outputs.


The FR document number is the join key:
nepatec_fr_evidence.fr_document_number  →  noi_corups.fr_document_number
Title and agency overlap are the acceptance gate, not alternative join keys. They determine whether a successful document-number join should be auto-accepted or sent to review. Title matching alone — without a document-number join — never populates noi_publication_date.
Example:
NEPATEC page text: [FR Doc. 2024–05618 Filed 3–15–24; 8:45 am]
Normalized:        2024-05618
API document_number: 2024-05618                          ← join succeeds
API title: "Jackalope Wind Energy Project"               ← corroboration: accept
API publication_date: 2024-03-18                         ← becomes noi_publication_date



Title matching has no temporal anchor. If a project was re-noticed after a prior iteration, title matching can return the old NOI date. The only guard against prior-iteration contamination is requiring a direct document-number join from the project’s own NEPATEC documents — which will reference the NOI for the iteration being reviewed, not an older one.
Title matches are kept as a review signal only: a strong title hit with no doc number evidence means “there may be an NOI for this project but we cannot verify it automatically.”

title: Federal Register Evidence Matching Plan
text:
NEPATEC normalized fr_document_number joins to API document_number.
The FR Doc. number passed the NOI proximity filter (within ~500 chars of a NOI-like phrase).
At least one corroboration signal is present:

API title has strong project-title token overlap, OR
Nearby NEPATEC page context has strong project-title token overlap, OR
Agency, state, or process-type context agrees.






Document number joins but all corroboration signals are weak or absent.
Multiple distinct API documents are joined for one project via direct evidence.
Evidence comes from an appendix or non-main-document page with mixed corroboration.
FR Doc. number appears but failed the NOI proximity filter (evidence_type = fr_doc_non_noi).
Title-only match, any strength — document-number join is absent.




CE projects do not follow the standard NOI workflow. Any FR doc number found in a CE NEPATEC document — even one that passes the proximity filter and has strong corroboration — should be sent to manual review, not auto-accepted. Once CE FR coverage patterns are understood after a first pass, this rule can be revisited.




The joined API record’s title/context clearly refers to a different project.
Only FR doc references failed the NOI proximity filter and no URL evidence exists.
Evidence is metadata-only (file_name or document_title) with no page-level FR doc number.
Title match score is below threshold and no direct evidence exists.

Do not auto-accept a document number just because it appears somewhere in the project files. EIS pages commonly contain adjacent Federal Register notices or references to related proceedings.

title: D1 — NEPA Trigger Classification
text:
Purpose: Classify the federal nexus that triggers NEPA review for each clean energy project. Input: data/analysis/projects_combined.parquet + source-level docs/pages parquets (CE, EA, EIS). Output: data/analysis/nepa_trigger/projects_nepa_trigger.parquet, data/analysis/nepa_trigger/projects_funding_details.parquet, and validation batch CSV. Cost: LLM tier (optional) ~$1–4 (Claude Haiku) depending on share of unresolved cases; Tier 5 has a hard budget guardrail (default $10). Scope: 20,725 clean energy projects (project_energy_type = 'Clean'). Scripts: - phase2/code/deliverable01/01_extract_nepa_trigger.py — extraction pipeline - phase2/code/deliverable01/02_analyze_triggers.R — analysis and figures
Reference docs (in phase2/code/deliverable01/): - _notes.md — tactical notes, model selection rationale, threshold guidance - _legend.md — rule ID format and common examples - _example_bank.md — calibration examples (positives and hard negatives per class) - tier4_refactor_spec.md — Tier 4 design spec - tier4_implementation_checklist.md — implementation sequence



Seven primary trigger classes, in priority order (used to break ties when multiple signals are present):








Priority
Class
Typical federal nexus




1
federal_action
Agency itself proposes or implements the action


2
federal_program
Programmatic EIS, resource management plan, rulemaking


3
federal_property_transaction
Land exchange, conveyance, disposal


4
federal_land
Project on or crossing federal land; ROW grant


5
federal_permit
Agency permit, license, or authorization required


6
federal_funding
Federal grant, loan guarantee, cost share


7
unknown
Clear NEPA review but nexus not identifiable



Primary trigger: the federal nexus most directly responsible for the agency’s NEPA decision. Secondary triggers: additional nexuses clearly present (nepa_trigger_secondary, stored as Arrow list). is_dual_nexus: computed flag for federal_land primary + federal_permit secondary (transmission line case).




Each tier runs on projects not yet finalized by a prior tier. Tiers 1–3 produce results that are either auto-accepted (deterministic high-precision rules) or held as provisional (awaiting Tier 4 confirmation). Tier 4 processes all unfinalized projects.









Tier
Method
Source
Notes




1a
Agency metadata heuristics
projects_combined.parquet
BLM/USFS/NPS/FWS → federal_land (verb signals disambiguate action); FERC/FAA/FCC → federal_permit; DOE → provisional (funding vs action boundary)


1b
Keyword patterns on title + description
projects_combined.parquet
~30 patterns per class; returns first match; negation guard suppresses checklist false positives


2
Document title keyword scan
*_documents.parquet
Scans all documents for a project; programmatic title patterns fire here


3
Purpose and Need section
*_pages.parquet
CE: full doc scan with conservative pattern set (no sec404/arra/rmp); EA/EIS: P&N header detection, first 10 pages


4
Retrieval-first local NLI
*_pages.parquet
Chunk retrieval + cross-encoder/nli-MiniLM2-L6-H768 zero-shot NLI; embedding fallback if NLI unavailable; DOE and CE-heavy rows route here


5
Claude Haiku LLM
Tier 4 evidence bundles
Only with --use-llm; receives top chunks + local NLI scores + provisional class; subject to budget guardrail



Routing policy: - AUTO_ACCEPT_RULE_IDS — deterministic high-precision rules that finalize immediately (e.g., T1a_FERC_permit, T1b_special_use, T3_npdes) - SEND_TO_TIER4_RULE_IDS — ambiguous rules always routed to Tier 4 (e.g., T1a_DOE_action, T3_sec404, T3_arra) - AUDIT_FIRST_RULE_IDS — rules held for review before promotion (e.g., T3_rmp)






Validates that the NLI hypothesis templates are well-calibrated before running at scale. Takes ~2 minutes. Downloads the NLI model (~67MB) on first run.
conda run -n nepa python phase2/code/deliverable01/01_extract_nepa_trigger.py --calibrate
Passing criteria: - Positive examples: correct class scores ≥ 0.75 - Hard negatives: all class scores ≤ 0.50
If any check fails, adjust HYPOTHESIS_TEMPLATES in the script and re-run calibration before proceeding. See _example_bank.md for guidance on hypothesis wording.



Runs tiers 1a–4. Appropriate for an initial build or after pattern changes.
conda run -n nepa python phase2/code/deliverable01/01_extract_nepa_trigger.py



Adds Tier 5 (Claude Haiku) for the small uncertain queue remaining after Tier 4. Tier 5 has a preflight guardrail: if the estimated spend exceeds the budget cap (default $10), it writes tier5_queue.parquet and stops unless --force-tier5 is passed.
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY='sk-ant-...'

conda run -n nepa python phase2/code/deliverable01/01_extract_nepa_trigger.py --use-llm



Regenerates projects_funding_details.parquet from the existing trigger output without rerunning the trigger classifier or rewriting projects_nepa_trigger.parquet.
conda run -n nepa python phase2/code/deliverable01/01_extract_nepa_trigger.py --funding-details-only





Run on a random subset before committing to the full corpus:
conda run -n nepa python phase2/code/deliverable01/01_extract_nepa_trigger.py --sample 50




Prints description coverage and process-type breakdown without writing output:
conda run -n nepa python phase2/code/deliverable01/01_extract_nepa_trigger.py --eda












Argument
Default
Description




--calibrate
off
Validate NLI hypothesis templates against example bank; exit without extracting


--eda
off
Print descriptive stats and exit without writing output


--use-llm
off
Enable Tier 5 (Claude Haiku) for uncertain cases

Override Tier 5 budget guardrail and send full queue

--sample N
None
Random sample of N projects (for testing)

One row per project where nepa_trigger_primary == "federal_funding". This sidecar is intentionally separate from the trigger output so funding mechanism and amount parsing can be refreshed without rerunning the full trigger classifier.
Key columns:

federal_funding_amount_candidates_json

Amount coverage is partial by design. Dollar amounts are only populated when the amount is tied to project-specific federal funding language. Generic dollar amounts elsewhere in a NEPA document are not treated as federal funding amounts.



Stratified sample of output rows for manual QA. Sampled by: - rule_id (up to 20 rows per rule family) - process_type (up to 20 rows per CE/EA/EIS) - DOE agency (up to 20 rows) - CE dataset (up to 20 rows)
Key columns: all output columns + validation_batch (batch label), batch_kind (rule/process/agency/dataset), batch_size (total rows in that group).










File
Description




data/analysis/nepa_trigger/context_candidates.parquet
All chunks retrieved and scored per project


data/analysis/nepa_trigger/tier4_chunk_scores.parquet
Per-chunk NLI scores for each candidate class

Projects queued for Tier 5 (written before any LLM calls)










The script enforces these before writing output; the run fails if any assertion fires:

Uniqueness: project_id is unique — exactly one row per project.
Scope: all project_id values are in the 20,725-project clean energy set.
List column: nepa_trigger_secondary is a Python list, not a JSON string.

Funding sidecar assertions:

Funding-only scope: sidecar project IDs exactly match nepa_trigger_primary == "federal_funding".
No trigger overwrite: --funding-details-only asserts that projects_nepa_trigger.parquet size and mtime are unchanged.
Numeric validity: amount fields are non-negative USD values; percentages are between 0 and 100.
List columns: funding mechanism and program multi-label fields are Python lists.
Conflict handling: conflicting amount candidates leave primary amount fields blank and set federal_funding_manual_review = TRUE.




After a successful run, review the highest-volume rule batches:
python -c "
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('data/analysis/nepa_trigger/validation_batches.csv')
rule_batches = df[df['batch_kind'] == 'rule'].drop_duplicates('validation_batch')
print(rule_batches[['validation_batch','batch_size']].sort_values('batch_size', ascending=False).head(15).to_string(index=False))
"
Accept a rule batch if manual precision ≥ 0.85. For rules below that threshold, correct patterns in the tier functions, re-run on a sample, and re-check.

df = pq.read_table("data/analysis/nepa_trigger/projects_nepa_trigger.parquet").to_pandas()

print(f"\nTier 4 diagnostic check:")

print(f"  Tier 4 auto-resolved: {t4['auto_resolve'].sum()} / {len(t4)}")
print(f"  Mean top class score: {t4['top_class_score'].mean():.3f}")
Targets: - Manual review rate < 5% - unknown share < 10% - federal_land or federal_permit should be plurality for clean energy (expect ~40–60% combined)

nepa_trigger_secondary is a list-column in R. tidyr::unnest(df, nepa_trigger_secondary) explodes it for frequency counts. purrr::map2_chr() handles it in Fig 3 (combination bar). Do not convert to a JSON string.
CE documents: Tier 3 scans the full document with a conservative pattern set that excludes sec404, arra, and rmp to avoid form checklist false positives. EA/EIS scan pages 1–10 only.
DOE corpus dominance: ~79% of projects are DOE-led. DOE Tier 1a results are always provisional (T1a_DOE_action, T1a_DOE_funding) and routed to Tier 4 for confirmation. DOE routing quality is the single biggest driver of overall output quality.
NLI model: Tier 4 uses cross-encoder/nli-MiniLM2-L6-H768 (~67MB, zero-shot). Downloads automatically on first run. If unavailable, falls back to all-MiniLM-L6-v2 cosine similarity. Run --calibrate to verify hypothesis templates before any full corpus run. See _notes.md (“Model selection rationale”) for the full explanation of why NLI was chosen over fine-tuned BERT.
Hypothesis tuning: HYPOTHESIS_TEMPLATES in the script is the primary lever for Tier 4 accuracy. The --calibrate flag scores all example bank entries and reports PASS/FAIL so you know immediately if a hypothesis change is an improvement.
Document routing uses the dataset_source column (CE, EA, EIS) from projects_combined.parquet to select the correct *_documents.parquet and *_pages.parquet paths.
nepa_trigger_rule_id format: T{tier}_{slug} (e.g., T1a_BLM_land, T1b_row_grant, T3_sec404, T4_local_federal_funding, T5_llm). Use this to trace any classification back to the exact rule that fired.
Negation guard: a regex negation filter suppresses matches in contexts like “Section 404 permit is NOT required” and CE checkbox forms where the box is unchecked ([ ]). This prevents the most common false-positive patterns in CE boilerplate.
Funding details are sidecar-only: grant/loan/amount extraction only runs for projects already classified as federal_funding. This avoids turning generic dollar amounts or unrelated grant terms in land/permit/program documents into funding facts.
Grant disambiguation: funding detail extraction suppresses land-authorization uses of “grant” such as right-of-way grants, ROW grants, easement grants, and perpetual ROW grants.
Amount extraction coverage: federal_funding_amount_usd is intentionally sparse. It requires an amount near project-specific federal funding language such as DOE Funding, Federal Cost Share, award/grant language, loan guarantee language, EECBG/SEP funding, or a similar cue.

title: D1 — NEPA Trigger Classification
text:
Seven primary trigger classes, in priority order (used to break ties when multiple signals are present):








Priority
Class
Typical federal nexus




1
federal_action
Agency itself proposes or implements the action


2
federal_program
Programmatic EIS, resource management plan, rulemaking


3
federal_property_transaction
Land exchange, conveyance, disposal


4
federal_land
Project on or crossing federal land; ROW grant


5
federal_permit
Agency permit, license, or authorization required


6
federal_funding
Federal grant, loan guarantee, cost share


7
unknown
Clear NEPA review but nexus not identifiable



Primary trigger: the federal nexus most directly responsible for the agency’s NEPA decision. Secondary triggers: additional nexuses clearly present (nepa_trigger_secondary, stored as Arrow list). is_dual_nexus: computed flag for federal_land primary + federal_permit secondary (transmission line case).

title: D1 — NEPA Trigger Classification
text:
Each tier runs on projects not yet finalized by a prior tier. Tiers 1–3 produce results that are either auto-accepted (deterministic high-precision rules) or held as provisional (awaiting Tier 4 confirmation). Tier 4 processes all unfinalized projects.









Tier
Method
Source
Notes




1a
Agency metadata heuristics
projects_combined.parquet
BLM/USFS/NPS/FWS → federal_land (verb signals disambiguate action); FERC/FAA/FCC → federal_permit; DOE → provisional (funding vs action boundary)


1b
Keyword patterns on title + description
projects_combined.parquet
~30 patterns per class; returns first match; negation guard suppresses checklist false positives


2
Document title keyword scan
*_documents.parquet
Scans all documents for a project; programmatic title patterns fire here


3
Purpose and Need section
*_pages.parquet
CE: full doc scan with conservative pattern set (no sec404/arra/rmp); EA/EIS: P&N header detection, first 10 pages


4
Retrieval-first local NLI
*_pages.parquet
Chunk retrieval + cross-encoder/nli-MiniLM2-L6-H768 zero-shot NLI; embedding fallback if NLI unavailable; DOE and CE-heavy rows route here


5
Claude Haiku LLM
Tier 4 evidence bundles
Only with --use-llm; receives top chunks + local NLI scores + provisional class; subject to budget guardrail



Routing policy: - AUTO_ACCEPT_RULE_IDS — deterministic high-precision rules that finalize immediately (e.g., T1a_FERC_permit, T1b_special_use, T3_npdes) - SEND_TO_TIER4_RULE_IDS — ambiguous rules always routed to Tier 4 (e.g., T1a_DOE_action, T3_sec404, T3_arra) - AUDIT_FIRST_RULE_IDS — rules held for review before promotion (e.g., T3_rmp)

title: D1 — NEPA Trigger Classification
text:
Validates that the NLI hypothesis templates are well-calibrated before running at scale. Takes ~2 minutes. Downloads the NLI model (~67MB) on first run.
conda run -n nepa python phase2/code/deliverable01/01_extract_nepa_trigger.py --calibrate
Passing criteria: - Positive examples: correct class scores ≥ 0.75 - Hard negatives: all class scores ≤ 0.50
If any check fails, adjust HYPOTHESIS_TEMPLATES in the script and re-run calibration before proceeding. See _example_bank.md for guidance on hypothesis wording.



Runs tiers 1a–4. Appropriate for an initial build or after pattern changes.
conda run -n nepa python phase2/code/deliverable01/01_extract_nepa_trigger.py

export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY='sk-ant-...'

conda run -n nepa python phase2/code/deliverable01/01_extract_nepa_trigger.py --use-llm

conda run -n nepa python phase2/code/deliverable01/01_extract_nepa_trigger.py --funding-details-only

title: D1 — NEPA Trigger Classification
text:
The script enforces these before writing output; the run fails if any assertion fires:

Uniqueness: project_id is unique — exactly one row per project.
Scope: all project_id values are in the 20,725-project clean energy set.
List column: nepa_trigger_secondary is a Python list, not a JSON string.

Funding sidecar assertions:

Funding-only scope: sidecar project IDs exactly match nepa_trigger_primary == "federal_funding".
No trigger overwrite: --funding-details-only asserts that projects_nepa_trigger.parquet size and mtime are unchanged.
Numeric validity: amount fields are non-negative USD values; percentages are between 0 and 100.
List columns: funding mechanism and program multi-label fields are Python lists.
Conflict handling: conflicting amount candidates leave primary amount fields blank and set federal_funding_manual_review = TRUE.




After a successful run, review the highest-volume rule batches:
python -c "
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('data/analysis/nepa_trigger/validation_batches.csv')
rule_batches = df[df['batch_kind'] == 'rule'].drop_duplicates('validation_batch')
print(rule_batches[['validation_batch','batch_size']].sort_values('batch_size', ascending=False).head(15).to_string(index=False))
"
Accept a rule batch if manual precision ≥ 0.85. For rules below that threshold, correct patterns in the tier functions, re-run on a sample, and re-check.



import pyarrow.parquet as pq, pandas as pd

df = pq.read_table("data/analysis/nepa_trigger/projects_nepa_trigger.parquet").to_pandas()
print(df["nepa_trigger_primary"].value_counts())
print(f"\nManual review rate: {df['nepa_trigger_manual_review'].mean():.1%}  (target: < 5%)")
print(f"Unknown rate: {(df['nepa_trigger_primary']=='unknown').mean():.1%}  (target: < 10%)")
print(f"Dual-nexus projects: {df['is_dual_nexus'].sum()} ({df['is_dual_nexus'].mean():.1%})")
print(f"\nTier 4 diagnostic check:")
t4 = pq.read_table("data/analysis/nepa_trigger/tier4_doc_scores.parquet").to_pandas()
print(f"  Tier 4 auto-resolved: {t4['auto_resolve'].sum()} / {len(t4)}")
print(f"  Mean top class score: {t4['top_class_score'].mean():.3f}")
Targets: - Manual review rate < 5% - unknown share < 10% - federal_land or federal_permit should be plurality for clean energy (expect ~40–60% combined)
